Where one change gets past nothing differs: the practice games give the same reports before and after.

### T-1058 – On a screen that has never scrolled, keeping the life is the way past
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 3, the AI smarter; what any game needs).
- **Why now:** Boss (18 Nov): "in a few days i'm going to plug a random new game which could be anything and i expect it it to learn from playing the game". On the one-screen game kept outside the app (T-1056 limit 5, T-1057) the app, helpers on, still played little better than pressing at random after T-1057: 41 to 68 points a go and 1.4 to 2.0 lives lost, where a hand-written player gets 170 to 270 with no life lost. Its log said why: "Lost a life at step 133. Went back 33 steps and made 120 tries in 0.1 s: none got past", search after search, on a game where stepping aside is all it takes.
- **Try-outs (19 Nov, scratch worktrees off the T-1057 branch and off main, the scratch game "Toy Catcher" put on the practice console from a script; nothing in the repository):**
  1. *The guesses are not it.* With all twelve bytes of the falling things kept out of the guesses by hand, the network on numbers alone over 75 goes is no better (T-1057, limit 6).
  2. *The picture is not it.* The screen network alone, 75 goes of 300 steps, blocks of 25: 44, 53, 61 points a go on seed 1 and 31, 32, 34 on seed 2 with the picture as it is (32 by 28); with a picture of 64 by 56: 37, 15, 22 and 27, 34, 35. Worse, not better.
  3. *What a go of 300 steps can hold* (the game itself, seeds 1 to 4): standing still 10 to 20 points, left and right at random 10 to 60, a hand-written player 170 to 270 with no life lost.
  4. *Why no search succeeds.* `training.search.find_way` takes a try for the way when it is `Outcome.past`: alive, and two steps or more of new ground by the screen watch. `observation.ground.Ground` counts, on a screen that has never scrolled, where the player newly stands in steps of its own size. The catcher's floor is ten of its own widths: after a few seconds there is no new ground left in the game, and from then on no try can be the way, whatever it does.
  5. *With "alive" taken for "past" everywhere* (a switch in the scratch copy, cruder than what is built here), the table with helpers on, 30 goes of 300 steps, blocks of 25 and 5: seed 1 lives lost a go 0.04 and 0.00 (2.00 and 1.80 without), points 55 and 86 (44 and 50); seed 2 lives lost 0.24 and 0.40 (1.76 and 0.60), points 247 and 394 (47 and 36). Ways found: 98 and 152 searches (the log's count), against a handful.
  6. *Boss's own game is not this.* His log of 18 Nov (Super Mario Bros.): the spot his goes end at is in the second level, "A life was lost falling off the bottom of the screen", settled 54 steps before, and 82 steps back about 106 tries in the 15 seconds a search may take find nothing, go after go. That screen scrolls, and new ground is counted there (a look ahead finds a way on try 3 a hundred steps earlier). It stays the task after this one.
- **Objective:** where the screen has never been seen to scroll, a search after a life lost (or for one seen coming) takes the first change that keeps the life to the end of the try for the way.
  1. `find_way(..., still=False)`: with `still`, a play that is not lost is the way at once: the plain way held, or the first small change to it or to what it did. It is not played again under a screen watch, and no watch is asked for. Everything else of a search is as it is: the plain way first, its share of the tries and of the time, `live`, `begin_at`, the budget, what is not played twice.
  2. Not at a standstill: there no life was lost and staying alive tells nothing. `still` with `stood` is refused.
  3. `EpisodeRunner._seek` passes `still` when the go's screen watch has never seen the screen scroll (`watch.ground.scrolls`, kept from go to go), and says so in the log once a go.
  4. A game that has been seen to scroll gets `still=False`: the same plays, the same answer as before.
- **Scope:** `training/search.py`, `training/episode.py`, their tests, the documents. **Not in it:** a room that stands still inside a game that scrolls (the watch knows only that the game has scrolled; noted in Limits); catching the stars (what the learner is paid for and how fast it learns); the spot Boss's game is stuck at; the practice console (no game is added, by Boss's choice of 19 Nov).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. With `still`, the plain way held that keeps the life is the way after that one play, with no play under a watch and no watch asked for.
  2. With `still`, where the plain way loses the life, the first change that keeps it is the way, found on the play that kept it; a change that loses it is passed over as before.
  3. With `still` and no plain move, the same for the changes to what it did; `live`, `begin_at`, the budget and the time are kept to as before, and a search that finds nothing says where it stopped.
  4. Without `still` (the default) every existing test of the search passes unchanged.
  5. `still` with `stood` is refused, and so is a `still` that is not true or false.
  6. The runner passes `still` exactly when its watch has never seen the screen scroll, after a life lost and for a life seen coming, and never at a standstill; on the practice hopper (it scrolls) every existing test of going back passes unchanged.

### T-1057 – "Is the game listening" is not fooled by buttons that undo each other
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 3, the AI smarter; what any game needs before anything is learnt).
- **Why now:** Boss (18 Nov): "in a few days i'm going to plug a random new game which could be anything and i expect it it to learn from playing the game". A one-screen game tried outside the app (T-1056, limit 5) showed this at once, before the first go: "The game is not listening to the AI; trying each button to get it going", three times, "No button got the game going", and all 10 goes began a life down, because the game ran on with nobody playing while the app looked for a button to wake it. The game was listening all the time.
- **Try-outs (19 Nov, a scratch worktree, the scratch game "Toy Catcher" of T-1056 put on the practice console from a script; nothing in the repository):**
  1. *Why.* `understanding.wakeup.probe_inputs` plays one run holding nothing and one holding each of the AI's buttons in turn for 5 frames, and says the buttons matter when the memory ends up different. The catcher walks 2 pixels a frame: left for 5 frames then right for 5 puts it back where it was, the other buttons do nothing there, and the falling things fall the same either way. Nothing differs, so "does not matter".
  2. *Each button asked alone where the buttons together change nothing:* the same script, the table, 10 goes of 300 steps, seed 1: "not listening" is not said, no go begins a life down (10 of 10 did), 0.90 lives lost a go (2.80), 26 points a go (12).
  3. *The practice racer and hopper are not fooled today:* speeding up and braking leave the racer somewhere else, and the hopper speeds up and slows down, so left then right does not put it back.
- **Objective:** where the AI's buttons held one after another change nothing, the check asks each button alone before it says the game is not listening.
  1. `probe_inputs`: the runs it makes today, unchanged. Only where they show nothing driven: two runs holding nothing for one button's frames and the settling frames (what differs between them is noise), then one run for each button, held alone for its frames and let go for the settling frames. What ends up different from the run holding nothing, noise left out, is driven.
  2. `self_moving` (T-855) stays what changed holding nothing and is driven by nothing: what a single button drives is taken out of it.
  3. The game is put back where it was, as today, however the probe ends.
  4. `inputs_matter`, `find_wake_button` and the three places in the training service that ask (`_listens`, the wake search, the start moved past a life) get this through `probe_inputs`; none of them changes.
- **Scope:** `understanding/wakeup.py`, its tests, the documents. **Not in it:** a button that only does something held together with another, or held longer than the probe holds it; the scores and progress guessed wrongly on the same game (next); the practice console (no game is added to it, by Boss's choice of 19 Nov).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. On a game where left then right puts the player back and nothing else answers the pad, `inputs_matter` says yes, and the game is put back where it was.
  2. Where the buttons together already change something, not one frame more is played than before: the same adapter operations, the same answer.
  3. A screen that ignores the pad still says no (the practice racer's game-over screen without Start, as the existing test holds), with the game put back; a byte that only echoes the pad still does not count; a byte that differs between two runs holding nothing still does not count.
  4. `self_moving` names what moves by itself and none of what a single button drives, on the game of criterion 1.
  5. `find_wake_button` finds the button that starts such a game from its game-over screen, and leaves it running.
  6. One button that matters among several that undo each other or do nothing is enough, whichever comes first or last.
  7. The training service on such a game: the first go is not taken for "not listening", no wake search is made and the go begins with the game where it was put.
  8. Every existing test passes unchanged; `ruff format`, `ruff check`, `mypy` clean; deliberate breaks of the new lines are noticed; README, ARCHITECTURE, CHANGELOG and this tracker say what is so; the scratch game's figures before and after are in the results, measured outside the app's tests.
- **Expected changes:** `src/retro_ai_lab/understanding/wakeup.py`; new `tests/unit/understanding/test_wakeup_buttons_that_undo_each_other.py`; README, ARCHITECTURE, CHANGELOG, this tracker.
- **Test plan (written before the code):**
  1. *Unit, a stand-in game inside the test* (a practice racer whose pad only walks its place left and right at one speed, put into the practice console's adapter the way the existing two-press racer is): the buttons matter; asked with left and right alone, with every button, with left last and with right first; the game is where it was afterwards; a stand-in that answers to nothing says no; one whose pad is only echoed in a byte says no; one with a byte of noise that is not replayed says no.
  2. *Unit, what is played:* a spy counts the adapter's steps and frames: on the practice racer in play (the buttons together change something) the count is what it is on main; on the stand-in it is that and the runs of the plan (two idle and one a button), to the frame.
  3. *Unit, `self_moving`:* on the stand-in the frame counter and timer are named and the place the pad walks is not.
  4. *Unit, the wake search:* the stand-in at its game-over screen: Start is found and the game left running; with a pad that undoes itself as the only playing buttons.
  5. *Unit, the service:* `TrainingService` started on the stand-in: no "not listening" in the log, no wake search (`find_wake_button` spied), the first step is played.
  6. *The existing tests* of `wakeup` and of the service pass unchanged.
  7. *Deliberate breaks* of every new line; *the whole suite alone*; CI on both systems.
  8. *Outside the app's tests:* the scratch one-screen game before and after, 10 goes, for the tracker.
- **Changed while building:**
  1. *The stand-in* is a practice racer whose pad only walks its place 2 a frame either way from the middle of its floor (`SideStepper`, inside the new test file), with two switches: one that ignores the pad altogether, and one with a byte that counts every frame ever played, which a save state does not put back (noise).
  2. *What is played is held run for run,* not only counted: a spy on the practice console's `step` lists every run (the buttons held and the frames), and the tests hold the whole list.
  3. *Three tests more than planned:* with no frames to let go in, the byte that echoes the pad would count for a button asked alone (why the settling frames are there); the game is put back when asking a button alone goes wrong half-way; on a game that ignores the pad, what moves by itself is still named.
  4. *Every button is asked, also after one has answered.* Stopping at the first that answers would save a few frames and lose what the others drive, which `self_moving` needs left out.
- **Results:**
  - **Criteria 1 to 6:** `tests/unit/understanding/test_wakeup_buttons_that_undo_each_other.py` (23 tests). The stand-in's left and right do undo each other (held in turn, the memory ends as it does holding nothing); the buttons matter all the same, asked with left and right alone, with the whole pad, and with the one button that matters first, last or in the middle; the game is where it was afterwards. A stand-in that ignores the pad says no and is put back; the byte that echoes the pad does not count, and would with no frames to let go in; a byte that differs from run to run does not count and does not hide a pad that is heard. On the practice racer in play the runs made are the runs the check has always made, to the frame, at the usual lengths and at others; on the stand-in they are those and two runs holding nothing and one a button, in that order. The game is put back when a run fails half-way. `self_moving` names the frame counter and the timer and not the place the pad walks. From the stand-in's game-over screen `find_wake_button` finds Start and leaves the game running.
  - **Criterion 7:** the training service started on the stand-in plays its first go of 12 steps with "not listening" not said and no wake search made, and the game has run exactly the go's 48 frames; on the stand-in that ignores the pad the search is still made. Before the change 12 of the 23 failed.
  - **Criterion 8, the existing tests:** all 295 other tests of `tests/unit/understanding/` pass unchanged, and the whole suite: 2,722 passed, 10 skipped (2,699 before this task, and 23 new), run alone. `ruff format`, `ruff check` and `mypy` clean. No line of an existing test changed.
  - **Criterion 8, deliberate breaks:** 27 ways of breaking the new lines, one at a time, from a scratch worktree (never asked alone, always asked alone, asked and the answer dropped, a button left out, the frames swapped or shortened, the game not put back, noise counted or not looked for, a button never let go, only the last button's answer kept, and so on): every one is noticed by a test.
  - **Criterion 8, the scratch one-screen game before and after** (outside the app's tests; `try_catcher.py` of T-1056's limit 5, 10 goes of 300 steps, main at 3b3d3b1 against this branch; "points" is the game's own score a go, on average):

    | Learner | Seed | "Not listening" said | Goes begun a life down | Lives lost a go | Points a go |

    The fault is gone in all twelve. Lives lost fall in eleven of twelve and points rise in eleven of twelve; the network on numbers alone on seed 2 loses a little more (2.30 for 2.10), and with helpers on seed 1 scores less (68 for 97) while losing fewer lives. Ten goes are few, and the game is still played badly. What a go of 300 steps can hold, by the game itself (seeds 1 to 4): standing still 10 to 20 points and a life or two lost; left and right at random 10 to 60; a hand-written player that walks under the stars and out from under the rocks 170 to 270 with no life lost. - **Limits:**

No better. So telling a score from a thing that moves down the screen, which was named as the next task, is not what holds the play back on this game, and is not taken up as a task on that ground. What does is looked for next.

Where left then right puts the player back, a listening game was taken for a deaf one, the app looked for a button to wake it, and the game ran on meanwhile with nobody playing. Where the buttons together change nothing, each is now asked by itself. A game that was heard before is asked exactly as before. Any one-screen game with a player that walks at one speed would have met this in its first minute.

### T-1056 – The bench counts how far a go got from where it began
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 3, the AI smarter).
- **Why now:** T-1055 left "the screen network does not learn the practice hopper by itself" as the next work. Seven try-outs at that (below) found no way that does it reliably, and found a fault in the measuring on the way: the app moves where its goes start past a life it takes for lost whatever is pressed (T-965; it does so on the practice racer, a parked fault of its own), and the bench's "how far" is the game's lap and place, so a go begun further on was counted as having driven the ground it was put past. Figures that are wrong, however little, are put right before anything is built on them. Boss was told so the same night (18 Nov).
- **Try-outs (18 Nov, a scratch worktree off main at fdc3177 with switches read from the environment, nothing kept but the figures; the screen network with every helper off; blocks of 25 goes of 300 steps; "far" is how far a go got on average, by the bench as it was):**
  1. *Practising a spot where a life went* (put back to a saved moment about 10 steps before, up to 6 times a go, half the next 20 moves random): hopper seed 1, how far 83 to 404 over 200 goes, no better than without (395).
  2. *What the hopper is paid, by the app's own rewards, in 40 goes:* "Getting somewhere new" 302 times for +302 (about +1 for 27 pixels of ground new in the go), "Losing a life" 36 times for -270, the score 34 times for +157. Ground walked again after a life lost pays nothing (T-1028 and the screen watch, on purpose), and the network learnt from a tenth of every reward.
  3. *Rewards evened out inside the network (what its 8 steps add up to kept between -1 and +1) and every life paid for its ground again:* hopper seed 1: how far 425, 786, 1,021, 968, 1,214, 996, 1,165, 1,312, single goes of 2,161 (the level is 2,560), lives lost a go 2.36 to 1.36. Either alone does nothing (372 and 282). **But seed 2 stays where it was:** 367 to 304. Racer: further in the middle of the run and no fewer lives lost.
  4. *Rewards at their full size instead* (a life lost is -7.5 against +1 for ground), ground paid again: hopper seed 1 loses no life at all from the 101st go on and stands still at about 250, before the first gap; seed 2 gets to 642 with 1.12 lives lost a go.
  5. *Each life a go of its own to the network* (a life lost ends what it reckons with, as the screen-watching networks for old console games are taught), with 3: hopper seed 1 about 1,000 (528 to 1,061, lives 1.88 to 1.52); seed 2 stays at about 400 and loses more lives (1.68 to 2.76).
  6. *Four times the learning from every step played* (four batches a step for one; a batch takes about 5 ms), with 5: the hopper loses hardly a life from the second block on, on both seeds (0.08 and 0.40 a go at the end), **by stopping before the first gap** (how far 279 and 258; the gap begins at 336 and 304). The racer likewise drives less far.
  7. *The same with a lost life practised* (1, with 5, at one batch and at four): the same standstill before the first gap on both seeds (272, 306, 317, 279).
  8. *What the gap asks:* a fresh press of the jump button within about four steps of the edge, held for two steps or more, with the button not already held. A move made at random does that perhaps once in thirty tries, so the network sees the life go there some thirty times for every time it gets over, and learns to stay away before it learns to jump. More learning from the same steps makes that worse, not better.
  9. *The screen network trained as the app trains it, helpers on* (not measured before): hopper seed 2, try-out 5's switches: no life lost from the 26th go on and 4,228 far in every go (the level finished and most of it again), because the way remembered plays the whole go. ### T-1055 – A network that watches the screen
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 3, the AI smarter; the change of direction of T-1054).
- **Why now:** T-1054's figures: the learner alone learns neither practice game. It is fed a handful of numbers guessed from the game's memory (on the racer the lane is taken for "progress" and nothing it is fed says where an obstacle is), so it cannot learn what it cannot see. Boss (17 Nov): "i want to plug it into any game, any it should learn by network or RL" and "any retro game, so still no massively complicated". The screen is the one thing every game shows.
- **Try-outs (17 Nov, scratch scripts outside the app, nothing kept but the figures; a numpy network of 128 and 64 on the game object itself, 4 frames a step, goes of 300 steps, seed 1; "alone" is a test go with nothing random and nothing put back):**
  1. *The racer, the picture (32 by 24 grey) and what changed in it, paid by the game's own truth (how far, lives):* 400 goes: lives lost a go 3.00, 3.00, 3.00, 3.00, 3.00, 1.80, 1.44, 1.24, ... 0.92; how far 349, 493, 603, 890, 1,202, 3,698, 4,415, 4,304, ... 4,605 (a lap is 256; T-1054's learner: 134 to 855 and over two lives a go). It learns the game.
  2. *The hopper, the same:* it stops before the first danger and stands (180, against the first wall, in every test go). Fewer buttons and rewards carried over 8 steps: the same.
  3. *Practising a spot where a life went* (back to a saved moment 6 to 40 steps before, half its moves random for a while; up to 6 times a go): the racer alone drives 4,718 with no life lost after 75 goes. The hopper gets further in training (615 after 100 goes) and alone still stands at the wall.
  4. *Its last buttons fed to it too, and paid for moving on rather than for a new furthest* (the hopper jumps on a fresh press only, so what to press depends on what was held; and "a new furthest" pays nothing for the same ground after a life lost, which taught it that passing the wall is worth nothing): alone it passes the wall and the first gap after 50 goes, is at 1,673 of 2,560 after 100 and at 2,405 with no life lost after 200 (a go of 300 steps cannot get further than about 2,400).
  5. *Paid by nothing of the game's truth but its score and lives, and for a screen not seen before in this life:* the racer alone drives 4,762 with no life lost after 75 goes; the hopper does not get going (three ways of telling a new screen tried). On the hopper the app's own rewards pay for ground gained (off the screen watch and off a memory value), which is what this task will measure.
  - **What they say:** the picture is enough to learn from, with a plain network, in tens of goes on the racer and a couple of hundred on the hopper. What it is paid for decides the hopper. Practising a spot from a saved moment helps and is the next task, not this one.
- **Objective:** a way of learning that sees the screen, chosen like the others, with nothing in it that knows a game.
  1. **The picture.** `learning/picture.py`: `shrink(frame)` gives the screen as 32 by 28 grey bytes whatever the console's size: the mean of the colour channels (alpha left out), averaged over the part of the screen each cell covers, nothing cropped.
  2. **What a state shows.** `Sight(now, before, held)`: the picture after the step, the picture a step earlier, and the move just made (none at a go's start). `State.sight` holds it, or None. It is left out of a state's key, its comparing and its hash: every state is the state it was.
  3. **The runner hands it over.** Where the learner says `wants_picture`, the runner asks the emulator for the screen with every step (with the same request as the step, T-824), takes one as the go begins and after the game is put back, and every state it gives the learner carries its sight. For any other learner nothing is asked for and nothing changes.
  4. **The screen network.** `learning/screen.py`, `ScreenLearner`, algorithm `"screen"`, "Screen network": a network (the app's own numpy `Network`) from the picture, what changed in it and the move last made to a value for every move. It learns as the present network does where that is sound (replay memory, a target network, the runner's rewards carried over several steps) and chooses the next move with the learning network and values it with the target (double). Rewards are scaled to a tenth: the app's are tens, and the network learns best near one. Exploring follows the same settings, the same lift when results fall and the same held runs. It is saved without its memory of pictures.
  5. **On the list.** Registered, labelled and described; "Choose for me" is left as it is (the table, then the present network).
  6. **Measured.** `learning_bench GAME --algorithm screen`, both games, helpers off, against T-1054's figures for the table and the present network.
- **Scope:** `learning/picture.py`, `learning/screen.py`, `learning/state.py` (the field), `learning/learner.py` (its label), `learning/__init__.py`, `training/episode.py` (the picture taken and handed over), their tests, the two tests that list the ways of learning (**Boss said yes to those two, 17 Nov 13:12, on a card: "I add the new screen-watching network to the list those two tests check, and change nothing else in them"**), the documents. **Not in it:** practising from a saved moment; a reward for moving on that needs no guess; making it what "Choose for me" picks; the picture in the window; a real emulator's cost of a screenshot every step (to be measured on Boss's machine, and said so).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. `shrink` gives 32 by 28 bytes for any frame of 1, 3 or 4 channels and any size from one pixel up; grey is the mean of the colour channels; a cell is the average of what it covers (a screen white on the left half and black on the right reads so, at every size tried); the same frame, the same bytes; what is not a frame is refused.
  2. A state with a sight equals, hashes and keys as the same state without; `coarse()` keeps the sight; `from_key` gives none. A `Sight` refuses pictures of the wrong size.
  3. With a learner that wants pictures, every state the runner hands to `choose` and to `learn` carries a sight: `now` the shrunk screen after that step, `before` the one a step earlier (the first: the same), `held` the move just made (none at the start); after the game is put back the sight is of the screen it was put back to. With a learner that does not, no state carries one and the emulator is asked for no screenshot more than before.
  4. The screen network learns: a seeded toy problem in which only the picture says which move pays is learnt (the paying move chosen in at least 9 of 10 pictures of each kind) within a fixed number of steps; one in which only the move last made says so is learnt too. The target is the double one; a reward is scaled; steps spanned discount as the runner means; a state with no sight is not learnt from and is counted.
  5. It is a `Learner`: `choose`, `greedy`, `values`, `learn`, `end_episode`, `configure`, `reset`, `policy`, `stats`, `to_dict` and `from_dict`; saved and loaded it chooses the same; it is saved without its memory; bad data is refused in plain words.
  6. `algorithms()` and `algorithm_choices()` list `"screen"`, `describe_algorithm("screen")` gives its label and sentence, and the two approved test lines are the only lines of existing tests changed.
  7. The training service trains with it on both practice games (through the bench): the runs are whole and seeded, the same arguments the same report.
  8. The tracker holds the bench's figures for it on both games beside T-1054's, whatever they are.
  9. Every other existing test passes unchanged; `ruff format`, `ruff check`, `mypy` clean; deliberate breaks of the new code are noticed; README, ARCHITECTURE, CHANGELOG and this tracker say what is so.
- **Expected changes:** new `learning/picture.py`, `learning/screen.py`; `learning/state.py`, `learning/learner.py`, `learning/__init__.py`, `training/episode.py`; new `tests/unit/learning/test_picture.py`, `test_screen.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_the_runner_hands_over_the_screen.py`, `tests/integration/test_the_screen_network.py`; one line each in `tests/unit/learning/test_learner.py` and `test_promotion.py`; the documents.

It was found by running the panel's tests, not changed, and asked about on a card: **Boss, 17 Nov 13:57, "Yes, update that test too": "I add "Screen network" to the list of names that test expects in the app's "how the AI learns" picker, and change nothing else in it."** Criterion 6 says two lines; it is three, each approved by name, and nothing else in an existing test is changed (`git diff main -- tests` shows those three lines and new files only).
  - *Changing a brain to or from the screen network* (not in the plan; found when the picker could choose it). `promotion.convert` knew no way from a table to the screen network and would have refused with "Can't turn a ... brain into a ... one." Pictures and numbers from the game's memory cannot be told in each other's words, so such a change is a new learner that knows nothing (`promotion.carries_over` says which changes those are; the screen network carries on the count of goes). The service used to say "keeping what it learned" after every change; after one of these it says "and starts learning afresh: what it had learned could not be taken along."   - *An emulator that gives no picture of its screen.* The runner asks `capabilities().screen_capture` as a go begins. Where it is not so, nothing is asked for, the states carry no sight, the log says once "This emulator gives no picture of the screen, so a learner that watches the screen has nothing to learn from here.", and the screen network counts the steps as unseen. Without this the first step would have failed.
  - *The brain is saved without the target network too,* not only without its memory of steps: loaded, the target is a copy of the network. The saved file holds the network once (about 2.6 MB with the default layers).
  - *The toy problems use pictures that are never the same twice* (bright on one half with random shades; noise where only the last move matters), and are judged on ten pictures of each kind it was never shown, as criterion 4 says. They are learnt with two small layers (32 and 16) in 1,000 steps on every seed from 1 to 10 tried; the tests run seeds 1 to 3.

It is a guard against the learner going blind, on one seed; the measure is the figures below.

  - The picture is 32 by 28 grey: a thing smaller than a cell (8 by 8 pixels on a 256 by 240 screen), or told apart only by its colour, may not show. Neither practice game needed more.

- **Objective:** one tool that says what the learner alone learns on a practice game, so that "the network learns this game" is a figure and not a hope.
  1. `retro_ai_lab.tools.learning_bench.run(game, goes, *, seed, algorithm, max_steps, block, helpers)` plays the practice game named ("racer" or "hopper") through the app's own services, as `practice_bench` does, and returns a `Report`.
  2. **Helpers off unless asked:** no going back, no way remembered, no pressing on, no standing still, nothing looked ahead (`ways_per_go=0`, `remember=False`, `stand_after=0`, `look_ahead=False`). `helpers=True` trains as the app does, to compare.
  3. **Counted by the game itself, go by go:** lives that were lost (by the game's own count of lives), how far it got (the racer: laps and place on the track as one number; the hopper: levels finished and how far into the level), the steps played, how the go ended.

- **Scope:** the new module, its tests, the documents. No change to the learner, the helpers or `practice_bench`. **Not in it:** the network learning from the screen (next); a third game; the real emulators.
- **Acceptance criteria:**

  2. With helpers off the runner goes back for nothing, remembers no way and looks ahead at nothing (`ways_sought`, `remembered`, `looked_ahead` all nought over the run), and the service is built with those options; with `helpers=True` it is built as the app builds it.
  3. How far: the racer's is `lap * TRACK_LENGTH + position`, the furthest of the go; the hopper's is `level * LEVEL_WIDTH + x`, the furthest of the go, from the level the go began at.
  4. Blocks: `Report.blocks()` gives for each whole block the lives lost a go, the mean and the best of how far, and the goes with no life lost; goes left over after the last whole block are a last, shorter block.
  5. `Report.lines()` says it in plain words: a heading (game, brain, goes, steps, helpers on or off), a line for each block, and a last line comparing the last block with the first.
  6. Seeded: two runs with the same arguments give equal reports; another seed gives another.
  7. Bad arguments are refused with a plain message (a game it does not have, goes or steps or block below 1, an unknown brain, helpers not true or false).
  8. The command line prints the lines and returns 0; its options are goes, seed, algorithm, steps, block, helpers.
  9. Every existing test passes unchanged; `ruff format`, `ruff check`, `mypy` clean; deliberate breaks of the new code are noticed; README, ARCHITECTURE, CHANGELOG and this tracker say what is so, and the tracker holds the first figures for both games and both brains.

### T-1053 – The last life costs points, it does not pay them
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 3, the AI smarter: what it is paid for is what happened).
- **Why now:** T-1050 made each game over the next go on a game that counts its lives in reserve (Boss's, 16 Nov: "when it got game over the 'goes' number didn't go up"), and wrote down what it left: "**The default "Gaining Lives" reward still pays for the count going from 0 to 255** … and his own "goes down" row does not pay for that last life. … it is pay for dying and is the next thing to mend." Boss was told it would be the small task after T-1052. Pay for dying teaches dying: every go that ends by game over ends on +5.
- **What was read (17 Nov, main at 2d6d41a):** `EventDetector._judge` says of a value taken for lives or health only `value < before`: a fall is a SETBACK, anything else a RECOVERY ("Lives rose to 255."), and of a value a person's reward is on only `value > before`: UP, else DOWN. `suggestions.py` puts "Losing {name}" (-10) on a lives SETBACK and "Gaining {name}" (+5) on a lives RECOVERY. A person's own row is a trigger on UP or DOWN (`rewards/own.py`). `EpisodeSignals._read_lives` (T-1050) already reads 0 to more than the go began with, on a count that has fallen by one in the go, as below nought, and adds the life itself (`if below: self._setbacks += 1`) because "it read as a rise". `EpisodeSignals._on_reward` notes every value paid on an event whose `after` is above its `before` as one paid for going up (T-1036).
- **Try-out (17 Nov, nothing kept):** the T-1050 test of the training service on the practice racer counting its lives in reserve (`tests/unit/training/test_each_game_over_is_the_next_go.py`), with the go's pay printed: a go ended by game over "lost a life 4 times" and was paid "Losing Lives -30.0 (3 times)" and "Gaining Lives +5.0 (once)".
- **Objective:** the fall below nought is told as what it is, where the events are made, so that every reward on it (suggested or his own) and every reader of the events sees a life lost and no life gained.
  1. **The most a layout can hold.** `Encoding.most(length)`, and `Variable.most`: all ones for the binary layouts (255 for a byte, 65,535 for two, `256**n - 1` for a sized one), all nines for the decimal ones (99 for a packed byte, `100**n - 1` packed, `10**n - 1` for digits), and None for a signed byte and an on-or-off flag (a signed byte reads -1 below nought, which is a fall already).
  2. **Below nought.** A watched value that has been seen to fall by exactly one (kept by where the value is held, as the lowest and highest seen are, T-1021) and now goes from 0 to the most its layout can hold has fallen below nought. No count gains as much as it can hold in one step; a count that never fell by one is left as it was (a byte that switches between 0 and 255 is no count).
  3. **What is told.** For a value taken for lives: a SETBACK and no RECOVERY, "{name} fell below nought (it reads 255)." For a value a person's reward is on, of any kind but health: DOWN and not UP, "{name} went down below nought (it reads 255)." `before` and `after` stay as read (0 and 255): the runner's reading of the game being over, and its line in the log, go by them.
  4. **The runner counts the life once.** A fall below nought that already counted as a life lost (it came as a SETBACK or DOWN on a value lives lost are counted on) is not added again by `_read_lives`; told as a rise (UP), as before, it is added there as before. The game being over is read as before either way.
  5. **A penalty is not a rise paid for.** `_on_reward` does not note a value as paid for going up when the event paid on is a SETBACK or a DOWN.
- **Scope:** `understanding/knowledge.py`, `understanding/events.py` (`_judge` and what is kept for it), `training/episode.py` (`_on_discovery`, `_read_lives`, `_on_reward`), their tests, the documents. **Not in it:** health (it is filled up in play, and from nothing to 99 is a refill on a decimal layout: left as it was); how the detector calls the game started over in that snapshot (`given_back`, the highest seen: left exactly as they were, so the detector may still say the game started over where it did); the count set anew afterwards (255 to 3 still reads as a fall; it happens between goes, where nothing is paid, and criterion 7 checks that); a count that starts at nought and never fell by one.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. `Encoding.most(length)` and `Variable.most` give the values of objective 1 for every layout, and None for a signed byte and a flag.
  2. A lives value that has fallen by one and goes from 0 to the most its layout holds gives one SETBACK and no RECOVERY, with `before` 0, `after` as read, and the sentence of objective 3. So on a byte, two bytes, a packed decimal byte and a sized layout.
  3. A value a person's reward is on, of a kind other than health, under the same condition gives DOWN and no UP, with its sentence; a lives value a reward is on gives both DOWN and SETBACK, each once.
  4. Left as they were: a rise from 0 to anything less than the most; from 1 to the most; from 0 to the most on a value never seen to fall by one; health, asked about or not; a signed byte (0 to -1 is a SETBACK as ever); a flag; a value of another kind nobody's reward is on (no event); and a fall by one that is seen under an older guess of the same place still counts after the guess is replaced.
  5. The runner counts one life for a fall below nought told as DOWN, as SETBACK, as both in one update, and as UP (as before), and reads the game being over each time with the same reason.
  6. A penalty paid on a SETBACK or DOWN whose `after` is above its `before` leaves `take_rises()` empty; a reward paid on a rise is noted as before.
  7. Through the training service, on the practice racer counting its lives in reserve, every go ended by game over is paid "Losing Lives" once for each life lost (one more than it has in reserve) and "Gaining Lives" not at all; with a person's own "goes down" row on the count, that row is paid once for each life lost too. Goes, lives lost, `ended_by` and the reason in the log are as T-1050 left them.
  8. The practice racer as it is (its count stops at nought) is paid as before.
  9. Every existing test passes unchanged; `ruff format`, `ruff check` and `mypy` are clean; every deliberate break of the new code is noticed by a test.
  10. README, ARCHITECTURE, CHANGELOG and this tracker say what is so.
- **Expected changes:** `src/retro_ai_lab/understanding/knowledge.py`, `src/retro_ai_lab/understanding/events.py`, `src/retro_ai_lab/training/episode.py`; new `tests/unit/understanding/test_the_most_a_layout_holds.py`, `tests/unit/understanding/test_events_below_nought.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_the_last_life_is_counted_once.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_the_last_life_costs_points.py`; README, ARCHITECTURE, CHANGELOG, this tracker.
- **Test plan (written before the code):**
  - *The most a layout holds:* each layout, at one, two and three bytes or digits where it is sized; signed byte and flag None; a variable gives its own.
  - *The detector:* a lives byte 2, 1, 0, 255 gives SETBACK, SETBACK, SETBACK and the sentence; two bytes to 65,535; packed decimal to 99; a sized packed layout to 9,999; asked about gives DOWN with it, and DOWN alone on a value of unknown kind; each "left as it was" of criterion 4 by name; the fall by one remembered across a replaced guess; `reset()` forgets it.
  - *The runner:* the four ways of telling of criterion 5, each `(1, 1, True)` restarts, lives and over, and the reason; with no values watched (every SETBACK counts) still one; criterion 6 both ways.
  - *The service:* criterion 7 with the suggested rows, and with his own row added; criterion 8.
  - *Deliberate breaks:* each new condition and sentence altered in turn from a scratch worktree; every one must fail a test.

- **Changed while building:** (1) **The fall by one outlives `reset()`.** The test plan said "`reset()` forgets it". It is kept, as the lowest and highest seen are (T-1022): `reset()` clears the watches and nothing in the app calls it, and what was seen of the game is not a watch's. `test_it_is_kept_as_the_lowest_and_highest_seen_are` holds that. (2) With no values named for lives lost (every SETBACK counts), `_on_discovery` notes which values' SETBACKs it counted, so that the reading knows there too (`told`). (3) His own row is named as the app names it, "Lifes goes down". (4) With his own row on, 2 of the 12 goes end by game over where 3 and more do without it (the pay differs, so the learner does); the test of his row asks for at least two, the test without it for at least three as T-1050's does. (5) Criterion 8 is held harder than planned: the six goes' pay on the racer as it is are pinned to what main at 2d6d41a paid (35, 0, 7, 0, 0, -18). (6) One deliberate break was missed at first ("counted where anything was told": with every setback counting, another value's SETBACK in the update made the count's own fall look counted); a case was added to `test_another_values_fall_is_not_the_counts` and it is noticed.
- **Results:** **65 new tests pass**: `tests/unit/understanding/test_the_most_a_layout_holds.py` 17, `tests/unit/understanding/test_events_below_nought.py` 26, `tests/unit/training/test_the_last_life_is_counted_once.py` 19, `tests/unit/training/test_the_last_life_costs_points.py` 3. With the source as it was on main, 26 of the detector's, runner's and service's 48 fail (and the 17 of the most a layout holds, which is new). **Through the training service** (criterion 7), the practice racer counting its lives in reserve, 12 goes: each of the six goes ended by game over reads "Losing Lives -40.0 (4 times) … lost a life 4 times … Lives at ram[7] went from 0 to 255: it fell below nought, so every life is lost", and no go's line names "Gaining Lives"; before, the same goes read "Losing Lives -30.0 (3 times)" and "Gaining Lives +5.0 (once)", so each such go is paid 15 less than it was. With his own row on the count ("Lifes goes down", -7), it pays once for each life lost in every go, the last among them. **The racer as it is** (criterion 8): the six goes paid 35, 0, 7, 0, 0, -18 before and after. **Deliberate breaks:** 74 of the new code (19 of the most a layout holds, 35 of the detector, 20 of the runner), every one noticed. **Existing tests:** none changed; `ruff format`, `ruff check`, `mypy` clean. **Whole suite, alone:** 2,494 passed, 10 skipped (main 2,429 and 10).

(2) **A count that never fell by one while the app watched** (a game of one life, whose count starts at nought) still reads as risen when it goes below nought; the rule needs to have seen it count down. (3) **Health is left out**, asked about or not: nothing to the most its layout holds is a refill on some games (0 to 99 on a packed decimal byte). (4) **The count set anew still reads as a fall** (255 to 3): it happens as the checkpoint is put back between goes, where no go is paid, and it did before; the Rewards panel still shows one "Losing Lives" there. (5) **How the detector calls the game started over is untouched:** in that snapshot the count still counts as given back, and 255 is still the highest it was seen at. (6) **A value a person's reward is on that counts down to nought and is then set to exactly the most its layout holds** (a timer put back to 99 on a packed decimal byte) is told as gone down where it was set anew. (7) **Only lives are read anew where no reward is on the value:** a progress number that goes below nought still tells "went up", and with a reward on it tells both. (8) **Other rows still pay as the game ends** on the practice racer: "Game over switches on +2.0" and "Something switches on +1.5", the suggested rows for flags. That is pay for the game being over, of another kind, and is not mended here.

### T-1052 – A life seen going is saved before it goes
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 3, the AI smarter: what it knows of the screen changes what it does).
- **Why now:** Boss, 16 Nov: "I still dont get how it keeps dying to the first enemy or any enemy of the same type. It should go oh whats that tag it, oh it killed me when it touch me, best keep the fuck away from them in the future." T-1051 was the first half (it knows what cost the life, and how). This is the second: it keeps away. T-1051's limit 1 said the next task would be "the lesson put where the touch was, not where the count dropped": that was tried first (below) and changes nothing by itself, so this task is the other thing its plan named, keeping away made direct.
- **What the code shows (17 Nov, read before the plan):** The learner is given a life's penalty at the step the count drops, which on his game is some 53 steps after the touch; it learns each step from the 8 steps after it (`LOOKAHEAD_STEPS`). What gets the AI past an enemy today is not the learner: it is the search after a life lost (`EpisodeRunner._seek`, T-1007), which goes back to a saved moment, tries small changes off the record until one stays alive, plays it, and the way is remembered from the go's start (T-1014). That search begins only once a life has gone. So every enemy met for the first time costs a life, whatever is known of its kind: nothing the watch learns of kinds is asked before the touch. The brain is shown where the nearest thing that hurts is (T-978), and no more.
- **Try-outs (17 Nov, before the plan, in scratch scripts that patch main as it runs, described as such).** The practice bench, levels 1 to 4, 12 goes of 300 steps each, with the long dying pause (200 frames, about his game's) unless said, counted by the game's own account of what each life went to.
  1. *The lesson where the touch was.* At a life put down to a thing (T-1051's `Blame`), the 8 steps up to the look of the touch are learned once more with that step's penalty as a final return. Simple table: 37 lives lost to walkers without, 38 with; 45 levels finished either way (three of the four runs are the same to the last figure). Neural network: 37 and 37; 42 and 46 levels. **Nothing.** The table cannot carry a lesson from one place to the next, and for both the search and the way remembered decide what is played near an enemy.
  2. *Looking ahead, the search made from where it stands.* When a thing of a kind found to hurt is within 128 pixels across (`PART_REACH`) and has not been looked ahead for, the game is saved, the moves already queued and then the best-paid button's move are played off the record for 40 steps and the dying pause the runner remembers, and where that loses a life `find_way` looks for a small change from the save and the way is played. Table: **12** lives lost to walkers for 37, **67** levels finished for 45. Network: **16** for 37, **70** for 42. With the game's own pause (48 frames), network: 27 for 39, 79 levels for 49. It looked ahead 57 to 106 times a run, saw a life going in 11 to 22 of them, and found a way in 97 of 119 with the long pause and 37 of 68 with the game's own. Where it found none, the tries ran out of changes, not of time: only 5 to 14 steps were left before the loss was settled. (A first version looked ahead only while no moves were queued, and never did: near an enemy the AI is nearly always playing the way it remembers or a way a search found.)
  3. *Every kind a life was ever put down to*, not only the kinds now found to hurt (a kind passed safely often enough reads as harmless again): the same, 11 and 16 lives.
  4. *Playing what was checked.* Where carrying on stays alive, the queue is filled up with the checked move to 40 steps: table **6** lives lost to walkers and 68 levels, network **11** and 54 (the levels finished vary a good deal by run: 9 to 25).
  Falls are as before in all of them (13 to 17 a run): a pit is not a kind of thing.
- **Objective:** (1) `ScreenWatch.threats()`: the things in sight, not the player's own, of a kind a life was ever put down to, within `PART_REACH` across of the player, nearest first. (2) `EpisodeRunner` looks ahead before a step when there is a threat it has not looked ahead for in this stretch of the go, a search may be made, and it last looked ahead at least `AHEAD_EVERY` steps ago: the game is saved, what it is about to do (the moves queued, then the best-paid button's move; with none paid, the move it mostly made since the oldest saved moment) is played off the record for `AHEAD` steps and the dying pause it remembers, and the game is put back. (3) Alive: the queue is filled up to `AHEAD` moves with that move, so the AI plays what it checked. (4) A life going: the search after a life lost is made before the life is lost, from a saved moment before, over what was done since and what it was about to do, with the step the loss is settled at asked for as after a loss; a way found is gone back for and played. (5) Such a search costs none of the go's searches after a life lost; a go stops looking ahead after as many of them for nothing as it has searches (`ways_per_go`). (6) The log, the go's result, the bench's report and the line the service writes once a session say so.
- **Scope:** `training/vision.py` (`threats`), `training/episode.py` (the look ahead, `_seek`, `_way_back` and `_settled` taking what it was about to do, the result), `training/service.py` (the sentence once a session), `tools/practice_bench.py` (the count), tests, the documents. **Out of scope:** falls (a pit is not a kind: looking ahead where the floor ends is its own task); the lesson for the learner (try-out 1); the brain's view; a look ahead that plays what the learner would choose and not the plain move; more than `ways_per_go` searches after a life lost; what is known of kinds kept between sessions; the default "Gaining Lives" reward paying for a count that falls below nought (T-1050's limit 2: its own task); how a way found is checked (it is held to be one when it is alive 20 steps past where the life went, which a long dying pause can outlast).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. `threats()` gives each thing in sight of a kind a life was put down to, within `PART_REACH` across, nearest first, with its kind; not a kind no life was put down to, a thing out of sight, a thing further off, the player's own, and nothing where the player was not seen.
  2. The runner looks ahead when there is a threat it has not looked ahead for, and only then: not for one it has (until the go is put back), not within `AHEAD_EVERY` steps of the last time, not where no search could follow (no saved moments, a console that cannot save, no life value watched, no watch, nothing paid and nothing done yet to go by).
  3. What is played ahead is the moves queued and then the plain move, `AHEAD` steps and the remembered dying pause long, off the record: afterwards the game, the go's steps, pay, lives lost, the learner and the saved moments are as they were.
  4. Alive: the queue holds at least `AHEAD` moves, those queued first and the plain move after; a longer queue is left alone.
  5. A life going: a search is made as after a life lost, over the moves since a saved moment and those played ahead up to the loss; a way found is gone back for and played, the go's result counts it as sought, found and ahead, and no life is lost.
  6. No way found: the game is as it was, the moments are kept, the go carries on. A go makes at most `ways_per_go` such searches for nothing and then looks ahead no more; one that finds a way costs nothing; neither takes from the searches after a life lost.
  7. The log says in a plain sentence what was near, what carrying on would have cost and what was found; a look ahead that stays alive is in the detailed log only; the service says once a session that the AI looks ahead.
  8. The go's result keeps `ways_ahead` (saved and read back, 0 where missing) and `describe_ways` says how many of the searches were before a life went; the bench counts them and its report says so.
  9. On the practice bench, levels 1 to 4, both brains, both pauses, 12 goes each: fewer than two thirds of main's lives lost to walkers in all, no fewer levels finished in all, and no run takes more than half as long again as main's.
  10. Every existing test passes with no assertion changed.
  11. Every new line broken on purpose in a scratch worktree and noticed; the whole suite passes, run alone.
- **Expected changes:** `src/retro_ai_lab/training/vision.py`, `src/retro_ai_lab/training/episode.py`, `src/retro_ai_lab/training/service.py`, `src/retro_ai_lab/tools/practice_bench.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_vision_threats.py` (new), `tests/unit/training/test_looking_ahead.py` (new), `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, this tracker.
- **Test plan (written before the task's code; the try-outs above came first):** `test_vision_threats.py`, on `ScreenWatch` with drawn screens: `test_a_thing_of_a_kind_that_cost_a_life_is_a_threat` (1), `test_what_is_no_threat` (1), `test_threats_are_nearest_first` (1). `test_looking_ahead.py`, on the runner with the practice game through the real services, a walker's kind made known to have cost a life: `test_a_life_seen_going_is_saved_before_it_goes` (5), `test_it_looks_ahead_for_a_threat_once` (2), `test_not_more_often_than_every_few_steps` (2), `test_where_no_search_could_follow_it_does_not_look` (2), `test_what_is_played_ahead` (3), `test_looking_ahead_is_off_the_record` (3), `test_alive_it_plays_what_it_checked` (4), `test_no_way_found_and_the_go_carries_on` (6), `test_it_stops_looking_after_as_many_for_nothing_as_a_go_has_searches` (6), `test_a_way_found_ahead_costs_none_of_the_gos_searches` (6), `test_the_log_says_what_it_saw_and_did` (7), `test_the_result_counts_them` (8); the service's sentence (7) and the bench's count (8) beside their existing tests, in new tests. Then the breaks of criterion 11, the existing tests of the runner, the service, the watch and the bench unchanged (10), the bench measure (9) and the whole suite alone.
- **Changed while building:** (1) **Alive, nothing is queued** (objective 3 and criterion 4 as planned are dropped). As planned and first built, a look ahead that stayed alive filled the queue of moves up to `AHEAD` with the checked move. Measured, level 1 with the network and the long pause then finished **no level in twelve goes** (14 on main): near a wall with walkers about, the queue never ran out, and `_stands_still()` and `_press_on()` only act when no moves are lined up, so the go never looked for a way on. With the filling taken out the same run finishes 21. Criterion 4 now reads: alive, the queue is as it was and the learner is asked. What try-out 4 gained by it (6 and 11 lives lost to walkers for 12 and 16) is given up. (2) **The searches ahead are counted apart.** As planned they were among `ways_sought`, with `ways_ahead` saying how many of them. An existing test of the bench (`test_the_bench_reports_the_ways_past`) holds `ways_sought` to three a go, and a way found ahead is free by design, so a go can now make more than three searches in all. `ways_sought` and `ways_found` stay the go's own searches (after a life lost, at a standstill), at most `ways_per_go`; `ways_ahead` and `ways_ahead_found` are beside them on the runner, in the result and in the bench's report, and `describe_ways()` says them after: ", saw a life going 3 times before it went and found a way past 2 times". Said plainly: a go's searches of all kinds together are no longer at most three. (3) **Giving up** (new). `give_up_after` searches ahead in a row for nothing, from go to go, and the runner looks ahead no more (`ahead_gave_up`), counted apart as the searches at a standstill are. Without it a game in which they never find anything would cost up to three searches of 15 s in every go for ever. (4) **A loop, mended.** A way found ahead put the game back; ten steps on the same loss was seen again from the same moment and the same way found, without end. `_ahead_past`: no look ahead until the story is past the step that life would have gone at. (5) **An option, off below the app.** `EpisodeRunner(look_ahead=False)`, `TrainingService(look_ahead=False)`, `practice_bench.run(look_ahead=False)` and `--look-ahead`; `AppContext` asks for it. Two older tests are why. With it on in every service, `tests/integration/test_first_demonstration.py::test_first_working_demonstration` fails: it measures the learner alone by lives lost late against early (0.0060 a step against 0.0066), and with so few lost early there is little left to improve. With it on in every bench run, `tests/integration/test_practice_bench.py::test_the_ground_holds_through_going_back` fails its `far.ways_sought >= 30  # it goes back often`: with fewer lives lost the goes' own searches in that run are 28 (36 on main), with 18 more made before a life went. Neither assertion is changed. The older tests of the service and the bench run with looking ahead off, as they were written (the bench's tests already say of `stand` and `remember` that they "stay on the goes they were written for"), and a new slow test, `tests/integration/test_practice_bench_looking_ahead.py`, runs that same level with it asked for and holds the ground count there too. Boss was asked (17 Nov) whether that one assertion may count both kinds of going back, in which case the bench would look ahead unless told not to, as the app does; the question was taken back once the task was merged, since nothing waited on it: the bench looks ahead only when told to, and the assertion stands as written. (6) Smaller: `Moments.before_loss(ahead)`; `_keep_moment()` goes on saving while a search ahead may still be made; a search ahead that finds nothing, or has no moment far enough before the step the life would go at, leaves the saved moments alone (no life was lost); a way found ahead does not touch the count of searches after a life lost that found nothing; the bench reads the new counts with `getattr`, since its older tests drive it with stand-ins that have none; the service's sentence is said where it was asked to look ahead and goes can go back. (7) The tests are more than the plan named, and some are named otherwise: see Results.

The goes' own searches were 465 for 513 (fewer lives are lost), and found a way in 397 for 407. The sixteen runs took 3,217 s for main's 2,962 s (9% longer), and the longest against main's was a third longer (163 s for 123 s; the criterion: not more than half as long again). - **Completion report:** Knowing which kinds of thing had cost a life changed nothing in what the AI did, because the search that gets it past an enemy began only once a life had gone. It now looks ahead when a thing of such a kind comes near: it plays what it is about to do off the record, and where that would cost a life it goes back to a saved moment and finds the way past before the life is lost. On the practice game, sixteen runs each, lives lost to walkers fell from 152 to 57 and levels finished rose from 182 to 255, for runs 9% longer. Measuring found two faults in what was first built (a loop, and a queue that kept a go from looking for a way on at a wall), and both are mended and tested. 40 new tests, 131 deliberate breaks all noticed, no existing test changed, the whole suite passing.

### T-1051 – What cost a life, by who was closest and how it was met
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 2, the screen read right: the AI cannot keep away from what it does not know hurts).
- **Why now:** Boss, 16 Nov: "I still dont get how it keeps dying to the first enemy or any enemy of the same type. It should go oh whats that tag it, oh it killed me when it touch me, best keep the fuck away from them in the future. And then if the same enemy kills them in a different way, oh they can do that too, best remember that. Why is not working like this."
- **What his logs and the code show (16 Nov, read before the plan):**
  1. *Most lives lost are put down to nothing.* The summaries `ScreenWatch.describe` writes, across his sessions: 92 lives lost, 32 soon after touching something, 4 after a fall; 67, 18 and 3; 48, 23 and 7; 29, 14 and 3. More than half the time nothing was waiting when the life went. `RoleLearner` counts a touch only at a look at which the player's box and a thing's box are within 2 pixels and the thing is in sight with its kind known. A look comes every 2 steps of 4 frames: 8 frames, in which the two close some 16 to 24 pixels, so the look before the hit shows them apart, and the looks after it show whatever the game shows of a hit (on his game everything stops; what the tracker makes of the stopped enemy beside the player is not known from the logs).
  2. *What is blamed is outvoted.* A kind hurts only if a life went after at least half of all its touches (`HALF`). The kinds twice marked as an enemy (thing-4, thing-5: "enemy" at 2 touches, "harmless" at 4) ended the last session as "thing-4 is harmless (high, 29 touches)". Coming down on an enemy is a touch too, and is harmless or a pick-up (it vanishes and the score goes up): one enemy met two ways is one tally.
  3. *The look back is barely long enough.* A touch waits `SOON_LOOKS` = 30 looks (240 frames, 4 s on his settings) for a life to go. His logs' searches say when each loss was settled: 52 to 57 steps before the count dropped where the way past was a jump (26 to 28.5 looks), 67 to 76 steps where it was not (falls, by the look of it: 33.5 to 38 looks, and only 3 to 7 lives in a session were put down to a fall). On the practice bench with its long dying pause (200 frames) main puts 6 of 56 lives lost to a walker down to nothing for the same reason.
- **Try-outs (16 Nov, before the plan, in scratch scripts and a scratch copy of main, described as such):** (a) On 12 practice runs (six levels, both pauses) main's learner, touches seen: every walker's kind is found to hurt; 123 walker deaths, 117 put down to the walker's kind (all 6 misses with the long pause). (b) The same with touches never seen at all (a stand-in for his game) and the rule "with no touch waiting, the thing that came closest within 32 pixels in the looks before": 125 walker deaths, 116 lives put down to the walker's kind, 4 to the pick-up's, and 5 walker deaths to nothing. (Whether any of those was a fall blamed on a thing the try-out did not tell apart: criterion 7 does.) (c) The rule (b) with touches seen as they are: the same tallies as main, run for run (it is used only where nothing waits). (d) `SOON_LOOKS` at 45 with (b) in place: `test_vision.py`, `test_roles.py` and both bench integration files pass but for one assertion, which is the point of (b) and needs Boss's word (criterion 8).
- **Objective:** (1) `RoleLearner` keeps each touch with the way it was made, from where the player was against the thing at that look: from above (its feet no lower than the thing's middle), from below (its head no higher than the thing's middle), else from the side; `KindEvidence` keeps touches, lives lost and pick-ups for each way beside the totals. A kind hurts when in any one way a life went after at least half its touches made that way, or by the totals as before. (2) At each look the learner also notes every thing of a known kind within `REACH` (32 pixels, what may move between two looks) of the player and not touching. A life lost with no touch waiting is put down to the closest of those still waiting (the latest of equals), as a touch that cost a life, made the way it stood then, and counted as `unseen`. (3) `SOON_LOOKS` is 45. (4) `ScreenWatch` writes one line to the log for every life lost: what it was put down to, how, how many looks before, what else was waiting; or that it was a fall; or that nothing was seen. Its summary says how many lives were put down to the closest thing, and a role's line says after how many touches of each way a life went.
- **Scope:** `understanding/roles.py`, `training/vision.py` (the calls, the log, the summary, `SOON_LOOKS`), tests, the documents. **Out of scope:** which of several waiting touches is blamed (the latest, as before: the new log line will show whether that is right on his game); what the brain is given of a thing that hurts (as before: where the nearest one is; the way it hurts is not yet in its view); the lesson put where the touch was instead of where the count dropped (the task after); the same enemy split over several kinds (75 kinds on his game); what is known of kinds kept from one session to the next (it is learnt anew each session, as before); the default "Gaining Lives" reward paying for a count that falls below nought (T-1050's limit 2: its own task).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. The way of a touch is told from the boxes as the objective says, for a player larger or smaller than the thing, and is that of the look the touch began at.
  2. A kind that costs a life from the side and is come down on harmlessly, however often, hurts; one that costs a life once among several harmless touches made the same way does not (as before); every result the old rule gave "hurts" for is still "hurts".
  3. A life lost with no touch waiting is put down to the closest thing of a known kind noted within `REACH` in the last `soon` looks, the latest of equals; not to the player's own tracks, a thing out of sight, a thing with no kind, or one further off or longer ago; a touch waiting is always preferred; a fall lets them go; one life is put down to one thing, and what was noted is forgotten with it.
  4. `SOON_LOOKS` is 45: through `ScreenWatch` a life lost 40 looks after a touch is put down to it, and one 50 looks after is not.
  5. The log has one line for each life lost, in each of the four cases (a touch, the closest thing, a fall, nothing), with the kind, the way, the looks before and the distance where there are any, and up to three other touches that were waiting.
  6. The summary says how many lives were put down to the closest thing, only when there are any; a role's line says after how many touches of each way a life went, only for a kind a life was ever put down to; `lives_after_touch` counts what it counted before.
  7. On the practice bench, six levels and both pauses, with touches seen: no fewer walker deaths put down to the walker's kind than main (117 of 123), and the long pause's misses (6 of 56) fewer. With touches never seen: at least 9 in 10 put down to the walker's kind, and no fall blamed on a thing.
  8. Every existing test passes with no assertion changed, but for those Boss approves by name: known so far, the last line of `test_a_life_lost_to_a_walker_on_the_ground_is_put_down_to_it` ("the same go seen the old way: nothing is put down to the walker"), which the closest-thing rule makes untrue.
  9. Every new line broken on purpose in a scratch worktree and noticed; the whole suite passes, run alone.
