### T-1050 – A go ends when the game is over
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (what a go is: Boss's ask of 15 Nov, "each try plays till game over and the restart counts as the next go", built as T-1044 and T-1045).
- **Why now:** Boss, 16 Nov: "when it got game over the 'goes' number didn't go up". **His log of that session** (the list on "game over"): go 68 began at 16:05:38 and ended at 16:22:28 because he pressed Stop, after 24,819 steps, with "Lifes goes down" paid 64 times: about 21 games played to their end inside one go. Its three searches (the most a go may make) were used up in the first minute, each at a standstill, so none of the 64 lives lost was followed by one.
- **What the log and the code show (16 Nov, read before the plan):**
  1. *The game starting over is not read on his game.* The count he named "Lifes" (ram[1882]) reads 2 at a game's start and falls 2, 1, 0; the last life takes it below nought, to 255; a new game sets it to 2. (The log records no readings of the count: that it is counted this way is known of the game, and the log agrees with it, as follows.) `EventDetector` (T-1022) holds that a life count going down is a life lost and never the game starting over: 255 to 2 is "down", so the one snapshot in which the game does begin again is ruled out as a restart, and counted as a life lost (64 is three for each game: 2 to 1, 1 to 0, and 255 to 2). The fall below nought, 0 to 255, reads as a rise: nothing.
  2. *The wait for nothing paid never runs out.* T-1044 ends such a go once it has been paid nothing for as long as "Each go lasts" says. His own row "x position goes up" paid 5,954 times in that go: a person's "goes up" row pays every time, new ground or not, so walking the first screens of each new game is pay.
  3. *What the app takes that count for changes from session to session* (in his nine logs: Unknown, Progress and Lives), so the rule cannot go by the kind the AI guesses. What does not change is that it is the value his penalty is on, which is what lives lost are counted on (T-940).
- **Objective:** `EpisodeSignals` reads the game being over from the values lives lost are counted on, health guesses left out (`watch_lives`). For each it notes what it read when the go began and whether it has fallen by one. A change of more than one, on a count that has fallen and has never before changed by more than one in this go, is the game over if (a) it leaves nought for more than the count began with (it fell below nought: every life is lost, and that life is counted as lost), or (b) it comes to exactly what the count read when the go began (the game set it anew). Either is a restart to the runner: a search for a way past the life goes first where one may be made (T-1013), and otherwise the go ends, by "game_over" where nothing else said the game started over, in words "the game was over", and the log says what was read.
- **Scope:** `training/episode.py` (signals and the two places a go ends by a restart), `training/service.py` (the reason in the go's log line), `ui/learning_panel.py` (the words), tests, the documents. **Out of scope:** `EventDetector`'s own rule for a restart (T-1021, T-1022: unchanged, and its RESET ends a go as before); a game with one life to spare, whose count is set anew by a step of one (it cannot be told from a life given: the wait for nothing paid is what is left there); the penalty for the life that falls below nought (the person's "goes down" row does not pay for 0 to 255; before this it paid when the next game began, some seconds late); more than three searches in a go.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. A count that fell by one at least once and then goes from nought to more than it began the go with: the game is over at that update, and one life lost is counted for it.
  2. A count that fell by one at least once and then comes to what it read when the go began by a change of more than one: the game is over, and no life is counted for it.
  3. Nothing else is: a change of one either way (a life lost, a life given, even back to where it began); a change of more than one before any fall; a change of more than one to anything else; and after any of the last two, nothing more in that go for that value (it is no plain count of lives). A health guess is never read. A value lives lost are not counted on is never read.
  4. What a count read when the go began and whether it fell are the go's: a new go begins anew. Going back to an earlier moment keeps them.
  5. The runner treats it as the game starting over: with a life lost at that step and a search still to be made, the search goes first and a way found carries the go on; otherwise the go ends. It ends "game_over" where the count alone said so, and "reset" as before where the detector did.
  6. The go's line in the log says what was read ("... went from 0 to 255 ..."), the Learning panel says "the game was over", and the log says in a plain sentence, once a session, that goes end this way. *(The last clause was dropped: see Changed while building.)*
  7. On the practice games through the real services nothing that ended a go before ends it otherwise. Every existing test passes with no assertion changed.
  8. Every new line broken on purpose in a scratch worktree and noticed; the whole suite passes, run alone.
- **Expected changes:** `src/retro_ai_lab/training/episode.py`, `src/retro_ai_lab/training/service.py`, `src/retro_ai_lab/ui/learning_panel.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_a_go_ends_when_the_game_is_over.py` (new), `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, this tracker.
- **Test plan (written before the task's code):** `test_a_go_ends_when_the_game_is_over.py`. On `EpisodeSignals` with events put on the bus: `test_below_nought_is_the_game_over_and_a_life_lost` (1), `test_set_anew_is_the_game_over` (2), `test_a_step_of_one_is_never_it` (3), `test_a_jump_before_any_fall_or_to_elsewhere_rules_the_value_out` (3), `test_only_the_values_lives_are_counted_on_and_no_health` (3), `test_a_new_go_begins_anew` (4). On the runner with the practice game, its memory's count of lives played as Boss's game plays it (a stand-in adapter that hands on every call and rewrites that one byte: 2, 1, 0, 255, then 2): `test_the_go_ends_by_game_over` (5, 6), `test_a_search_goes_first_and_a_way_found_carries_on` (5), `test_the_detectors_restart_still_ends_it_by_reset` (5, 7). The panel's words (6). Then the breaks of criterion 8, the existing tests of the runner, the service and the practice games, and the whole suite alone.
- **Changed while building:** (1) **Criterion 6's last clause was dropped**: "the log says in a plain sentence, once a session, that goes end this way". The go's own line in the log gives the reason each time ("... went from 0 to 255: it fell below nought, so every life is lost"), which says more than a sentence once a session would, and nothing was built for the sentence. (2) **The tests are more than the plan named.** On the signals: `test_below_nought_is_the_game_over_and_a_life_lost`, `test_below_nought_is_anything_above_what_the_go_began_with`, `test_set_anew_is_the_game_over`, `test_set_anew_from_wherever_it_stood`, `test_a_step_of_one_is_never_it`, `test_a_jump_before_any_fall_rules_the_value_out`, `test_a_jump_to_elsewhere_rules_the_value_out`, `test_only_the_values_lives_are_counted_on_and_no_health`, `test_the_values_read_are_those_last_handed_over`, `test_a_change_told_twice_is_read_once`, `test_nothing_is_read_while_no_go_is_on`, `test_a_new_go_begins_anew`, `test_with_the_detectors_restart_it_is_a_restart`. On the runner, the practice game's dying pause replaced by one that counts as Boss's game does (the plan said a stand-in adapter; patching the game's own pause is less code and the same bytes): `test_the_go_ends_by_game_over`, `test_without_the_count_nothing_is_read`, `test_a_count_nobody_named_is_named_as_the_ai_names_it`, `test_a_health_guess_is_not_read`, `test_a_search_goes_first_and_a_way_found_carries_on`, `test_with_no_way_found_the_go_ends_by_game_over`. The plan's `test_the_detectors_restart_still_ends_it_by_reset` is the existing `test_restart_with_a_life_lost.py`, unchanged and passing. (3) **A second file was added, through the training service** (`test_each_game_over_is_the_next_go.py`): the plan tested the runner only, and Boss's words were about the number of goes, which the service counts. The practice racer is made to count the lives in reserve and go below nought with the last. (4) A test that the tries of a search cannot change how the go is said to have ended was written and taken out again: the tries are played off the record and tell the signals nothing, so the case cannot arise and the test could not stage it.
- **Results:** 30 new tests pass (28 in the first file with their parameters, 2 in the second). **Through the training service**, twelve goes with the racer counting as Boss's game does: every go that lost its last life (the last six in a row among them) ended "game_over" at that step with its line in the log giving the reason, every other go ended as before ("no_gain"), each go began from the saved start with every life, and the number of goes was twelve; with the racer as it is, six goes ended as before. **Broken on purpose** in a scratch worktree, 60 ways, against the three new and changed places (`episode.py`, `service.py`, `learning_panel.py`): the first round noticed 47 of the 55 that applied (5 did not apply: the script looked for three lines that are not next to each other); the 8 missed were real gaps (a game over nobody asked about before a go was stopped carried into the next go; values handed over earlier staying read; a change with only one reading; a count that had only risen; the values the detector blamed last kept beside the count's reason; a health guess read; the reason left off a detector's restart in the log). Six tests were added or widened and one existing test added to those run, and then **all 60 were noticed**, run again from the start against the finished tests. **No existing test was changed.** The whole suite, run alone: **2,354 passed, 10 skipped**. `ruff` and `mypy` clean.
- **Limits:** (1) **Not yet seen on his game.** It is built from his log and from how his game is known to count; his next log will show it (each go's line says what the count did). (2) **The default "Gaining Lives" reward still pays for the count going from 0 to 255** (seen in the service test: +5 once in each such go), and his own "goes down" row does not pay for that last life. The go now ends there, so it is once a go and not once a game, but it is pay for dying and is the next thing to mend. (3) A game with one life in reserve, whose count is set anew by a step of one, cannot be told from a life given: the wait for nothing paid is what is left there. (4) A go that begins with no saved start, on a screen where the count is already below nought, reads nothing in that go (the first change it sees is a jump before any fall). (5) Two lives lost between two looks at the memory read as a jump and rule the count out for that go. (6) A value that is no count of lives but behaves like one (falls by ones and then returns to exactly where it began by a jump) would end a go: only the values lives lost are counted on are read, and health guesses never. (7) After a game over the game is not asked whether it listens (T-848 asks after "stuck" and "reset"): the next go begins from the saved start as always.
- **Commit:** see PR #292. **PR:** #292.
- **Completion report:** Boss's game counts the lives in reserve and takes the count below nought when the last one goes, and the app read neither that nor the new game's count as the game starting over, so one go ran through some twenty games. The signals of a go now read the game being over from the values lives lost are counted on: a count that has fallen by one in the go and then goes from nought to more than it began with, or comes back to exactly what it began with by a jump, is the game over, and the last life is counted. The runner treats it as any restart (a search for a way past first, where one may be made), ends the go "game_over", the goes table says "the game was over" and the log says what the count did. 30 new tests, 60 of 60 deliberate breaks noticed after eight gaps were closed, no existing test changed, the whole suite passing.

### T-1049 – A put-back the screen cannot show
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 2, the screen read right: what is paid for must be what was done). Begun while T-1048 waits for Boss's word on two older tests, on its own branch; this task does not touch what T-1048 changes.
- **Why now:** T-1041's limit 3 was open: "a next level that looks just like the last is no cut to the tracker: the watch stays in one place and its camera carries on". Tried out (below), that is harmless. The same try-out showed something that is not: **after a life lost in the second practice level the ground walked there before is paid again**, and on single practice levels too. Pay for ground walked twice after dying is pay for dying. Boss's standing proof is a level finished without dying.
- **Try-outs (16 Nov, before the plan, in scratch tests and a scratch copy of main, described as such):**
  1. *A second level that looks like the first* (T-1047's go, the practice game's colours made the same for every level). The watch stays in one place and its camera carries on from 2,327 to 4,631: the second level's ground is counted once, 144 steps and 151 points, the same as where the level is a new place. Nothing to mend.
  2. *A life lost 87 steps into the second level* (the same go, then holding right into what is in the way; with the level a new place or looking like the first, with the camera's count known or not: the same each time). The game puts the player back at the level's start. The watch's furthest was 561; walking on again from the start it rises at once (644 after 20 steps, 957 after 60), and at the flag it stands at 2,848 on a level whose camera travels 2,304: **178 steps of ground counted where the level has 144.** In the first level of the same cartridge the same loss is seen for what it is: the furthest stays at 576 until the player is past it.
  3. *Why.* A life lost is taken for a put-back when the screen jolts (2 in 100 of it changed with no camera move to explain it, T-993) or cuts. At the first level's loss 6 in 100 changed. At the second level's, bare ground with one wall in sight, 0.7 in 100: the picture lines the start's screen up with the screen where the life went and reads a slide of 17 pixels back. No jolt, so the camera carries on from where the life went and every step walked again is new. With the count known the tracker is, rightly, not given its word at a look in which a life went (T-1020), so nothing gainsays the picture.
  4. *How often on the practice levels* (the bench, levels 0 to 7, the game's own pause, 12 goes each, main): the furthest the watch counted is the game's own, to a step, in **79 of 96 goes** (the bench's target is 90 in 100). Of the 17 that are not, 7 counted too little (early goes, before the camera is followed) and **10 counted too much, by 18 to 513 pixels, every one of them a go with lives lost.** On level 6 the losses the watch missed read as slides of 13 to 31 pixels on with 0.3 in 100 of the screen changed.
  5. *A first rule:* a life lost, the player seen elsewhere on the screen, and the game's count of its camera gone to what it was at the place's door by something other than the slide the picture read. **86 of 96.** It misses the losses of level 6: there the life goes 24 pixels short of a multiple of 256, the count goes from 232 to 0, which is 24 on the short way round, and the picture, lining up ground that repeats every 32 pixels, reads 24 on as well. Count and picture agree and both are wrong.
  6. *The rule of this task:* a life lost, the player seen elsewhere on the screen, and the count at what it was at the place's door while the watch's camera is more than a look's slide from that door. **88 of 96**; of the 8 left, 6 counted too little as before and 2 too much (by 104 and 424 pixels). 78 levels finished either way, 55 lives lost for 50. The tests of the bench, of the watch and of the two-level cartridge pass with it unchanged (112 tests).
- **Objective:** `ScreenWatch` keeps, for each place of a go, the game's memory as it was at that place's door (the go's first look, or the look a new place was settled at). At a look in which the player is seen further than its own size from where it was last seen, every byte found for the camera's count (T-1020) reads what it read at the door of the place it is in, and the ground's camera stands more than `LOOK_SHIFT` from that door in a way a byte is found for, the count is said to have gone to the door. With a life lost within `BACK_LOOKS` looks of that, before or after, the game put the player back: the ground is at the door (`Ground.back()`), what the picture read as that look's slide is not counted, and the log says so the first time.
- **Scope:** `training/vision.py`, tests, the documents. **Out of scope:** a put-back to somewhere that is not the place's door (a checkpoint part-way: the count is not the door's, and the jolt and the cut decide as before); a count not found yet (twenty looks moving and twenty still, T-1020: as before until then); the high half of a count that is two bytes wide, which would tell a put-back from a slide outright; the watches a search lends its tries (they are given no memory); a life lost where the player stays on the same spot of the screen through a put-back.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. With the count found, a life lost at a look in which the player is seen elsewhere, the count is the door's and the camera is more than `LOOK_SHIFT` from the door: the ground is at the door at that look (its camera at nought, the slide the picture read not counted), what was reached stays reached, and ground walked again is counted and paid nothing until the furthest is passed.
  2. The life and the count's going to the door may be up to `BACK_LOOKS` looks apart, either first; further apart nothing is done.
  3. Each of these alone, or any but all, is nothing: the life lost; the player seen elsewhere; the count at the door's value; the camera far from the door.
  4. The door's value is the place's own: for a go's first place the memory at its first look, for a new place the memory at the look it was settled at. A place whose door had no memory, or a memory of another layout than now, has no door value and nothing is done.
  5. A watch handed no memory, or one whose count is not found yet, is look for look the watch it was.
  6. The first such put-back of a watch is said in the log in a plain sentence; later ones in the detailed log only. A new go or a going back to a kept moment forgets a count gone to the door that no life has yet answered.
  7. On the two-level practice cartridge through the real services, with the count known: after a life lost in the second level the furthest does not rise until the player is past where it was, and at the level's flag it is the camera's whole travel to within a step.
  8. Measured on practice levels 0 to 23 with both pauses on the usual dice and with the game's own pause on other dice, against main: the goes whose counted ground is the game's own. Every new line broken on purpose in a scratch worktree and noticed. Every existing test passes with no assertion changed; the whole suite passes, run alone.
- **Expected changes:** `src/retro_ai_lab/training/vision.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_vision_put_back_by_count.py` (new), `tests/integration/test_a_life_lost_in_the_second_level.py` (new), `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, this tracker (and T-1041's limit 3 is answered here).
- **Test plan (written before the task's code; the try-outs above came first):** `test_vision_put_back_by_count.py`, on the practice game with a watch handed its memory and one handed none, the lives lost told to the watch by the test so that each condition can be had without the others: `test_put_back_by_the_count_where_the_picture_reads_a_slide` (1), `test_ground_walked_again_pays_nothing_until_the_furthest` (1), `test_the_life_and_the_count_may_be_a_few_looks_apart` (2), `test_no_one_sign_is_enough` (3), `test_near_the_door_nothing_is_done` (3), `test_the_door_is_the_places_own` (4), `test_a_door_with_no_memory_has_no_value` (4), `test_without_the_count_it_is_the_watch_it_was` (5), `test_the_log_says_it_once` (6), `test_a_new_go_and_a_going_back_forget_it` (6). `test_a_life_lost_in_the_second_level.py`: `test_the_ground_walked_again_is_not_paid_again` (7). Then the measurements and the breaks of criterion 8, the tests of the bench, the watch and the two-level cartridge, and the whole suite alone.
- **Changed while building:** (1) **Three conditions written first were taken out, because nothing could ever make them matter** (the deliberate breaks showed it, and reading the code why): a door's memory of another length than now (a change of layout voids every door's memory already, and that is what a new test, "renamed", holds: the same bytes under another name); a ground that does not scroll (a count is only found from looks in which the camera moved, and those are what make a ground scroll); a quiet watch saying it in the detailed log only (a watch lent for a try has found no count). (2) **The tests' names and number.** `test_put_back_by_the_count_where_the_screen_shows_none` for the planned `..._where_the_picture_reads_a_slide`; and six tests the plan did not have, each for a line the breaks showed unheld: `test_a_count_one_off_the_doors_is_not_the_doors` (3), `test_far_from_the_door_is_far_either_way` (3: left of the door as well as right), `test_with_no_life_lost_it_is_no_put_back` (3; `test_no_one_sign_is_enough` keeps the life lost where the count comes round to the door's value 256 pixels on with the player on the same spot of the screen), `test_a_new_places_door_is_its_own` (4: a cut to a level's start in other colours, whose door reads nought where the first place's read 73; and a watch lent for a try, which knows the places and none of their doors' memory), `test_a_look_handed_no_memory_tells_nothing` (5), `test_a_put_back_told_uses_up_its_signs` (6: neither the life nor the count answers twice). 23 unit tests and 1 through the real services. (3) **How the unit tests take the screen's own sign away.** On the first practice level the screen does show a put-back (a jolt), so the tests set `JOLT` out of reach: the count is all there is to go by. Where a put-back is *not* taken for one, the picture reads a few pixels of slide into that look, so those tests hold that the watch is still out where it was to within one look's slide, not to the pixel; where it *is* taken for one they hold nought exactly. Within a look's slide of the door the picture reads the put-back as the slide it is and has it right by itself: there the test holds that the rule is not used (nothing said) and the watch is where the one without the count is. (4) **The measurement of criterion 8 is wider than planned** (below): the long pause on three sets of dice, because the first long-pause run finished fewer levels.
- **Results:** 24 new tests pass; against main's watch the tests of the rule fail as they should, the integration test among them (the camera at 544 where it should be at the door). **Broken on purpose** in a scratch worktree, 37 ways: **36 noticed** (11 of 38 were not at the first round; six tests were added and three conditions taken out for them, changes 1 and 2). The one left changes nothing that can be seen: a new go forgetting the last go's door memory, where every place's door is written again before it can be read; the line is kept so that nothing of a go outlives it. **The second practice level through the real services:** a life lost 87 steps in, the watch at the door one look later, the furthest still 561 until the player is past it, nothing counted and nothing paid on the way, and at the flag the camera's whole travel (2,304) with **144 steps of ground counted for the level, where main counted 178.** **Measured** (the practice bench, levels 0 to 23, 12 goes each, 288 goes a run; the try-out's code, which the built code equals to the last figure on the 12 levels compared, and the built code itself for the last two runs), goes whose counted ground is the game's own to a step, main then this: the usual dice with the game's own pause **202 then 236**, with the long pause **203 then 219**; dice 1000 with the game's own pause **234 then 254**, with the long pause **222 then 247**; dice 2000 with the long pause **214 then 246**. Together **1,075 then 1,202 of 1,440** (75 in 100, then 83; the bench's target is 90). Levels finished, the same five: 209 then 211, 210 then 198, 201 then 203, 191 then 196, 193 then 185: **1,004 then 993.** Lives lost: 505 then 508. With T-1048 merged in as well (levels 0 to 7, the usual dice, the game's own pause, against main with T-1048): 82 of 96 goes counted right for 77, 83 levels finished for 86, 50 lives lost for 47. Whole suite, run alone with main (T-1048) merged in: 2324 passed, 10 skipped. ruff and mypy clean.
- **Limits:** (1) **It does not get the AI through more levels.** Levels finished are as they were, to within what the dice alone do (two runs of five a little up, one the same, two down by 12 and 8). What is mended is what the AI is paid for: ground walked again after dying no longer pays. (2) **17 goes in 100 are still not counted right** on the practice levels. On the first two runs, where the try-out's code says which way each is out, 74 of the 121 counted too little (on the eight levels looked at closely those were early goes, before the camera is followed) and 47 too much. (3) Only a put-back to the place's door is told: a checkpoint part-way reads another count. (4) A put-back that leaves the player on the same spot of the screen is not told (a go begun part-way along and put back to its beginning). (5) Nothing until the count is found (twenty looks moving and twenty still, T-1020), and nothing for the watches a search lends its tries. (6) A count two bytes wide would tell a put-back from a slide outright; only the byte that moves with the camera is found. (7) **Not yet seen on a real game.**
- **Commit:** see PR #291. **PR:** #291.
- **Completion report:** After a life lost on plain ground the start of a level can look so much like the spot where the life went that the screen shows no jump; the watch's camera then carried on from where the AI died and every step walked again was paid as new. The watch now keeps the game's memory as it was at each place's door, and a life lost with the player seen elsewhere on the screen and the game's own count of its camera reading what it read at that door, while the watch has the camera more than a look's slide from it, is the game putting the player back. On the second practice level the ground is counted once (144 steps for 178), and on 24 practice levels five ways the counted ground is the game's own in 1,202 of 1,440 goes for 1,075. Levels finished did not change. **Next:** T-1050, a go that ends when the game is over on Boss's game (his log of 16 Nov: one go ran 17 minutes through 64 lives lost); then a kind of thing that has cost a life staying known as one that hurts (in nine of his logs, some 340 lives lost and never more than two kinds marked, each outvoted by harmless touches soon after).

(1) **The cause.** In the second level's first 80 pixels of camera travel the picture alone reads "no move" (plain ground and one 16-pixel wall in sight: all that changes is one small thing, which T-992 rightly takes for no camera move). That is the case the game's own count of its camera is for (T-1020), and the watch had not found it: `camera_bytes` was `(None, None)` at the flag, with 146 looks read as moving and only 8 as still, where a byte needs 20 of each before it is believed. The player of T-1041 runs right from its first step and never stands. (2) **With the count found.** The same go with a player who first hops on the spot for 60 steps (and for 40): the watch finds `ram[19]`, the practice game's scroll, on the way to the first flag ("in 49 of the 55 looks it has compared"). In the second level the tracker then takes the count's word at every look where the picture reads nothing (9, 16, 16, 16, 16 pixels), the watch's furthest is never more than a step (8 pixels) behind the game's camera, at the flag it is the game's 2,304 to the pixel (2,147 before, 157 short), and 144 steps of ground are counted there (134 before) and 151 points paid (135 before). (3) **Boss's game.** His two logs of 15 Nov each have the line "The AI found where the game keeps count of its camera" in the first go: 12 and 17 seconds after training began (11:25:36 and 17:54:16), long before a second level. A learning AI stands, waits and loses lives in its first goes; the practice player that never does was the odd one out. So this is not a fault his game meets, and nothing in the app is to be mended for it.
- **Objective:** an integration test on the two-level practice cartridge through the real services that holds try-out 2: with the camera's count found before the flag, the second level's ground is measured from the camera's first move. And T-1041's limit 2 answered in the documents.
- **Scope:** one new test file and the documents. **Out of scope:** any change to how a byte proves itself (20 looks of each kind is what keeps a clock or a counter from being taken for the camera); keeping the count between sessions (it is found again within the first minute); a next level that looks like the last (T-1041's limit 3); the bench on more than one level.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. A player who hops on the spot before it sets off has no count while it hops (the camera has not moved yet) and has it by the first flag: the practice game's scroll byte, across only, and the log says so once.
  2. Four steps after the flag the watch is in a second place with nothing reached there (as T-1041).
  3. From there, over the next 30 steps, the watch's furthest in the new place is never ahead of the game's camera and never more than one step's move (8 pixels) behind it.
  4. At the second flag the watch's furthest is the furthest the game's camera went, to the pixel; at least 140 steps of ground were counted in the second level, no life was lost, and the go was paid at least a point for each.
  5. The same holds for a shorter wait (40 steps) as for a longer (60).
  6. The test fails when the count's word is taken away, each way: the watch not handing it to the tracker, the tracker not taking it, and a byte never proving itself (broken on purpose in a scratch worktree). Every existing test passes unchanged; the whole suite passes, run alone.
- **Expected changes:** `tests/integration/test_a_new_level_with_the_camera_known.py` (new), `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, this tracker (and T-1041's limit 2 is answered here).
- **Test plan (written before the test):** `test_the_second_levels_ground_is_measured_from_its_first_move`, run for a wait of 40 steps and of 60 (5): no count while hopping, the count and the log line by the first flag (1); the second place four steps on (2); 30 steps with the watch's furthest set against the game's camera at each (3); the second flag (4). Then the breaks of criterion 6 in a scratch worktree, the existing tests of the integration folder, and the whole suite alone.
- **Changed while building:** (1) The try-out's times for Boss's logs were wrong as first written in the plan (I had read two lines of one log for the two logs) and are corrected above: 12 and 17 seconds after training began. (2) The hopping player's runner has giving up for standing about switched off (`unstick_after=None`): with it on, the go ended after 25 steps of hopping, which is right for a go and not what this test looks at. (3) Hopping, the player ends at the level's left edge and not where it started; the test asks only that the camera has not moved. (4) Six breaks were tried for criterion 6, not three: the three named, the runner not showing the watch the game's memory, the watch never showing memory to what learns the count, and the count's change read the wrong way round.
- **Results:** 2 new tests pass (one test, for a wait of 40 steps and of 60; 15 seconds together), on the practice game through the real services. **What they hold (seed 0, two levels):** no count while the player hops; by the first flag the count is the practice game's scroll byte, across only, said once in the log; four steps after the flag the watch is in place 2 of 2 with nothing reached there; over the next 30 steps its furthest is never ahead of the game's camera and never more than 8 pixels behind (81 pixels behind with the count's word taken away); at the second flag it is the camera's 2,304 to the pixel, with at least 140 steps of ground counted in the second level, no life lost, and at least a point paid for each step counted. **Breaks** in a scratch worktree, this test run against each: **6 of 6 noticed**. Whole suite, run alone: 2,281 passed, 10 skipped (2,279 and 10 on main, unchanged, and the 2 new). **T-1041's limit 2 is answered:** the cause was the practice player, not the new place.
- **Limits:** (1) A byte is believed only after 20 looks with the camera moving and 20 with it at rest, so until then bare ground is still not measured, in a first level as in a new one. On Boss's game that was the first 12 to 17 seconds of training. A player or a remembered way that never lets the camera rest would not get there; a learning AI does, and each go begins with the camera at rest. (2) The count is not kept between sessions: it is found again each time training starts. (3) One cartridge (seed 0) and a player who knows the levels, as in T-1041. (4) T-1041's limit 3 stays open: a next level that looks just like the last is no cut to the tracker.
- **Commit:** see PR #288. **PR:** #288.
- **Completion report:** The camera's first moves in the second practice level went unmeasured in T-1041 because that test's player never stood still, so the AI had not yet found the game's own count of its camera, and bare ground is where the picture needs it. With a player who waits first, the count is found before the first flag and the second level's ground is measured from its first move, to the pixel at its flag. A test holds that and fails each way the count's word is taken away. Nothing in the app changed, and none was needed: Boss's game has its count found in the first go. **Next:** T-1043 once Boss has answered its card; otherwise practice levels that never finish, or a next level that looks like the last.

- **Status:** Done

### T-1044 – A go can last until the game is over
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (asked for by Boss on 15 Nov: "is it possible to have like a button or list for time or game over, then each try plays till game over and the restart counts as the next go"). T-1043 is built and measured on its own branch and waits for Boss's word on three older tests that state the rule it replaces; nothing of it is in this task.
- **Why now:** Boss's game now reaches its third level in goes of 40 seconds, and he asked whether the timer holds it back and for a go that lasts until game over. A go's own steps are what the timer counts (the way it remembers is played on top, T-1015), so the timer costs little; but a go that is getting further has no reason to be cut off, and he asked for the choice.
- **Try-out (before the plan, in scratch, described as one):** the service on the practice game (the racer of `test_service.py`) with the timer set out of reach. Go 1: the three lives went by step 110, the game sat at its game-over screen, and with no wake button known the go ended "stuck" at step 165. Goes 2 and on, with the wake button found: the lives went by step 48 or sooner and the go **never ended**. Nothing changing for 25 steps makes the go press on with its best-paid button first (T-1011, "once for each standstill"), the press moves a value on the dead screen, that counts as the standstill being over, and so on round: 123 presses in 3,000 steps, the wake button never pressed, the game never started over. With a timer the timer ends this; without one nothing does. So "until the game is over" needs a way to tell a game that is over which does not rest on the game saying so. With a rough form of criterion 2 in a scratch copy (50 steps), every go ended, the longest 86 steps.
- **Objective:** a go setting, kept for each game: the go lasts until the game is over. Such a go has no timer; it ends when the game starts over (as a go does now), when the go gives up (as now), or when its points have reached no new best for as long as "Each go lasts" says. What the points are is the person's rewards, so nothing about any game is written in. The restart is the next go, from the checkpoint, as every go begins.
- **Scope:** `training/episode.py` (`EpisodeRunner(gain_within=…)`, the end "no_gain"), `training/service.py` (`go_until_over`, `set_go_until_over`, what a go is built with), `training/brain.py` (`until_over`), tests, documents. **Out of scope:** the panel's list and its words (T-1045, next); a countdown on screen (Boss's other ask, after that); why the press at a standstill goes round on a dead screen in a go with a timer (it costs the rest of that go's time, as it did; here the new end covers it); tournaments and `run_for`, which keep their own limits.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. Without `gain_within` (the default) a go is the go it was, step for step: every existing test passes unchanged.
  2. With `gain_within` a go ends "no_gain" at the first step by which that many of its own steps have passed since its points last reached a new best; a go that never gains anything ends after that many own steps. The points are the rewards paid and what a go played straight would have been paid again after a going back (T-1028), as the way it remembers is valued.
  3. The steps of the way it remembers do not count (as for the timer, T-1015), and a way a search has just found is played to its end first (T-1018). The game starting over still ends the go as "reset", and the timer where it is reached first as "max_steps".
  4. A `gain_within` that is not a whole number of at least 1 is refused, in words.
  5. The service: `go_until_over` is off until asked for; `set_go_until_over` takes yes or no and nothing else, only while training is stopped; the change is announced as go settings are and written to disk at once.
  6. It is kept in the brain for that game (`until_over`, written only when on), comes back on reconnecting, and another game starts with it off. A brain saved before this task loads with it off; a value that is not yes or no is refused as bad brain data.
  7. With it on, the go is built with the 30 minutes of console time as its most (`UNTIL_OVER_MOST_FRAMES`) and with the time of "Each go lasts" as `gain_within`; that time itself (`max_steps`) is kept and is the timer again when the choice is switched off.
  8. On the practice game through the service, with it on: goes last past the time while they gain, none ends by the time, a go whose game is over ends (by the game starting over, by giving up, or "no_gain" the chosen time after its last gain) where in the try-out it never did, and the next go begins from the checkpoint with every life. The log's line for the go names the end.
  9. Every new line broken on purpose and noticed. The practice levels play as on main to the last figure (the bench builds its goes without the setting). The whole suite passes, run alone.
- **Expected changes:** `src/retro_ai_lab/training/episode.py`, `service.py`, `brain.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_go_until_over.py` (new), `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, this tracker. (The README says it with the panel's list, T-1045: until then a person has no way to choose it.)
- **Test plan (written before the code):** `test_go_until_over.py`. The runner, on the practice game with the rewards announced on the bus by the test: no `gain_within`, and a go of steps with and without pay ends by its timer at the step it did (1); with 10, paid at steps 3 and 7, it ends "no_gain" at step 17 and not before, and never paid at step 10 (2); a penalty and a pay that only makes the penalty good are no new best, a pay that tops the best is (2); what a straight go would have been paid again counts (2); a go that begins with a remembered way of 12 steps and gains nothing ends at 12 + 10 (3); a way a search found is played out past the count (3); the game starting over on the step the count runs out is "reset", and a timer of 8 with a count of 10 is "max_steps" at 8 (3); 0, -1, 2.5, true and a word are refused (4). The service: the default, the refusals, idle only, the announcement, the save, the brain's field both ways, an older brain's data, bad data, reconnect, another game (5, 6); what the runner is built with on and off, and the most a go may last for other frames a step (7); six goes on the practice game with it on and the time at 50 steps, their ends, their lengths, the lives at each go's first step, and the go's log line (8). Breaks in a scratch worktree (9), the practice levels (9), the whole suite alone (9).
- **Changed while building:** (1) **What ends such a go is that it has been paid nothing, not that its points have reached no new best** (criterion 2 and the plan's wording). Reading how rewards are paid showed why the points will not do: what pays for getting further pays only past the go's best (T-878), but penalties are paid again every time (a life lost, a step back). A go that had lost a life and been put back would have had to get well past its furthest, by as much as the penalties cost, before it counted as gaining anything, and would mostly have ended the set time after its first loss that stood. So the runner notes the own step on which the go was last paid, a step whose reward is above nought, and ends the go once `gain_within` own steps have passed since; a go never paid ends after that many. And what a go played straight would have been paid again after a going back (T-1028) is **not** counted, where the plan counted it: nobody is paid it, and a go that loses a life, goes back and gets the same ground again, round and round at one spot, would have counted as gaining for as long as it had searches left. The test plan's cases changed with it: a penalty, a step that costs more than it pays, a step that pays what it costs and what a straight go would have been paid again start no new count; a step that pays more than it costs does. (2) Two test files, not one: the runner's tests are on the practice hopper (`test_go_until_over.py`, 14) and the service's and the brain's on the practice racer (`test_go_until_over_setting.py`, 7), and the two games' fixtures have the same name. (3) The names: `EpisodeRunner(gain_within=…)`, the end "no_gain", `TrainingService.go_until_over`, `set_go_until_over`, `go_limits` (what the next go is built with), `until_over_most_steps`, `UNTIL_OVER_MOST_FRAMES`, `Brain.until_over`. (4) On one step the game starting over comes first, then the timer, then no pay. (5) A test beyond the plan: with the choice off and the timer out of reach the practice game's second go runs all its 3,000 steps at the game-over screen (the try-out, kept as a test of what the choice is for).
- **Results:** 21 new tests pass. **Broken on purpose** in a scratch worktree: 62 breaks, **62 noticed**; two were missed at first (the choice on before any game is connected; a brain made with nothing said about it having the choice on) and each got a check. **On the practice racer through the service**, the time at 50 steps, eight goes with the choice on: every go ends "no_gain" (83, 50, 109, 50, 50, 74, 50 and 58 steps), none by the time; the goes that were paid anything last past the time; three lost every life, were paid the last time as the game-over switch came on, and ended 50 steps later, where with no timer the same game's go never ended; every go begins from the checkpoint with its three lives. **The practice levels** (the bench builds its goes without the choice; long pause, levels 0 to 23, 12 goes each): 210 levels finished, 153 goes finishing, 77 lives lost, as on main to the last figure of all 24 runs. Whole suite, run alone: 2,255 passed, 10 skipped (2,234 on main and the 21 new; the two checks added after that run are in the new files, which were run again).
- **Limits:** (1) **Nobody can choose it yet.** The Learning panel's list is T-1045, next; until then the service has the choice and the panel does not, and the panel has no words for a go ended "no_gain" (it would show that word). The README says nothing of it until the list is there. (2) **Not seen on a real game.** On Boss's game a go that keeps getting further will now not be cut off, which is what he asked for. What happens there when the lives run out is not known: if the game shows a screen where nothing changes, the go gives up or presses the wake button and the game starts over, as before; if not, it ends the set time after its last pay. Either way the wait is at most that time. (3) **It is "until the game is over or nothing is paid for the set time", and the second can come first.** A go that stands about, or that keeps losing lives at one spot and is put back by the game with nothing new paid, ends the set time after its last pay with lives still in hand. On the racer four of eight goes were never paid and ended after 50 steps. A longer time (the box takes up to 600 seconds) makes that rarer. (4) A reward that pays again and again for nothing (a clock taken for a score, say) would keep such a go alive: 30 minutes of console time is the most a go may last. (5) Why a go with a timer sits at the practice game's game-over screen pressing on, and never presses the wake button it knows, is not looked into: it costs that go the rest of its time, as it did before this task. (6) Tournaments and `run_for` keep their own limits.
- **Commit:** see PR #285. **PR:** #285.
- **Completion report:** The training service has a choice, kept for each game in its brain and off unless asked for: a go lasts until the game is over. Such a go has no timer. It ends when the game starts over or the go gives up, as a go does now, or once it has been paid nothing for as long as "Each go lasts" says, counted in its own steps and with a way a search has just found played out first; 30 minutes of console time is the most. Without the choice a go is step for step the go it was. **Next:** T-1045, the list in the Learning panel to make the choice ("Each go lasts: for a set time / until the game is over"), with words for the new end and the README; then the countdown Boss asked for. T-1043 still waits for his word.

### T-1043 – The plain way has half of a search's time, as it has half its tries
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 3: getting past what stops it. T-1042's limit 2; from Boss's log of 15 Nov.)
- **Why now:** T-1012 gave the plain way (the best-paid button held, and the small changes to that) "at most half the budget" so that the changes to what the AI did always get their turn. The budget is counted in tries: 60 of 120. On the practice game a search makes its 120 tries in a second or so and the half holds. On Boss's game a try costs a quarter of a second and the 15 seconds a search may take (T-1008) are up after 58 to 67 tries: where the plain way loses the life, its changes take the first 60 and the changes to what the AI did get what is left, 2 to 7 tries a search. T-1042 lets each list carry on from search to search, which helps the plain way's list at 60 changes a search and the other at 2 to 7. Of the six ways past his log shows found, three were changes to what it did (on tries 51, 6 and 29).
- **Try-out (before the plan, in scratch worktrees, described as one):** the practice bench with the long pause, levels 0 to 23, 12 goes each, every search timed by its plays as if each cost a quarter of a second, so that 15 seconds are 60 plays as on Boss's game; T-1042's code. (a) As it is: 111 levels finished, 137 lives lost; of the searches after a life lost 304 found a way and 102 found none. (b) With no change to the plain way started once half the time has passed: **156 levels finished, 86 lives lost; 352 found a way and 66 found none.** (In T-1042's try-out 73 of 74 ways found by carrying on were changes to what it did.)
- **Objective:** in a search after a life lost that has a time limit, no change to the plain way is played once `PLAIN_SHARE` of the time has passed since the search began; the search then goes on to the changes to what it did, which have the time that is left. Half the tries stays the plain way's most as well.
- **Scope:** `training/search.py` (`find_way`), tests, documents. **Out of scope:** the searches where it stands still (there the plain way's changes are what finds a way on: in Boss's log all four ways on were such, and their list is tried first on purpose, T-1018); the plain way's own play and the look at it, which are one or two plays and tell where its list ends; how long a search may take; what T-1031 spends on finding where a loss was settled before the search begins.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. With no time limit a search is the search it was, play for play. Every existing test of the search passes unchanged.
  2. With a time limit, where the plain way loses the life: no change to it is started once half the time has passed, blind or under the screen; the changes to what it did are then played until the time is up or their tries are.
  3. Stopping the plain way's list for its time is not the search running out of time: a search that then gets through its other list in time is not `out_of_time`, and one that finds a way there has found it.
  4. Where the plain way's list stops for its time is said as where it stopped (T-1042), so the next search at the place carries on there.
  5. Half the tries is still the plain way's most where that comes first.
  6. A search at a standstill is as it was: the plain way's changes there may take the time they took.
  7. Measured on the practice levels with every search timed by its plays (the try-out's measure, with this code against main); the practice levels with the bench's own setting play as on main to the last figure (no search there runs out of time). Every new line broken on purpose and noticed. The whole suite passes, run alone.
- **Expected changes:** `src/retro_ai_lab/training/search.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_search_plain_time.py` (new), `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, this tracker.
- **Test plan (written before the code):** `test_search_plain_time.py`, with the plays scripted and a clock that moves a second with every play: with no time limit the plays of a search with a plain way are those of T-1012's rule (1); with 8 seconds, the plain way and three of its changes, then four changes to what it did, and the same search without the rule would have given the plain way all eight (2); a change to the plain way that stayed alive when its time ran out is not looked at, and is where the list stopped (2, 4); the other list gone through in time after the plain way's time was up is not out of time, and a way found there is the way (3); what `stopped_at` says, and a second search begun there (4); tries the smaller limit (5); a standstill with a time limit plays what it played (6). On the practice game's first gap with the real plays and the clock of the existing time tests: a plain way whose changes cannot get over, and the way found among the changes to what it did within a time in which, without the rule, it is not (2). Breaks in a scratch worktree (7), the practice levels both ways (7), the whole suite alone (7).
- **Changed while building:** (1) **Criterion 1's "every existing test of the search passes unchanged" was wrong.** Three merged assertions state the rule this task replaces, that under a time limit the plain way's changes may take the search whole: `test_search_plain_first.py::test_the_time_limit_holds_over_both_parts` ("what it did is not begun"), `test_search_carries_on.py::test_the_two_lists_are_carried_apart` (which plays a timed search made of and where each list stopped) and `test_search_at_a_loss.py::test_a_search_out_of_time_leaves_the_loss_standing` (4 tries in 6 seconds, now 3). They were left failing on the branch and Boss was asked once, on a card (15 Nov); he said yes on 16 Nov ("Yes, change those three") and each was rewritten to the new rule, as strict as it was. The task waited for that; T-1044 to T-1047 were built meanwhile and main was merged in before the last runs. (2) A ninth test, `test_the_half_is_of_the_time_not_of_the_plays`. (3) The list's own time is checked inside `may_play(until)`, so the clock is read once for a play's leave.

The built code gives the try-out's figures to the last number. **With the bench's own setting** (no search there runs out of time) the 48 levels play as on main to the last figure with both pauses: 424 levels finished and 159 lives lost with the long pause, 439 and 271 with the game's own. Whole suite, run alone after main was merged in: 2290 passed, 10 skipped.
- **Limits:** (1) **Not yet seen on a real game.** The measure above stands in for Boss's game by counting each play as a quarter of a second; what a play costs there varies. His next log shows it: a search that finds nothing should now say it made tries in both lists. (2) A search at a standstill is as it was: there the plain way's changes are what finds a way on, and they may take the time they took. (3) Half is `PLAIN_SHARE`, the same half as of the tries; no other share was measured. (4) The plain way's own play and the look at it are not counted against its half: they are one or two plays.
- **Commit:** see PR #289. **PR:** #289.
- **Completion report:** In a search after a life lost that has a time limit, no change to the plain way (the best-paid button held) is started once half the search's time has passed; the changes to what the AI did then have the rest, where on Boss's game they had 2 to 7 tries of about 60. That the plain way's list stopped for its time is not the search out of time, and where it stopped is carried to the next search (T-1042). With no time limit, and at a standstill, a search is the search it was. Three older assertions that stated the old rule were rewritten with Boss's word. **Next:** T-1048 (pressing on with buttons never paid), which waits for his word on two older tests.

### T-1042 – A search that found nothing carries on where it stopped
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 3: getting past what stops it. From Boss's log of 15 Nov, 17:53 to 18:49.)
- **Why now:** Boss ran the build with T-1038 and T-1039 for 21 goes. Both do what they were built for on his game: from go 50 it finishes the first level every go and is paid for the ground of the next, from go 56 the second too, and its score went from about +80 a go to about +1,800 (he confirms it reaches level 3). There it stalls. Goes 56 to 60 lose a life at one spot (steps 2,747, 2,677, 2,677, 2,654, 2,666; a second a little further on at 2,906, 2,851, 2,805), and each of the ten searches there "made 58 to 67 tries in 15 s, all the time a search may take: none got past". A search lists its changes most promising first (the shortest hold, 4 steps, from the loss backwards; then 8; then 16) and starts that list from the top every time, the plain way's changes first with up to half the tries. With some 60 tries of a list several times that long, every search at the spot made the same tries again, and changes held for 16 steps (a long jump) were never reached. Then T-1039's rest set in, as built.
- **Try-out (before the plan, in a scratch worktree, described as one):** the practice bench with the long pause, a search's tries cut from 120 to 30 so that a search cannot get through its lists (as on Boss's game), levels 0 to 23, 12 goes each. (1) **From the same state:** at each of the 113 searches after a life lost that found nothing, further searches were made from the very same saved moment, each beginning where the last stopped, and thrown away. 74 of the 113 (65%) found a way: 36 at the next search, 23 at the second, 8, 5 and 2 at the third to fifth; 39 found none in six. A search that starts from the top again finds nothing there, being the same search. 73 of the 74 ways were changes to what it did, one a change to the plain way. (2) **From one go to the next, first form:** the runner remembering, for the place, the number of changes each list had gone through, and the next search there skipping that many. No gain: 453 ways found against 451 without, and 76 levels finished against 92. The next go arrives a little differently (its saved moment lies up to 20 steps elsewhere), so the same number is another change in its list, and a search could skip just the stretch that mattered. (3) **Second form:** remembering instead the hold and how many steps before the last step a change may go at, which mean the same in any go's list. Searches at a place where one had found nothing before: 57 of 106 found a way (54%), against 39 of 96 (41%) without carrying on; in all 91 levels finished against 92, 144 lives lost against 154. (On the practice game the learner arrives differently each go, so even a search from the top is often another search; on Boss's game the life went at the very same step in consecutive goes.) (4) At the app's own 120 tries (first form, 48 levels): 6 of 48 runs differ from main, levels finished 423 and 423, lives lost 159 against 165.
- **Objective:** a search after a life lost that finds nothing reports where in its two lists it stopped; the runner remembers that for the place; the next search after a life lost at about that place begins there, comes round to the start of each list when it reaches the end, and stops where it began.
- **Scope:** `training/search.py` (`find_way(begin_at=…)`, `Search.stopped_at`), `training/episode.py` (what is remembered for a place, and the log line), tests, documents. **Out of scope:** the searches where it stands still (they keep starting from the top; their list goes forwards and their tries are twice as many; a later task if a log shows the same there); the plain way's share of a search's *time* (with 15 seconds and some 60 tries the plain way's changes take nearly all of every search and the changes to what it did get 2 to 7; that is the next task, T-1043); beginning with the change that got past at a place last time; keeping any of this from one runner to the next.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. With nothing to begin at, a search is the search it was: the same plays in the same order, the same way, the same tries. Every existing test of the search passes unchanged.
  2. A search that ran out of tries, or of time, says where in each list it stopped: which hold, and how many steps before the last step a change may be placed at. A search begun there plays none of the changes at the places the first one finished, goes on with the rest, and finds the way a search with tries enough for the whole list finds.
  3. At the end of a list it comes round to the start, and stops where it began: no change is played twice in one search, and a search that went through a whole list for nothing says it stopped where it began.
  4. The plain way's list and the list of changes to what it did are carried apart: each begins where its own stopped.
  5. The runner: a search after a life lost that found nothing is remembered for the place (which place of the go the saved moment was in, and where in it); the next search after a life lost whose moment is in the same place and within half a screen begins there, and what it says replaces what was remembered. A search elsewhere begins from the top and is remembered apart. A way found changes nothing remembered. The searches where it stands still begin from the top and remember nothing. At most 32 places are remembered, the oldest forgotten first.
  6. The log says when a search carries on, in plain words, and the lines there were stay as they are.
  7. Through the real services on the practice game, with searches too short to find the way over the first gap in one: the first go's search finds nothing, a later go's search at the gap carries on and finds the way; with nothing carried (broken on purpose) the same goes find none.
  8. Measured on the practice levels against main: at the app's own tries, 48 levels with both pauses, finished and lives lost stated; with tries cut to 30, what searches at a place searched before come to, with and without. Every new line broken on purpose and noticed. The whole suite passes, run alone.
- **Expected changes:** `src/retro_ai_lab/training/search.py`, `src/retro_ai_lab/training/episode.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_search_carries_on.py` (new), `tests/unit/training/test_going_back_carries_on.py` (new), `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, this tracker.
- **Test plan (written before the code):** `test_search_carries_on.py` on the practice game's first gap, with every play's moves noted: nothing to begin at is the search as it was, play for play (1); a search three tries short of the way finds nothing and says where it stopped, and one begun there finds the same way in fewer tries than from the top, playing none of the changes of the places the first finished (2); a search begun past the way comes round to it, plays no moves twice, and one with no way in its list stops where it began (3); with a plain way, both lists carried apart, and time running out carried like tries (2, 4); what is refused: a place to begin that is no pair of pairs of whole numbers from 0, and one given to a search at a standstill (5). `test_going_back_carries_on.py` with the search scripted, on the `Lab` of the going-back tests: what the runner hands each search and what it remembers, at one place, at two, in another place of the go, after a way found, at a standstill, with more places than it keeps, and the log (5, 6); and with the real search made short, over goes (7). Breaks in a scratch worktree (8), the practice levels (8), the whole suite alone (8).
- **Changed while building:** (1) **A place is told by where the life was seen lost, not by the saved moment** (criterion 5 said the moment). The first tests on the practice game showed the moment will not do: a go's first moment is taken before the watch has looked at a screen; after a life lost in a game that puts the player back at once the next moment is taken where the life went, not where the player then is; and moments lie up to 20 steps apart from go to go. With the moment, the first gap a life down (camera 136 and where it stood) and the next place a life goes at (camera 97, a moment taken just over the gap) came out 39 pixels apart and were taken for one place. So the runner asks the go's own watch, when the life has just been seen lost and before anything goes back, which place of the go it is in and where in it (`Ground.place`, the camera's travel on a screen that scrolls): 136 or 137 pixels at the first gap on every life of every go, 329 and 553 at the next two places. The try-out's figures were measured with the moment; criterion 8's are with this. (2) The names: `find_way(begin_at=…)`, `Search.stopped_at`, `TOP`, `Spot`, `MOST_SOUGHT`. (3) A search cut off between the two changes at one place begins that place again: one play is made twice (a place in the list is the hold and the steps, not the move). (4) Tests beyond the plan: a place to begin means the same change in a longer trace, where a count of changes means another (`test_a_place_in_the_list_means_the_same_in_another_go`); a search that stopped at the top is begun there with nothing said, and counted all the same; the place not searched for longest is the one forgotten; where the life went on the practice game, to the pixel, and the place of the go as the watch has it. (5) What "about here" means is tested with the places scripted (`_lost_where` replaced): the practice game through the `Lab` has one place and no two losses between half and a whole screen apart.
- **Results:** 19 new tests pass (8 of the search, 11 of the runner); the 61 existing tests of the search and of going back pass unchanged. **Broken on purpose** in a scratch worktree: 85 breaks, **84 noticed**. One changes nothing a search can do and is not counted (coming round the list and then going through its later part once more: every change of that part has been played and is passed over). One was missed at first (the place of the go always taken for the first) and got a test of its own. **The practice levels at the app's own 120 tries** (48 levels, 12 goes each, against main): with the long pause 424 levels finished against 423, 159 lives lost against 165, 123 searches after a life lost for nothing against 127, 7 of 48 runs differ; with the game's own pause 439 against 443, 271 against 273, 129 against 133, 11 runs differ. Of the searches that carried on, 70 of 98 and 109 of 149 found a way. No run rests or stops going back, as on main. At 120 tries a search on the practice game gets through most of its lists, so there is little to carry on: this shows no harm, not the gain. **With searches cut to 30 tries** (as short of their lists as Boss's 60 in 15 seconds are; long pause, levels 0 to 23, the same code with and without what is carried): searches at a place searched for nothing before found a way 96 times of 148 (65%) carrying on, against 61 of 118 (52%) from the top each time; in all 96 levels finished against 92, 142 lives lost against 154, and 91 of 288 goes finished a level against 83. Whole suite, run alone: 2,234 passed, 10 skipped (2,215 and 10 on main).
- **Limits:** (1) **Not yet seen on a real game.** In Boss's log this is what would have had the second search at the spot go on from the first; whether a change in the rest of the lists gets past that spot is not known until he runs it. (2) **The plain way's changes still take nearly all of a search that runs out of time.** The plain way may use half a search's *tries* (60 of 120), and on Boss's game 15 seconds are about 60 tries: the plain way's list is carried on at some 60 changes a search and the list of changes to what it did at 2 to 7. In the try-out 73 of 74 ways found by carrying on were changes to what it did. The plain way's share of the time is the next task (T-1043). (3) A place is where the watch was when the life was seen lost. Where a game has already shown another screen by then, every loss in that place of the go is "at its door" and shares what is remembered; the searches there then go round one list between them, which costs order and nothing else. The camera's first moves in a new place not being measured (T-1041's finding, 73 pixels on the practice game) is within the half screen allowed. (4) Carrying on goes by place in the list, not by what was played: a go that arrives differently plays other moves at the same place in the list, and what it skips there was tried on another trace. Coming round the list makes up for it in time. (5) The searches where it stands still start from the top each time, as before. (6) A way found does not move where the next search at the place begins: it begins where the last search for nothing stopped, which is before the way in the list or past it. Beginning with the change that got past last time is left for a later task. (7) Nothing of this is kept from one runner to the next (a new connection, a forgotten brain, another kind of brain), like the rests of T-1039.
- **Commit:** see PR #284. **PR:** #284.
- **Completion report:** A search after a life lost that finds nothing now says where in its two lists it stopped (the hold, and the steps before the last step a change may be placed at), the runner remembers that for the place the life went at (the place of the go and the camera's travel there, within half a screen), and the next search there begins with the changes the last one did not get to, comes round each list at its end and stops where it began. The log says when a search carries on. With nothing remembered a search is play for play the search it was. **Next:** T-1043, the plain way's share of a search's time, so that on a real game the changes to what it did get their half of every search; then Boss's two asks of 15 Nov (a go that lasts until game over, chosen in the panel; a countdown while a go has a time limit).

### T-1041 – A new level is new ground, shown from end to end on the practice game
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 3; a test task: no code of the app changes. The second of two: T-1040 gave the practice game its levels.)
- **Why now:** T-1038's limit 1: "Not yet seen on a real game... the new-level case is tested with scripted screens only." Boss has the build and may run it at any time; what the eyes, the tracker and the runner make of a real change of level together should be known here first, and held by a test so it stays so.
- **Try-out (before the plan, in a scratch test, described as one):** the real services on a practice cartridge of two levels (seed 0), a player who knows the levels, a watch, no searches. (1) The first level: 144 steps of new ground counted to its flag. Two looks after the flag the watch is in a new place (place 2 of the go), says so once, and has counted nothing for the cut. The second level then counts 134 steps of new ground to its own flag. At that flag the game goes on to the first level again: two looks later the watch is back in its first place, and 80 steps of walking there count nothing. So T-1038 does on the practice game what it was built to do. (2) **Found:** in the second level the camera's first 80 pixels of travel are not measured (the tracker reads "no move" for 11 steps while the screen scrolls 8 pixels a step), and its furthest there ends 157 pixels short of the game's. The same happens with that level drawn in the first level's colours, so it is the layout and not the colours: that level opens on plain ground with one 16-pixel wall in sight, where the first opens with a three-tile gap in sight. Under-paid, not over-paid; not this task's to mend. (3) **Found:** with the second level drawn in the first's colours the flag is not seen as a cut at all: the watch stays in its one place with its camera where it was, and counts the next level's ground on from there. That pays the new level (good) and pays the first level a second time when it comes round (as the one-level game always has). It is the case T-1038's limit 3 describes, seen now.
- **Objective:** an integration test on the practice game through the real services (`ConnectionService`, `ObservationService`, `DiscoveryService`, `RewardService`, `EpisodeRunner`, `ScreenWatch`), with a two-level cartridge and a player who knows the levels, that holds what the try-out saw.
- **Scope:** tests and the documents. **Out of scope:** the practice bench on more than one level (its camera and ground figures compare the watch with one level's own camera, and need rethinking for a go that changes level; a later task); the camera's travel not measured on a sparse screen (try-out 2; a later task); levels that look alike (try-out 3).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. To the first flag the watch is in one place and counts the first level's ground.
  2. Within 4 steps after the flag it is in a second place, with nothing counted for the cut and nothing reached there yet, and the log has said "takes it for a new place (number 2 of this go)" once.
  3. The second level's ground is counted as new: more than 100 steps of it by its flag, with no life lost, and the go is paid for them.
  4. When the first level comes round the watch is in its first place again within 4 steps, a third place is not made, and walking there counts nothing.
  5. A life lost in the second level puts the player back at its start, and the watch takes that for the same place: no new place, nothing counted on the way back to where it had been, and counting again past it.
  6. The test fails when T-1038's rule is broken: with a new place never taken up, with a place known again taken for a new one, and with the game's putting back after a life lost taken for a new place (broken on purpose in a scratch worktree). Every existing test passes unchanged.
- **Expected changes:** `tests/integration/test_a_new_level_end_to_end.py` (new), `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, this tracker (and T-1038's limit 1 is answered here).
- **Test plan:** written before the test. `test_the_second_level_is_a_new_place_and_the_first_is_known_again` (1, 2, 3, 4), `test_a_life_lost_in_the_second_level_is_the_same_place` (5). Then three breaks of T-1038's rule in a scratch worktree (6), and the whole suite alone.
- **Changed while building:** (1) Criterion 5's "nothing counted on the way back to where it had been" is held in the watch's own terms: nothing is counted while the game's camera is short of the furthest the watch had counted in that place. As first written (nothing counted until the player is back at the gap) it failed, and rightly: on first arriving the watch had counted 73 pixels short of the game's camera (try-out 2), and after the life lost it measured the camera from the start, so it counted the ground it had missed the first time. (2) Criterion 6 named three breaks; eleven were tried, and the third as named (the game's putting back after a life lost not known as that) is **not** noticed by this test: on this game the player is put back at the level's start, which is the screen at that place's door, so the place is known again by its door with the other rule gone. The break of that step this test does notice is "being put back after a life lost does not put it at the door". The criterion stands as amended here; the rule itself is held by T-1038's unit tests.
- **Results:** 2 new tests pass (16 seconds together), on the practice game through the real services. **What they hold (seed 0, two levels):** to the first flag one place, more than 130 steps of ground counted and the camera past 2,200 pixels; four steps after the flag the watch is in place 2 of 2 with nothing counted for the cut and nothing reached there, and the log line said once; by the second flag more than 100 steps of the second level's ground counted (134 in the try-out), no life lost, and the go paid at least a point for each; four steps after that flag the watch is in its first place again with what it had reached there, no third place, and 120 steps of walking there count nothing; a life lost in the second level leaves it in the same place of 2, counts nothing until the game's camera is back at what it had counted there, and counts on past it. **T-1038's limit 1 ("not yet seen on a real game... tested with scripted screens only") is answered for the practice game; Boss's game is still to be seen.** Breaks of T-1038's rule in a scratch worktree, this test alone run against each: **6 of 11 noticed** (a new place never taken up; a place it has been in never known again; every screen taken for a place it knows; a new place keeping what was reached before it; being put back after a life lost not putting it at the door; a place known again not gone to). The 5 not noticed are each a line whose job a second line also does on this path: the cut's own putting at the door and the arrival's (three breaks), and the rule for the game's putting back and the door's screen (two). Each of those lines is held by T-1038's unit tests (122 breaks, all noticed there). Whole suite, run alone: 2,215 passed, 10 skipped (2,213 and 10 on main).

(2) **Open, from the try-out:** right after arriving in a new place the camera's first moves are not measured (11 steps, 73 pixels on this level), so that much of a new level's ground goes unpaid. Why is not known yet; after a life lost in the same level the same stretch is measured. **Answered in T-1047:** this test's player never stands still, so the watch had not found the game's own count of its camera; with the count found the stretch is measured. (3) **Open, from the try-out:** a next level that looks just like the last (same colours, plain ground at both ends) is no cut to the tracker: the watch stays in one place and its camera carries on. *Answered by T-1049: tried out, that is harmless (the second level's ground is counted once either way); what was not harmless, ground paid twice after a life lost on plain ground, is mended there.* (4) The practice bench does not take `levels` yet: its camera and ground figures compare the watch with one level's own camera.
