### T-1040 – The practice game can have more than one level
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 3; a practice-game task: nothing the app does changes. The first of two: this one gives the game its levels, the next plays the app on them.)
- **Why now:** T-1038 and T-1039 are what stood between Boss's game and its second level, and neither has been seen at work on a game: Toy Hopper's flag adds one to its level counter and puts the player back at the start of the same level, so the practice game has no "next level" to arrive in. T-1038's limit 1 says so. Boss's stated proof is a first level finished "and then the same on a second game"; before he has to find out on his own machine whether a new level is taken for one, the practice game should be able to show it. This task is the game's half of that.
- **Objective:** `ToyHopper.levels`: how many levels the cartridge holds, a whole number from 1 (as it was, and the default) to `MOST_LEVELS` (8). It is the cartridge's, like `dying_frames`: a reset keeps it. The level being played is the level counter modulo `levels`: at the flag the counter goes up as it did, and the player is at the start of the next level; after the last comes the first again. Level n of a cartridge with seed s is laid out as the practice level of seed s + n (so each is one of the levels known to be finishable), and is drawn in the colours of `PALETTES[n % 3]`: the backdrop, the ground, its top and the walls differ from level to level, as a real game's levels do; the player, the walkers, the coins, the flag and the strip along the top keep theirs. `gaps`, `walls`, `walkers` and `coins` tell of the level being played. A life lost starts the level it was lost on again; game over and Start begin at the first. A snapshot brings back the level it was made on.
- **Scope:** `emulator/fake/toy_hopper.py`, its tests, the documents. **Out of scope:** the bench and the app playing on more than one level, and T-1038 shown from end to end (the next task); a levels count kept in the game's memory (it is the cartridge's: a snapshot made with one count and loaded with another plays the level its counter says under the new count); Toy Racer.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. With `levels` 1, said or not, the game is the game it was: the same memory and the same screen, frame for frame, over a long scripted play that passes the flag. Every existing test of the game passes unchanged.
  2. With `levels` 2, at the flag: the score and the level counter go up, lives and score are kept, the player is at the start, and the level is the next one: `gaps`, `walls`, `walkers` and `coins` are those of the practice level of the next seed, the walkers in memory and the coins are its own, and the screen is drawn in the second palette.
  3. After the last level comes the first again, with its layout and colours; with three levels all three differ.
  4. A life lost on the second level starts the second level again. Game over and Start begin at the first level.
  5. Every level of a cartridge can be finished in turn without losing a life (several seeds, three levels each).
  6. A snapshot made on the second level and loaded later, on whichever level the game then is, brings back that level: what is played from there is what was played the first time, frame for frame, and the screen is its own.
  7. Each palette's colours are apart from each other and from the colours of the player, the walkers, the coins and the flag, which are the same on every level.
  8. `levels` is refused, with a plain message and the game unchanged, when it is 0, 9, a fraction, a word or true; a reset keeps it.
- **Expected changes:** `src/retro_ai_lab/emulator/fake/toy_hopper.py`, `tests/unit/emulator/fake/test_toy_hopper_levels.py` (new), `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, this tracker.
- **Test plan:** written before the task's code. `tests/unit/emulator/fake/test_toy_hopper_levels.py`: `test_one_level_is_the_game_it_was` (1), `test_the_flag_leads_to_the_next_level` (2), `test_after_the_last_level_comes_the_first` (3), `test_a_life_lost_starts_the_level_it_was_lost_on` (4), `test_every_level_of_a_cartridge_can_be_finished` (5), `test_a_snapshot_brings_back_its_level` (6), `test_each_level_has_colours_of_its_own` (7), `test_levels_that_are_no_count_are_refused` (8). Then every new line broken on purpose in a scratch worktree, and the whole suite alone.
- **Changed while building:** (1) `README.md` is not changed: nothing a person runs takes `levels` yet (the practice tool does with the next task, and the README says so then). (2) Criterion 1's "the game it was" is held by a number: the test keeps a hash of a long scripted play (memory at every frame, the screen at every sixtieth, through the flag and 200 frames on, and the saved game at the end) worked out on the code before this task, and the game with one level, said or not, must come to it. (3) The comparison of criterion 2 is played two ways: as one who knows the level plays it, in step with the practice level of the next seed up to that level's own flag (the varied presses of the other tests never get past its first gap, so they met no walker), and then with varied presses that fall in. (4) Added to the plan's tests: the walkers in memory at the very frame the flag is passed are the new level's (a break that took up the level after writing them showed nothing held it), and which palette is the second level's.
- **Results:** 8 new tests pass and the 10 existing tests of the game pass unchanged. Every new line was broken on purpose in a scratch worktree: 42 of 44 breaks were noticed at first; one of the other two was a break that changed nothing as written (it took up the level twice, not later) and was written again, and one (the second and third palettes changing places) got an assertion; **44 breaks, all noticed**. On the practice bench, which does not say `levels`, levels 3 and 11 with the long pause and 4 and 24 with the game's own give main's figures to the last number. Whole suite, run alone: 2,213 passed, 10 skipped (2,205 and 10 on main).
- **Limits:** (1) Nothing uses it yet: the bench, the app and T-1038 shown from end to end are the next task. (2) The count is the cartridge's and not in the game's memory, so a snapshot made under one count and loaded under another plays the level its counter says under the new count. (3) Level n is the practice level of seed + n: a cartridge's second level is another cartridge's first. That keeps every level one known to be finishable; it also means two neighbouring cartridges share a level. (4) Three palettes: with more than three levels the fourth is drawn in the first's colours, and where it also opens on plain ground the AI's eyes may take it for the first (T-1038's limit 3), as they would in a real game whose levels look alike. (5) Toy Racer has no levels.
- **Commit:** see PR #282. **PR:** #282.
- **Completion report:** `ToyHopper.levels` (1 to 8, 1 unless told) makes the practice game's flag lead to the next level: the practice level of the next seed, drawn in a palette of its own, the first again after the last. A life lost starts the level it was lost on, game over starts at the first, and a snapshot brings back its level. With one level the game is what it was, frame for frame. **Next:** T-1041, the bench takes `--levels` and the app is played on a two-level cartridge to its second level, to see T-1038 take it for a new place and pay for its ground, with the real services.

### T-1039 – Going back rests where it has worked, and does not stop for good
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 3, the AI smarter; the second of the two things that stopped Boss's game after its first level.)
- **Why now:** In Boss's log of 15 Nov going back after a life lost found no way past in goes 3 to 7 (6 searches, never 8 in a row), found one 9 times in goes 8 to 10, and then found none 8 times in a row in goes 11 to 14, all at the start of the second level, where until T-1038 no ground was new and so no try could be told to have got past. At the eighth the runner stopped going back "in this game: here it only costs time" (T-1009), and the 24 goes that followed each lost their lives with no search made. T-1009's rule is for a game where going back cannot work (the racing practice game: nothing the eyes count tells a way past). A game where it found 9 ways in 3 goes is not that game: there, 8 in a row for nothing says something about the place it is at, and it will be at other places. T-1038 removes the cause of those 8; this removes the rule that made them final.
- **Objective:** `EpisodeRunner`: where `give_up_after` searches after a life lost in a row have found nothing, (1) a runner none of whose such searches ever found a way stops going back for good, with the log line it had, as before; (2) a runner one of whose searches after a life lost has found a way rests: the rest of that go and the next `REST_GOES` (4) goes make no search and save no moment, `gave_up` is true meanwhile, and the go after those goes back again with the count of searches for nothing started again, saying so once in the log; (3) each rest that follows another with no way found between them is twice as long, up to `MOST_REST` (32) goes, and a way found makes the next rest `REST_GOES` again. A way on found where it stood still (T-1018) is not a way past a life lost and does not count for this.
- **Scope:** `training/episode.py`, tests, the documents. **Out of scope:** the searches where it stands still, which keep their own count and still stop for good (their existing test holds the wording of that with a way found before it, and in Boss's game none of 16 found a way); giving up place by place; keeping any of this from one runner to the next (a new connection, a forgotten brain or a move to a neural network still starts afresh).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. A runner whose searches after a life lost never found a way: at `give_up_after` in a row for nothing it has `gave_up` and never searches again, however many goes follow, and says the line it said. The existing tests of giving up pass unchanged.
  2. A runner that found a way before: at `give_up_after` in a row for nothing it has `gave_up`; the rest of that go and the next 4 goes make no search, no save and no load; the fifth go after it has `gave_up` false and searches.
  3. After a rest the count starts again: it takes `give_up_after` more searches for nothing in a row to rest again, not one.
  4. A second rest with no way found since the first lasts 8 goes, a third 16, and none more than 32. A way found between two rests makes the next one 4 again.
  5. A way on found at a standstill does not make a runner one that "found a way before": it still stops for good. The count and the stopping of the searches at a standstill are as they were.
  6. The log says, once each time, in plain words: that it leaves going back for so many goes and why, and that it goes back again.
  7. On the practice game the bench's figures are those of main to the last number on the levels compared, with both pauses (no run of the baseline, 192 of them, gives up going back after a life lost at all), and every existing test passes with no assertion changed.
- **Expected changes:** `src/retro_ai_lab/training/episode.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_going_back_rests.py` (new), `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, this tracker.
- **Test plan:** written before the task's code. `tests/unit/training/test_going_back_rests.py`, on the practice game through the real services with the search's outcome scripted as in `test_a_way_found_starts_the_count_again`: `test_it_rests_where_going_back_has_worked` (2, 6), `test_the_count_starts_again_after_a_rest` (3), `test_each_rest_for_nothing_is_twice_as_long` (4), `test_a_way_found_makes_the_next_rest_short_again` (4), `test_where_it_never_worked_it_stops_for_good` (1), `test_a_way_on_at_a_standstill_does_not_count` (5). Then every new line broken on purpose in a scratch worktree, practice levels with both pauses against main (7), and the whole suite alone (7).
- **Changed while building:** (1) One test beyond the plan: `test_one_for_nothing_where_one_is_enough` (with `give_up_after=1` a rest follows one search for nothing, the next rest is 8 goes, and the log says "1 time"). (2) Each go of the new tests loses two lives, not one. The tests put the practice game back to its start between goes with nobody told, so with one life a go the life count goes up as often as down, and after nine goes the understanding engine drops it as no life count ("a life count does not bounce"); from then on nothing is watched and no search is made, whatever the runner would do. With two lives a go it goes down twice for each time up and is kept. (3) `test_each_rest_for_nothing_is_twice_as_long` runs with the most set to 16 goes (rests of 4, 8, 16, 16, 16), which keeps it to 60 goes where 32 would take 140; the first test holds that the app's most is 32. (4) The first test's go may search twice (`ways_per_go=2`), to show that what is left of the go in which it gives up makes no search although one is left to it.
- **Results:** 7 new tests pass, and the existing tests of giving up (`test_search_at_a_loss.py`, `test_standing_still.py`, `test_pressing_on.py`, `test_restart_with_a_life_lost.py`) pass with nothing changed. Every new line was broken on purpose in a scratch worktree: **40 breaks, all noticed**. Three more that were written changed nothing a runner can do and are not counted: the starting values of `_rest` and `_rest_next`, which are always set again (by a way found, and by the search at which it gives up) before they are read. **The practice game (criterion 7):** in the baseline's 192 runs (48 levels, both pauses, dice 0 and 1000) not one gives up going back after a life lost, so this task's lines are never reached there; played to be sure, levels 2, 7, 20 and 33 with the long pause and 15, 21, 31 and 46 with the game's own give the figures of main to the last number, and no run rests or stops. Whole suite, run alone: 2,205 passed, 10 skipped (2,198 and 10 on main).
- **Limits:** (1) **Not yet seen on a real game.** In Boss's log this is the rule that would have had the AI go back again from go 19; whether it then finds ways depends on T-1038, and his next run shows both. (2) A rest goes by goes, not by places: after it the AI may arrive at the same place by the same way and search for nothing again (T-1029 moves where its own play starts from, which helps). The rest doubling bounds what that costs: at most `give_up_after` searches for every 32 goes left alone. (3) The searches where it stands still keep T-1018's rule and still stop for good after 8 in a row for nothing, even after one found a way on. In Boss's log none of 16 found one. (4) Nothing of this is kept from one runner to the next: a new connection, a forgotten brain or a move to a neural network starts afresh, as before. (5) Seen while testing and not looked into here: a life count that has gone up four times or more and down fewer than twice as often is dropped by the understanding engine (T-864). In the tests that came from putting the game back by hand; whether a game whose every go costs exactly one life can look the same in the app is a question for a later task.
- **Commit:** see PR #281. **PR:** #281.
- **Completion report:** A runner whose searches after a life lost have found a way in this game no longer stops going back for good at `give_up_after` searches in a row for nothing: it leaves going back alone for 4 goes and takes it up again, twice as long each time that comes to nothing again (8, 16, at most 32), and 4 again after a way found. Where no search ever found a way it stops for good as before. The log says each. The practice game plays as it did. **Next:** Boss's run of the build with T-1038 and this; then the remedy for levels that never finish (T-1037's try-out 4), measured on three sets of dice.

### T-1038 – A new level or room is new ground
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 3, the AI smarter; what stood between Boss's game and its second level.)
- **Why now:** Boss started a fresh brain on the build with T-1031 to T-1036 and sent the log (15 Nov, 38 goes of Super Mario Bros.). Go 1 scored -187 points and go 10 +966; going back after a life lost found a way past 9 times, where on the build before it found none in 8. From go 10 on "Getting somewhere new" is paid 195 to 200 times a go, which at the player's 16 pixels a step is the 3,136 pixels the camera can travel in level 1-1, and the score goes up some 60 times while the AI stands still at the end, as it does at the flagpole: the go covers the whole first level, and the way it remembers (1,210 steps) loses no life. Then nothing more: from go 11 a life goes at about step 1,450, 8 searches in a row find no way past, the AI stops going back for good (T-1009's rule), and the last 24 goes all score about 1,000. The cause is in `observation/ground.py`'s own words: after a cut to another place "a new room pays only once it is as far from its door as the go's furthest. That under-pays a new room". The next level is such a room, 3,136 pixels long before anything in it is new. So "Getting somewhere new" pays nothing there, and since a try only counts as past a death when it reaches two steps of new ground (T-1001), no search there can succeed, whatever it tries.
- **Boss's word:** one merged test holds the old rule (`test_a_cut_puts_it_back_where_the_go_began`: through a door, nothing pays until further from the door than the go's furthest). Asked on a card on 15 Nov, "Change one old rule so a new level counts as new ground?", Boss chose "Yes, change that rule". That one test's last assertion is rewritten to the new rule; no other existing assertion changes.
- **Objective:** (1) `Ground` keeps the ground of a go place by place: `new_place()` (somewhere it has not been this go: at its door, nothing reached there), `go_to(number)` (at the door of a place it has been in: what it reached there stays reached), `back()` as before (the door of the place it is in), `place_number`, `places`; `steps` is the count over all places; a kept moment says which place it was in and how far the go's story had got in each, and putting back returns to that place. (2) `observation/places.py` `same_view(a, b)`: whether two screens show the same spot, allowing for a camera move. (3) `ScreenWatch`: a cut (a quarter of the screen or more that no camera move explains) still puts it at a door at once and pays nothing; at the first look after that the screen can be measured against the one before, the watch settles where it is: within `RESPAWN_LOOKS` (60) of a life lost it is the game putting it back, the same place as now; the same view as before the cut is the same place (a flash); the view at the door of a place it has been in this go is that place again; anything else is a new place, and the screen is kept as its door. A life lost within `BACK_LOOKS` of taking up a place undoes it. At most `MOST_PLACES` (16) places a go; past that a cut is the old rule. One log line for each new place, from the go itself and not from its tries.
- **Scope:** `observation/ground.py`, `observation/places.py` (new), `training/vision.py`, tests, the documents. **Out of scope:** giving up going back for good after 8 searches for nothing (next task); a second, different level in the practice game to measure this on (a later task: the practice game's flag puts the player back at the start of the same level, which is the same place and must stay unpaid); keeping the camera's travel across a flash; places kept from go to go.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. `Ground`: in a new place the first step from the door pays, in every direction, whatever was reached elsewhere; back in a place it has been in, only past what it reached there; `back()` is unchanged; `steps` counts all places; a new go has one place and nothing reached.
  2. `Ground` kept and put back: a moment kept in one place and put back from another returns to the first, at the spot kept; ground of both walked again pays nothing; the story's reach in each place is what it was at that moment and nothing in a place taken up later, so `again` says what a go played straight would be paid; a copy is its own.
  3. `same_view`: the same screen, and one the camera moved over by up to its reach, are the same view; another room, and a blank screen, are not; screens of different sizes and nonsense are refused.
  4. Through a door to somewhere new with no life lost: nothing is paid at the cut, and from the next look each step from the door pays (the rewritten assertion of the existing test). Back out through the door: nothing is paid on either side for ground walked before, however often it goes in and out.
  5. A cut within 60 looks after a life lost is the game putting it back: the same place, and its ground pays nothing again. The existing tests of a life lost with a jump of the screen, a hit and a crash pass unchanged.
  6. A flash (a cut that comes back to the view before it, moved or not) starts no new place and pays nothing twice. Several cuts in a row (a fade, a card between levels) make one arrival, settled at the first look that can be measured.
  7. A life lost within `BACK_LOOKS` after a place was taken up puts it back in the place before, at its door. No more than `MOST_PLACES` places are made in a go.
  8. A moment marked before a door and gone back to after it: the watch is in the place before the door again; through the door again it is the same new place and pays nothing twice. A try's watch (`trial`) settles a door as the go would, counts the new ground behind it, and changes nothing in the go's watch.
  9. On the practice game with the real services, where the flag puts the player back at the start of the same level: the figures of the bench are those of main, to the last number, on the levels compared, with both pauses.
  10. Every other existing test passes with no assertion changed.
- **Expected changes:** `src/retro_ai_lab/observation/ground.py`, `src/retro_ai_lab/observation/places.py`, `src/retro_ai_lab/observation/__init__.py`, `src/retro_ai_lab/training/vision.py`, `tests/unit/observation/test_ground_places.py`, `tests/unit/observation/test_places.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_vision_places.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_vision.py` (the one assertion), `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, this tracker.
- **Test plan:** written before the task's code. `tests/unit/observation/test_ground_places.py`: `test_a_new_place_pays_from_its_door` (1), `test_a_place_it_has_been_in_pays_only_past_what_it_reached_there` (1), `test_back_is_the_door_of_the_place_it_is_in` (1), `test_a_new_go_has_one_place` (1), `test_put_back_returns_to_the_place_kept` (2), `test_the_story_of_each_place_goes_back` (2), `test_a_copy_keeps_its_places_to_itself` (2), `test_nonsense_is_refused` (1, 2). `tests/unit/observation/test_places.py`: `test_the_same_screen_is_the_same_view`, `test_a_view_the_camera_moved_over_is_the_same`, `test_another_room_is_another_view`, `test_nonsense_is_refused` (3). `tests/unit/training/test_vision_places.py`: `test_in_and_out_of_a_door_pays_each_side_once` (4), `test_a_cut_after_a_life_lost_is_the_same_place` (5), `test_a_flash_is_no_new_place` (6), `test_a_fade_is_one_arrival` (6), `test_a_life_lost_just_after_undoes_the_place` (7), `test_no_more_places_than_the_most` (7), `test_gone_back_to_before_the_door` (8), `test_a_try_settles_a_door_as_the_go_would` (8), `test_a_new_place_is_said_once` (objective 3). The existing `test_a_cut_puts_it_back_where_the_go_began` with its last assertion rewritten (4). Then every new line broken on purpose in a scratch worktree, the practice levels with both pauses against main (9), and the whole suite alone (10).

Boss's log of 15 Nov showed a harder stop on his own game, so this task came first and the remedy waits. (2) The rewritten test is renamed with its rule: `test_a_cut_puts_it_back_where_the_go_began` is now `test_a_cut_to_somewhere_new_pays_from_its_door`, and besides the last assertion (`[1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1]` for `[0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1]`) it says which place it is in, what was reached there and the count over both places. Its other assertions are as they were. (3) A place is known again by two screens, not one: the screen at its door and the screen it was last left by. Out of a door the player comes back where they left, which is seldom where they first came in. (4) The place it is in is asked first, so a flash stays where it is whatever other place looks like it. (5) `same_view` takes the share of what is drawn (what is not the backdrop on either screen) that differs, where the plan said only "allowing for a camera move": two rooms with the same plain backdrop would pass a count over the whole screen. (6) Tests added beyond the plan for what the deliberate breaks showed untested: `test_a_moment_written_by_hand`, `test_a_cut_right_after_a_life_lost`, `test_a_card_between_two_levels_is_a_place_of_its_own`, `test_a_new_go_knows_no_places`, `test_a_new_go_forgets_what_was_under_way`, `test_a_moment_kept_in_another_go`, `test_a_screen_of_another_size_is_never_a_place_it_knows`, `test_a_place_is_known_by_the_view_it_was_left_by`, `test_the_place_it_is_in_is_asked_first`, `test_what_was_undone_is_forgotten`, `test_a_try_keeps_what_it_learns_of_places_to_itself`, `test_a_life_lost_just_after_a_place_known_again`, `test_an_undone_place_is_undone_once`, `test_a_flash_and_then_a_hit`. (7) Lines that did a job a second time were found by the breaks and removed, not tested.
- **Results:** 41 new tests pass (9 of the ground, 4 of the view, 28 of the watch), and the one rewritten. Every new line was broken on purpose in a scratch worktree: 114 of 125 breaks were noticed at first; 4 of the other 11 were lines doing a job twice and were removed, 7 got tests; **on the code as it stands, 122 breaks and all noticed**. **The practice game (criterion 9):** levels 0 to 15 with the long pause and with the game's own, 12 goes of 300 steps, against main: levels finished, goes that finished, lives lost, deaths, searches, ways found and the standing-still figures are the same to the last number on all 32 runs (long pause per level 10 10 11 8 13 0 10 14 12 7 12 9 10 9 11 6, the game's own 13 8 11 12 11 4 7 12 13 0 13 9 11 12 9 3), and no new place was logged on any of them: the flag puts the player back at the start of the same level and the watch takes it for the place it is. Eight of those runs were played again on the final code after the last lines were removed, with the same figures. Whole suite, run alone: 2,198 passed, 10 skipped (2,157 and 10 on main).
- **Limits:** (1) **Not yet seen on a real game.** The practice game has no second level, so the new-level case is tested with scripted screens only. Whether Boss's game gets past the start of its second level is known when he runs this build. (2) A place is known again by two screens only. Left by one way and come back to by another, at a spot that looks like neither, it is taken for a new place and its ground pays a second time. (3) A new place whose first screen looks like the door of an earlier one is taken for that one and paid as before this task. (4) A level change within 60 looks after a life lost is taken for the game putting it back, and pays as before this task. (5) A fade is settled at the first look that can be measured against the one before, which may be half-way through it. (6) The camera's travel is not kept across a flash: after one, the place's ground is counted from its door again and pays nothing until past what was reached. (7) The tracker does not see a cut between a black card and a dark room; that is the tracker's and not this task's. (8) Places are a go's own: nothing of them is kept from go to go. ### T-1037 – The bench can throw other dice
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 3, the AI smarter. A measuring task: nothing the app does changes.)
- **Why now:** T-1036's next step was to be asking over a shorter stretch, and then the levels that never finish. Both were tried out first (below), and the try-outs showed that the measuring itself is not to be trusted yet: the bench gives the learner the level's number as the seed of its dice, so every build has been measured on one set of dice for each level, and the tasks since T-1015 were chosen and judged on those.
- **Try-outs (before the plan, on scratch copies of main, described as such):**
  1. *Asking over a shorter stretch (T-1036's limit 1).* `rose_anyway` held the other moves for the last 4 steps only. The clock was then called "earned" at 2 of 18 askings with the long pause and 6 of 22 with the short one (29 of 74 and 63 of 118 on main). But on 8 levels with the game's own pause 83 levels were finished for 94, and on 8 with the long pause 73 for 70 with 24 lives lost for 33. Set aside: right more often, and no better at playing on the dice it was measured on.
  2. *Why the clock's pay helped with the game's own pause.* With the clock's pay kept out of the remembered way only: 95 levels for 94. With the penalty for a life doubled by hand: not one number changed. So the 14 levels T-1036 lost with that pause were not the route and not the size of the penalty; the pay moved which button the AI pressed on with, by accident.
  3. *Level 21, never finished.* The AI dithers at the start. Paid nothing for 24 steps, it presses on with the button paid best so far, and on 40 of the 48 levels that is jump: its score guess is the game's vertical speed, which pays for jumping on the spot. Buttons never paid are never tried there.
  4. *Three remedies, on 20 levels a pause* (main: long 155 finished and 62 lives lost, short 166 and 111). A failed press not repeated: 133 and 171. The button paid most often first: 172 (43 lives) and 180 (121). **That, and then the buttons never paid: 201 (48 lives) and 196 (132); levels 21, 17, 5 and 42 finish 8, 10, 5 and 6 times with the long pause.**
  5. *The same build with other dice.* T-1036's code, the 48 levels, the long pause, the learner's seed moved by 1000 and nothing else: **332 levels finished for 423**, 166 lives lost for 165. Level by level the difference averages 1.9 with a spread (standard deviation) of 5.5. The levels never finished are 13, 14, 37 and 43, where they were 5, 17, 21 and 42. So "a level that never finishes" is mostly an unlucky start, a difference of 20 or 30 levels between two builds on one set of dice is within what the dice alone do, and the remedies of 4 must be measured on more than one set before one is built.
- **Objective:** `practice_bench.run(..., dice=0)`: the learner (the brain, what it tries, the demonstrations) is seeded with the level's number plus `dice`; the level, the game's noise and the scripted first go are those of the level's number whatever the dice. `--dice N` on the command line. `Report.dice`; the report's first line says which dice where they are not the usual ones, and is the line it was where they are. A whole number from 0 to 65535, refused otherwise before anything is connected.
- **Scope:** `tools/practice_bench.py`, tests, the documents. **Out of scope:** any change to how the AI plays (the remedy of try-out 4 is the next task, measured with this); a tool that runs many levels at once (the scratch scripts do); the practice game's own noise.

  2. The report keeps the dice; its first line ends ", with other dice (7)" after anything else a run is said to be with or without, and is unchanged with dice 0.
  3. The same dice give the same report, line for line; other dice on the same level give the same scripted first go and a different training (shown on a run where they differ).
  4. `--dice 7` does the same from the command line; `--dice` with -1, 65536, a word or a fraction is refused with a plain message; `run(dice=)` with True, -1, 65536, 2.5 or "7" raises `ConfigurationError` before anything is connected.
  5. Measured and written down as the baseline later tasks are held to: main on the 48 levels, both pauses, 12 goes of 300 steps, with dice 0 and dice 1000 (and one more set if time allows); `--dice 1000` gives the figures the try-out's patch gave, to the last number.

### T-1036 – The AI asks whether a rise was earned, during a go
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 3, the AI smarter. The third of three pieces: T-1034 asks the game, T-1035 keeps the answers and judges, this one has the runner ask during a go and measures the levels.)
- **Why now:** With a long dying pause eight of the 48 practice levels are never finished in 12 goes (5, 17, 21, 32, 35, 39, 42, 45). On four of them looked at (32, 35, 39, 45) the AI is paid "Progress goes up" for the top byte of the game's clock, and standing still pays best: with that pay withheld by hand they finish 10, 6, 6 and 8 times (T-1034). The two pieces that can find this out are merged and nothing calls them.
- **Try-out (before the plan, on a scratch copy at T-1035's head, described as one):** the runner asked at every step a value was paid for rising, from the newest saved moment eight steps or more back, and told the service. Levels 32, 35, 39 and 45 with the 200-frame pause, 12 goes of 300 steps: **9, 9, 3 and 3 levels finished for 0, 0, 0 and 0**. On level 45 the clock's top byte was asked about at steps 64 and 128 of the first go (15 plays each: it rose with every other move), doubted at the next review, dropped at the one after, and its pay taken out of the way the AI remembers before the second go. Real progress was asked about four to six times a value at 2 to 7 plays each and never called unearned. Asking costs: 11 to 20 askings a level over 12 goes.
- **Objective:** (1) `EpisodeSignals.take_rises()`: the values a rise of which was paid since the last call (a payment whose cause names a value and went up), each once, in the order they first paid; cleared by the call and by a new go. (2) `EpisodeRunner` takes `rise_worth_asking` and `rise_answered` (both or neither). After a step that cost no life, for the values that rose and are worth asking about: the newest saved moment `RISE_BACK` (8) steps or more before, and no more than `RISE_MOST` (40); the present is saved in `NOW_SLOT`; `rose_anyway` is asked for each value with what the go did since that moment, within the search's seconds; each answer is told (no answer is told nothing); the present is loaded back. A rise on a step a life went on is not asked about. One log line for each answer, in plain words. (3) `TrainingService` hands the runner the discovery service's `rise_worth_asking` and `rise_answered` where the go can go back.
- **Scope:** `training/episode.py`, `training/service.py`, tests, the documents. **Out of scope:** the mode byte paid at a death with a long pause; the speed read as progress for longer; levels 5, 17, 21 and 42, not looked at yet; what else stands in level 32's way; saving the counts with the game.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. `take_rises`: a payment for a value that went up is noted once, in order; one for a value that did not go up, one that names no value, and one while no go runs are not; the call clears, and so does a new go.
  2. The runner asks at the step the rise was paid on, from the newest moment eight steps or more back, with exactly what the go did since, the value from the knowledge, the frames a step and the search's seconds; it tells each answer; several values of one step share one save of the present and one load.
  3. It does not ask: with no callables; with no moments; for a value not worth asking about (not a play, not a save); with every moment less than eight steps back or the newest far enough more than forty back; on a step a life went on (nor later for that rise); for a value no longer in the knowledge.
  4. After the asking the game is where it was: a go that asks and one that does not read the same memory, step for step, to the end; the learner is told nothing of the plays.
  5. No answer (out of time, or no rise when played again) tells nothing and still puts the game back. A dropped link ends the go as "disconnected".
  6. On the practice game itself, with the real services: standing still, the clock's top byte paid as progress is asked about at steps 64 and 128 and called unearned both times; two reviews later it is dropped and no longer paid; the page crossed by walking and jumping is called earned and kept.
  7. The service hands the runner the discovery service's two functions where a go can go back, and none where it cannot. Misuse is refused.
  8. Measured on all 48 practice levels with both pauses, 12 goes of 300 steps, against main (short 457 levels finished and 262 lives lost; long 395 and 173): the four levels at 0 with the long pause finish; the totals are reported as measured, whichever way they fall.
  9. Every existing test passes with no assertion changed.
- **Expected changes:** `src/retro_ai_lab/training/episode.py`, `src/retro_ai_lab/training/service.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_rises_asked.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_rises_asked_in_training.py`, `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, this tracker.
- **Test plan:** written before the task's code; the try-out above came first. `tests/unit/training/test_rises_asked.py`: `test_the_signals_note_what_was_paid_for_rising` (1), `test_the_runner_asks_from_the_newest_moment_eight_steps_back` (2), `test_several_values_share_one_save_and_one_load` (2), `test_when_it_does_not_ask` (3), `test_a_rise_as_a_life_goes_is_not_asked_about` (3), `test_the_game_is_where_it_was` (4), `test_no_answer_tells_nothing` (5), `test_a_dropped_link_ends_the_go` (5), `test_a_clock_paid_as_progress_is_dropped_and_real_progress_kept` (6), `test_misuse_is_refused` (7). `tests/unit/training/test_rises_asked_in_training.py`: `test_the_service_hands_the_runner_the_asking` (7). Then every new line broken on purpose in a scratch worktree, the 48 levels with both pauses (8), and the whole suite alone (9).
- **Changed while building:** (a) `test_the_runner_asks_from_the_newest_moment_eight_steps_back` failed on its first run with a `ConfigurationError` out of `Moments.since`: a rise paid in the first seven steps of a go asked for a moment before step 0. The step asked for is now never below 0, and such a rise is not asked about (every moment is too close). Now `step()` takes them once and hands them to `_ask_rises(rose)`; the second run noticed every break. Per level: 10 10 11 8 13 0 10 14 12 7 12 9 10 9 11 6 11 0 10 12 3 0 10 11 7 14 13 8 9 11 11 5 9 15 10 9 10 3 10 3 10 12 0 12 11 3 8 11 (main: 10 10 12 8 13 0 10 14 12 5 12 9 7 9 11 6 11 0 10 12 3 0 7 11 7 14 13 8 9 10 11 10 0 15 10 0 10 2 11 0 9 12 0 12 11 0 10 9). ### T-1035 – What goes up whatever is pressed is not progress (what the AI knows)
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 3, the AI smarter. The second of three pieces: T-1034 asks, this one keeps the answers and judges, the next has the runner ask during a go and measures the levels.)
- **Why now:** With a long dying pause the practice game's clock is paid as progress and standing still pays best (T-1034: with that pay withheld by hand four levels finish 10, 6, 6 and 8 times for 0). The app already has a check for the top byte of a clock (T-996), and it does not catch this one here: it wants the byte below to tick at one pace, and with a long pause that byte stands still for 200 frames at every death. A value's own statistics depend on what the game happens to do; whether it rises whatever is pressed does not. T-1034 built the asking. Its answers are single pieces of evidence that can be wrong one way (another move gets the player killed and the clock stops: 3 of 30 in the try-out from 10 steps before, more from further back), so they have to be counted before anything is said, and what is said has to go the way every other doubt about a guess goes.
- **Objective:** (1) `understanding/unearned.py`: `Unearned`, a count for each value of the rises the game was asked about and of those that rose anyway. `note(var_id, anyway)` takes an answer; `counts(var_id)` gives (asked, anyway); `verdict(var_id)` is True where it rose anyway at `SAY_AFTER` (2) rises or more and at half or more of those asked about; `wants(var_id)` says whether another answer is still wanted: no verdict yet and fewer than `ASK_UP_TO` (6) answers. So a value is asked about six times at most, and one whose rises are earned costs a few plays and is then left alone. (2) `DiscoveryService`: one `Unearned` with each knowledge (as `Aftermath`), read-only as `unearned`; `rise_worth_asking(var_id)`: the value is one the AI reads as progress, not set aside, and another answer is wanted; `rise_answered(var_id, anyway)` takes an answer for such a value. In `doubt_bouncing`, a progress guess with that verdict and no other doubt gets the reason `ON_ITS_OWN`: the AI's own guess is doubted at that review and dropped at the next, with the counts in the evidence ("went up whatever was pressed 2 of the 2 times the AI asked the game; what goes up by itself is not progress"); a person's confirmed guess is kept and questioned, in the same words. A value dropped stops being paid through what is there already (the rewards follow the knowledge).
- **Scope:** `understanding/unearned.py`, `services/discovery.py`, tests, the documents. **Out of scope:** the runner asking during a go and telling the service (the next task, with the measurement on the 48 levels); the mode byte paid at a death with a long pause; the speed read as progress for longer.
- **Acceptance criteria:**

  2. The service: `rise_worth_asking` is True for a progress guess of the AI's or a person's, False for a value of another kind, one set aside, one not in the knowledge, and one with a verdict or six answers; `rise_answered` counts for such a value and refuses an unknown one; a game connected afresh starts counting afresh.
  3. `doubt_bouncing`: a progress guess that rose anyway is doubted, then dropped at the next call, with the counts and "what goes up by itself is not progress" in its evidence and the update announced; a confirmed one is kept and questioned in those words; a guess whose rises were earned, and one asked about once, are left alone; a guess with another doubt keeps that reason.
  4. Every existing test passes with no assertion changed.
- **Expected changes:** `src/retro_ai_lab/understanding/unearned.py`, `src/retro_ai_lab/services/discovery.py`, `tests/unit/understanding/test_unearned.py`, `tests/unit/services/test_discovery.py` (new tests only), `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, this tracker. (Nothing a person sees changes until the runner asks; the README waits for that.)

(3) A guess dropped by mistake stays dropped until a person confirms it, like every guess the AI drops. (4) The counts live as long as the game stays connected and are not saved.

### T-1034 – Asking the game whether a rise was earned
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 3, the AI smarter. T-1031's Limit 2: why eight levels never finish with a long dying pause.)
- **Why now:** With a dying pause of 200 frames eight of 48 practice levels never finish (5, 17, 21, 32, 35, 39, 42, 45); with the game's own pause 32, 35, 39 and 45 finish 3, 14, 14 and 10 times. Those four were looked at. The standstill searches, the first suspect, are not the cause. In their first goes the AI stays about one spot, loses no life, and is paid: on level 32, go 12, "Progress goes up +430.0 (43 times)" with three new places reached in 2,796 steps. That "progress" is the high byte of the game's clock (ram[22]: it goes up every 256 frames, 64 steps), which the classifier reads as a round counter. Standing still and staying alive is what it pays best.
- **Try-outs (before this entry, described as such; none of it is in the code):** (1) An oracle, not a fix: the four levels at 200 frames, 12 goes of 300 steps, with the progress pay withheld by hand for named bytes. Nothing withheld: 0, 0, 0, 0 levels finished. The clock's two bytes (ram[21], ram[22]) withheld: **10, 6, 6, 8**. The speed and the sub-pixel (ram[7], ram[4]), which are also read as progress for a while: 0, 0, 0, 0. The game's mode byte (ram[17], which goes to "dying" at a death and is paid 10 points for it, because the check of T-997 looks 90 frames ahead of a loss and the pause is 200): 0, 0, 7, 0. All five: 0, 6, 9, 8. So the clock is the cause on these, the mode byte a second one on one level, and level 32 has more than one thing in its way. (2) A longer look-ahead for T-997's check (250 frames for 90): 0, 1, 4, 0. (3) Whether asking the game can tell a clock from progress, on the practice game itself with a random walker on sixteen levels: at each rise of a byte, the steps before it were played again from a save with every other move held instead, and the rise called unearned where the byte ended as high with every one of them. From 10 steps before: the clock's high byte unearned in 27 of 30 rises (in the other three another move got the player killed or the level restarted, and the clock with it); the page of the player's place 0 of 26; the page of the scroll 0 of 20; coins 0 of 3; the score 0 of 3. From 20 steps before the clock is unearned in 20 of 30, from 40 in 17 of 30, the others 0 throughout. So real progress never rose anyway, and the clock nearly always did: the two can be told apart by asking, with a wide margin, and the nearer the save the cleaner.
- **Objective:** `training/earned.py`: `rose_anyway(connection, slot, trace, space, *, frames_per_step, value, seconds=None, clock=time.monotonic) -> Rise | None`. It loads the save, reads `value` (a `Variable` of the game's memory), plays `trace` and reads it again: None where it does not end higher than it began (played again, nothing rose). Then for every other move of the controls in turn (those a button away from the first move made first, as `last_chance` asks), it loads the save, holds that move for as many steps and reads the value: where it ends lower than the trace left it, the rise was earned and the answer is `Rise(anyway=False, plays)` at once; where it ends as high or higher with every one of them, `Rise(anyway=True, plays)`. Plays are tries like any other: off the record, nothing learned, nothing paid. With `seconds`, no play starts after that time and the answer is None. No game, byte or button is named.
- **Scope:** `training/earned.py`, its tests, the documents. **Out of scope:** who asks and when, and what follows from the answer (the next task: the runner asks at the first rises of each progress guess from the newest saved moment, and a guess that rose anyway at most of them is no longer read as progress, a person's confirmed guess being kept and questioned as ever); the mode byte paid at a death with a long pause (T-997's fixed look-ahead; the dying time T-1033 remembers could set it); the speed read as progress for longer with a long pause.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. On scripted plays: a value that ends as high whatever is held gives `Rise(True, 1 + the other moves)`; one that a single other move keeps from rising gives `Rise(False, plays)` with the plays made up to that move and none after, the near moves asked first; a trace that played again leaves it no higher gives None after one play; a move that leaves it higher still counts as "as high".
  2. On the practice game behind the real services, with both pauses: the page of the player's place crossed while walking right is earned (False); the high byte of the clock ticking over in the same stretch rose anyway (True); the game is left for the caller to put back, and nothing of a play reaches the learner, the rewards or the count of lives lost.
  3. Out of time: no play is started once the time is up, and the answer is None. Misuse is refused before anything is played: no save, nothing done, a move the controls do not have, a value that is no value of the game's memory, a bad `frames_per_step`, `seconds` or `clock`.
  4. Every existing test passes with no assertion changed.
- **Expected changes:** `src/retro_ai_lab/training/earned.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_earned.py`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, this tracker. (The README says what the app does; this task changes nothing a person sees, so the README waits for the next one.)
- **Test plan:** written before the task's code. `tests/unit/training/test_earned.py`: on scripted plays `test_a_rise_whatever_is_pressed`, `test_a_rise_one_move_prevents`, `test_nothing_rose_when_played_again` (1), `test_no_play_is_started_once_the_time_is_up`, `test_misuse_is_refused` (3); on the practice game `test_a_page_crossed_is_earned_and_the_clock_is_not` with both pauses, `test_nothing_of_it_is_on_the_record` (2). Then every new line broken on purpose in a scratch worktree, the new tests with a clock that stands still, and the whole suite alone (4).
- **Changed while building:** (a) Criterion 2 had the clock rise anyway "in the same stretch" as the page is crossed. It does not there: the first other move held, a jump kept up, drops the player into the gap, and this game's clock stops while the player dies, so the clock ends lower and its rise looks earned (`Rise(False, 2)`). That is the three-in-thirty case of try-out (3), and the reason one answer is one piece of evidence. The test holds both: in that stretch the clock looks earned, and standing at the start, where no move kills the player in fourteen steps, it rose anyway with every one of the fourteen other moves, whether the AI stood or walked itself. (b) In `test_nothing_of_it_is_on_the_record` the trace is seventy steps of standing with a dying pause of 8 frames, so that a play which walks into the gap has lost its life and restarted the level before it is over; the first draft walked right itself, lost the life in the replay and had no rise to ask about. (c) The play itself is a function of its own, `earned.ends` (what the value read at the save and after the moves), which the tests on scripted plays stand in for; the objective did not name it.
- **Results:** 8 new tests pass (5 on scripted plays, 3 on the practice game behind a real connection, one of them with both pauses). Every new line was broken on purpose in a scratch worktree: **42 breaks, all noticed**. A rise whatever is held costs one play for what it did and one for every other move (15 on a six-button pad); an earned one is known at the first move that leaves the value lower (2 plays for the page on the practice game). The new tests also pass with a clock that stands still for 15 ms at a time, as on Windows. Whole suite, run alone: **2,133 passed, 10 skipped** (2,125 and 10 on main); ruff, format and mypy clean.
- **Limits:** (1) Nothing uses it yet: no level finishes more often for this task. Who asks, when, and what follows is the next task. (2) One answer is evidence, not proof, both ways: a clock that stops or restarts when another move gets the player killed looks earned (3 of 30 rises in the try-out from 10 steps before, 13 of 30 from 40), and progress that every move reaches anyway (a level that scrolls by itself) would look unearned, which no game here has shown. (3) Only rises are asked about: the value ending as high or higher. (4) The mode byte paid at a death with a long pause, and the speed read as progress for longer, are untouched (out of scope).
- **Commit:** see PR #276. **PR:** #276.
- **Completion report:** `training/earned.py` `rose_anyway` asks the game whether a value went up whatever was pressed: it plays what the AI did up to the rise again from a save, then every other move held for as many steps, and says no at the first that leaves the value lower. On the practice game the page of the player's place is earned in two plays, and the high byte of the clock rose anyway with all fourteen other moves. It is a tool and changes nothing a person sees yet. **Next:** the runner asks with it at the first rises of each progress guess, from the newest saved moment, and a guess that rose anyway at most of them is no longer read as progress (a person's confirmed guess is kept and questioned); then the 48 levels with both pauses.

### T-1033 – Remembering how long a game takes over a lost life
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 3, the AI smarter. T-1032's Limit 1.)
- **Why now:** After T-1032 an asking still costs about 51 plays a life with a dying pause of 200 frames (40 with the practice game's own), about 7 of the 15 seconds a search may take on Boss's machine by his log's timings, at every life lost, before the search itself begins. Most of it is spent finding out again what the last loss already showed: the newest saved moment lies in the dying pause (15 plays to learn that), and the step is then halved for from the far end, where every step found too late costs a play for every other move (14 on a six-button pad) and a step found in time costs one or two. A game takes nearly the same time over every loss: the measured asks put the settled step 50 to 56 steps before the counter with the long pause and 12 to 18 with the short. This is what stands between T-1031 and a build Boss can try without each lost life costing seconds.
- **Objective:** (1) `training/chance.py`: `last_chance(..., guess=None)`: a step the caller expects to be the last at which the loss could still be changed. The trace is played again as before; then that step is asked. Where it still changes the loss, the steps after it are asked one at a time, `WALK` of them at most, until one is too late: that is the answer. Where the walk ends with none too late, or the guessed step is itself too late, the halving goes on as it did between what is known by then, so the answer is the one the asking gives without a guess, whatever the guess. (2) `training/episode.py`: the runner remembers the dying time, the steps from the settled step to the loss, from every sure answer that found one: the longest so far, or the newest where that one is more than `WALK` steps shorter than remembered (then what was remembered was another kind of loss, and a walk from it would not arrive). At a later loss it passes over the saved moments that by the remembered time leave fewer than `ROOM` steps before the settled step, as long as an older one is there, and asks the first that is left with the guess the remembered time gives (none where the guess does not lie inside the trace, or at or past a step already known to be too late). Everything after the asking is as in T-1032. Nothing about any game is written down: the time is this game's own, found by asking it, and kept for as long as the runner lives (a training session).
- **Scope:** `training/chance.py`, `training/episode.py`, tests, the documents. **Out of scope:** keeping the dying time between sessions; the order in which other moves are asked; why eight levels never finish with the long pause (T-1031's Limit 2); the penalty reaching the learner as late as the counter.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. `last_chance(guess=)` on scripted plays: for every settled step and every guess the answer is the one without a guess, sure; with the guess on the step before the settled one it takes the trace again, one or two plays at the guess and one play for every other move at the next step, and no more; with the guess up to `WALK` steps early, one step at a time and nothing halved; no guess is the asking as it was, play for play; a guess that is no whole number from 1 to below the step known to be too late (`shut`, or the length) is refused.
  2. Out of time with a guess (`partial=True`): the latest step found too late so far, `sure=False`; None where none was found.
  3. The runner on the practice game at 200 frames, two lives lost in a go: the first asking is the one T-1032 made, play for play; the second begins at the moment the remembered time leaves room at, not at the newest, with the guess the remembered time gives, makes fewer than half the plays of the first, finds the step the asking without memory finds, and the go gets past as before.
  4. The runner's memory, with the asking stood in for: a sure answer is remembered and an unsure one, one of 0 and None are not; the longest is kept, and one more than `WALK` shorter replaces it; moments are passed over only while an older one is there; no guess is given where it would lie outside the trace or at or past `shut`; a runner that never found a dying time asks as in T-1032.
  5. Every existing test passes with no assertion changed. Measured on the first sixteen levels with both pauses against main (148 levels and 62 lives with the long pause, 150 and 94 with the short; 51 and 40 plays an asking): the plays an asking takes, and the levels finished and lives lost, whatever they are. The levels may differ from main's: passing over a moment can put the search at an older one than before.
- **Expected changes:** `src/retro_ai_lab/training/chance.py`, `src/retro_ai_lab/training/episode.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_chance_guess.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_dying_time_remembered.py`, `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, this tracker.
- **Test plan:** written before the task's code; no try-out came first (the plays a step costs on either side were measured in T-1032). `tests/unit/training/test_chance_guess.py`, scripted plays: `test_a_guess_never_changes_the_answer`, `test_a_good_guess_costs_a_walk_and_one_step_too_late`, `test_out_of_time_with_a_guess`, `test_misuse_is_refused` (1, 2). `tests/unit/training/test_dying_time_remembered.py`: on the practice game with the real asking, `test_the_second_life_costs_far_fewer_plays` (3); with the asking stood in for, `test_what_is_remembered`, `test_moments_passed_over`, `test_where_no_guess_is_given` (4). Then every new line broken on purpose in a scratch worktree, the new clock-free tests run with a clock that stands still, the sixteen levels with both pauses (5), and the whole suite alone.
- **Changed while building:** (a) The first build passed moments over and searched from the one it asked. Measured on the sixteen levels with the long pause it finished 142 levels with 67 lives lost where main finishes 148 with 62 (20.1 plays an asking): a loss that took fewer steps than the longest remembered left a passed-over moment with room after all, and the search began 20 steps further back than main's. Now, after a sure answer, the newest moment passed over that has `ROOM` steps before the step found is the one searched from, with the count as that moment has it. With that the levels are main's, level for level (Results). `test_a_moment_passed_over_that_has_room_after_all` and the unsure case in `test_moments_passed_over` were added for it; they were not in the test plan. (b) The objective gave no guess "at or past a step already known to be too late". A moment asked after one that was too late from its first step gets no guess at all: the first moment asked has `ROOM` steps or more by the time remembered (or is the oldest), so the next one's guess would always lie past its `shut`. The rule in the code is "nothing asked yet". (c) The test plan's three tests with the asking stood in for became seven (`test_what_is_remembered`, `test_a_shorter_loss_takes_its_place_only_when_far_shorter`, `test_room_enough_is_fifteen_steps` twice, `test_moments_passed_over`, `test_a_moment_passed_over_that_has_room_after_all`, `test_an_older_moment_must_be_one_to_search_from`, `test_where_nothing_was_found_nothing_is_guessed`), because the unit lab holds for six goes of the same walk only: nobody has confirmed its life count, and at the seventh go its discovery counts lives on ram[6] in place of ram[10], so that go sees no life lost. Each test makes six goes at most on one lab, and the tests' `Goes` refuses a seventh. Seen while building; not looked into (Limit 4). (d) Numbers I expected wrongly when writing the tests, corrected against this entry and not against the code's convenience: on scripted plays the asking without a guess for step 30 of 40 costs 21 plays, not 48 (few of its halving steps land too late there); a check that the same moment asked without the guess takes more than twice the plays did not hold in the second loss of the practice go (33 for 19) and is "more plays" in the test; criterion 3's "fewer than half the plays of the first asking" holds (19 for 73, and 19 for 48 with the game's own pause). (e) The log line for a replay that does not lose the life again named the steps of the moment the search starts from. With a moment passed over, what was played again is an older moment's: the line names those steps now. Where nothing is passed over it is the number it was. (f) Criterion 5 allowed the levels to differ from main's. With (a) they do not.
- **Results:** 14 new tests pass (4 of the asking on scripted plays, 10 of the runner on the practice game). Every new line was broken on purpose in a scratch worktree: **56 breaks, all noticed** (48 of the first build, all noticed; one of those replaced and nine added with (a)). On scripted plays, for every settled step of a list of forty, every guess and three things that can be known of it, the answer is the one without a guess; with the guess on the step before the settled one the asking takes 610 plays over steps 2 to 40 where it takes 1,524 without (16 a step for 39). A guess from anywhere saves nothing (64,549 plays for 62,829 over all of them): the saving is in the guess being right or a little early. On the practice game, three lives lost in one go: **73, 19 and 16 plays** with a pause of 200 frames (dying time 53, 50 and 53 steps), **48, 19 and 16** with the game's own (15, 12, 15); each search is told the step the unguessed asking finds, and each finds its way. Measured on the first sixteen levels (simple table, 12 goes of 300 steps), frozen at this branch's code, against main: with 200 frames **148 levels, 62 lives lost, 515 searches, 420 ways found, the same level for level** (10 10 12 8 13 0 10 14 12 5 12 9 7 9 11 6), and 324 askings at **19.9 plays each (60 at most) where they took 51.3 (75 at most)**: 6,441 plays for 16,612. With the game's own pause **150 levels, 94 lives lost, 495 searches, 401 ways found, the same level for level** (7 12 13 12 11 1 12 12 13 0 13 9 12 11 9 3), and 347 askings at **19.9 plays (60 at most) where they took 40.1 (65 at most)**: 6,896 for 13,923. By the timings in Boss's log of 14 Nov that is about 3 seconds a life lost on his machine where it was about 7, and about 12 before T-1032 (an estimate from another kind of play). The new tests also pass with a clock that stands still for 15 ms at a time, as on Windows. Whole suite, run alone: **2,125 passed, 10 skipped** (2,111 and 10 on main); ruff, format and mypy clean.
- **Limits:** (1) The first life lost after training starts is asked in full (50 to 73 plays): the time is kept while the runner lives, which is until a setting changes or training starts from scratch, and not between sessions. (2) Two kinds of loss whose times lie more than 8 steps apart, taking turns, cost about a full asking at each turn; the practice game has one kind, so that is not measured. (3) The seconds for Boss's machine are an estimate. (4) The unit lab's life count moving to another value at the seventh go of the same walk (c) was seen and not looked into: it concerns a lab where nothing is confirmed by a person. (5) Unchanged: the eight levels that never finish with the long pause, and the penalty reaching the learner as late as the counter.
- **Commit:** see PR #275. **PR:** #275.
- **Completion report:** The AI now remembers how many steps this game takes over a lost life, and at the next life lost goes straight to a saved moment that leaves room before that step and asks there first, a step at a time (`last_chance(guess=)`, `EpisodeRunner.dying_steps`). An asking costs 20 plays where it cost 51 with a long dying pause and 40 with the practice game's own, and the levels finished and lives lost are what they were, level for level, with both. What is remembered is only where to begin: the step found is the one found without it, and the moment searched from the one it was. **Next:** a build for Boss to try on his game; then why eight levels never finish with the long pause (T-1031's Limit 2).

### T-1032 – Asking for the last chance costs less, and its time running out is not for nothing
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 3, the AI smarter. T-1031's Limit 1, taken before its Limit 2 because it decides whether T-1031 works on Boss's machine at all.)
- **Why now:** T-1031 asks the game from when on a loss was settled, and that costs plays: 77 a life on average with a dying pause of 200 frames (49 to 109), 40 with the game's own. In Boss's log of 14 Nov a play of 45 steps takes about 0.11 s (120 tries in 13.7 s), so on his game an asking would take about 12 of the 15 seconds it may take (15 plays of 45 steps from the moment 45 steps back, which is too late, then about 62 of 65 steps from the one before). That is an estimate from another kind of play, and close: if it is wrong by a quarter the time runs out, and then T-1031 knows nothing, searches from the first moment as before, finds nothing, and Boss's game is where it was. Two things are known for free and not used. (1) When the moment 45 steps back is too late from its first step, the moment 65 steps back is too late from its 20th step on at the latest: the halving there need not start from the end. (2) When the time runs out in the middle of the halving, the latest step found to be too late is known: going back to before that and trying changes before it is far better than nothing, since steps tried in vain only cost tries.
- **Objective:** (1) `training/chance.py`: `last_chance(..., shut=None)`: the caller knows the loss to be settled from step `shut` of the trace on at the latest; the halving starts from there instead of from the end, and no step from `shut` on is asked. (2) `Chance.sure` (True unless said): where the time runs out after the trace played again did lose the life on its last step, and a step is known from which on the loss was settled (by `shut` or by what was asked so far), `last_chance` returns `Chance(that step, plays, sure=False)` instead of None: the true step is that one or an earlier one. None as before where nothing is known. (3) `training/episode.py`: an older moment is asked with `shut` = the steps between it and the newer moment that was too late from its first step. Where an asking gives no answer because the time ran out (not because the trace did not lose the life again), and a newer moment was too late, the older moment is taken with that same bound, unsure. An unsure count is used like a sure one (the older moments' counts derived from it, the search told it), and the log says that it is the latest the step can be, not the step.
- **Scope:** `training/chance.py`, `training/episode.py`, tests, the documents. **Out of scope:** remembering how long a game takes over a loss and asking there first (the next task: it makes every asking after the first cost about 16 plays); the order in which other moves are asked; the dying pause possibly taken for a standstill (T-1031's Limit 2).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. `last_chance(shut=)` on scripted plays: the same step as without it wherever the step lies at or before `shut`, with no step from `shut` on asked and never more plays than without; `shut` equal to the length is the asking as it was, play for play; a `shut` that is no whole number from 1 to the length is refused.
  2. Out of time on scripted plays: before the trace was played again, or with nothing known, None as before; with `shut` given, `Chance(shut, plays, sure=False)` however early the time runs out after the first play; in the middle of the halving, the latest step found settled so far, never a step that was not found so (a step whose asking the time cut short counts for nothing), `sure=False`; in time, `sure=True` and the answer as before.

### T-1031 – Going back to before the last chance
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 3, the AI smarter. Named in T-1030's report as the next task: the fix that T-1030 made measurable.)
- **Why now:** Boss's log of 14 Nov shows going back for a way past failing 8 times of 8 on Super Mario Bros., after which the app stops going back: the life counter drops about 50 steps after the hit, the AI goes back 30 to 45 steps from the counter dropping, and every change it tries is to steps the game no longer listened to. With the practice game's dying pause at 200 frames (T-1030) the bench shows the same: 0 of 48 levels finished where 449 are with the game's own pause of 48 frames, 0 of 124 searches after a life lost finding a way on the first sixteen levels, and the AI giving up going back on 41 levels. Even with the short pause part of every search is spent there: the pause and the fall are 12 to 18 steps, and the places a change is tried at run from the last step backwards, every second step, so the first six to nine places of each round are ones where nothing can be changed.
- **Try-outs (14 Nov, scratch worktrees on T-1030's code, nothing kept; the first sixteen levels, simple table, 12 goes of 300 steps; main there: 155 levels finished with the game's own pause, 0 with 200 frames):** before a search, play what the AI did again from the saved moment with another move held from some step on, and halve the way to the step from which the life goes at the same step whatever is held (the last chance is the step before it); go back to a moment that leaves room before that step, and try changes before that step only. *First form:* three other moves asked at each step, those sharing the fewest buttons with the move made; a moment with 30 steps of room; the changes listed for the part of what it did before the last chance. With 200 frames **25 levels** (221 of 297 searches found a way); with the game's own pause **45** for 155 (50 with the story of a go also ended before the last chance, which is not this task's). Two things were wrong. The three moves asked left the jump out, so the last chance was put a few steps early, and those steps are where most ways past begin (on main 852 of 903 ways found start 13, 15 or 17 steps before the life went). And a change's hold was cut where the list ended, so a jump held 8 or 16 steps at the last place was taken for the one held 4 and left out. *Second form:* every other move asked, those one button from the move made first; a moment with 15 steps of room (what 30 steps before the counter leave with the game's own pause): 200 frames **94**, own pause **121**. *Third form:* the changes listed on all of what it did, placed before the last chance only, with their holds running on: **200 frames 148 levels finished (0), 62 lives lost (185), 277 of 324 searches after a life lost finding a way (0 of 124); own pause 150 levels (155), 94 lives lost (101), 301 of 347 searches (306 of 357).** With 200 frames levels 4 and 9 finish 13 and 5 times, which with the game's own pause on main finish 3 times and never.
- **Objective:** (1) `training/ways.py`: `changes(..., upto=None)` places changes at steps before `upto` only, from the last of those backwards (forwards with `early`), each still applied to, and told apart on, the whole of what it did. (2) `training/chance.py`, new: `last_chance(connection, slot, trace, space, frames_per_step=, lives=, seconds=None, clock=)` plays `trace` from the save, and if the life goes on its last step, halves its way to the first step from which every other move, held from there to the end, loses the life on that same step: it returns how many steps of the trace come before it (`live`) and the plays it made, or None where the trace played again does not lose the life on its last step, or the time is up. Off the record like any try. (3) `training/search.py`: `find_way(..., live=None)` places the changes to what it did before `live`, and the changes to the plain way before the step that way loses the life at, less as many steps as lie between `live` and the end of what it did. (4) `training/episode.py`: `EpisodeRunner(..., last_chance=False)`. When on, a search after a life lost first asks `last_chance` from the moment it would go back to, and from older moments while fewer than `ROOM` (15) steps lie before the last chance, puts the game back, says in the log what it found, and searches from that moment with that `live`. Off, the runner is what it was. (5) `TrainingService` turns it on.
- **Scope:** `training/ways.py`, `training/chance.py`, `training/search.py`, `training/episode.py`, `training/service.py`, tests, the documents. **Out of scope:** where the story of a go and the remembered way end after a loss that stands (still 30 steps before the counter: the next task, a try-out is running); the search at a standstill, where no life is lost; the penalty reaching the learner as late as the counter; how far back moments are kept (six, 20 steps apart: 100 to 119 steps, enough for a pause of some 70 steps).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. `changes(upto=)`: only places before `upto`, the nearest first (the furthest first with `early`); a hold reaches past `upto` and to the end of the trace; two changes that differ only past `upto` are both listed; `upto` at or past the end, or None, is the list as it was; a value that is no whole number of 1 or more is refused.
  2. `last_chance` on scripted plays: it finds the step exactly, wherever it lies (the first step, the last, between); asks the moves one button from the one made first and every other move before it calls a step too late; counts its plays; returns None where the trace played again loses no life, or loses it at another step; 0 where even the first step is too late; None once its time is up, with no play started after that; refuses what `find_way` refuses.
  3. `last_chance` on the practice game with the real services, pause 48 and 200 frames: a walk into the first gap has its last chance the same number of steps before the fall begins either way, and the steps after it are the fall and the pause.
  4. `find_way(live=)`: no change to the trace is tried at a step from `live` on, and none to the plain way in its last `len(trace) - live` steps; with the practice game at 200 frames it finds the way across the first gap from a moment before the last chance; `live=None` is the search as it was, play for play; nonsense is refused.
  5. The runner with `last_chance=True` on the practice game at 200 frames: a go that walks into the first gap goes back to a moment before the last chance (further than the 30 to 49 steps it went before), finds the way and gets across, and the log says from when on nothing could be changed; where the moment gone back to first leaves too little room it takes an older one; with nothing found the game is put back where it was; without the setting the same go finds nothing, as before.
  6. `TrainingService` runs its goes with it. Every existing test passes with no assertion changed. Measured on the 48 levels with the game's own pause and with 200 frames, against main (449 and 0 levels finished), with the figures in the results whatever they are.

It now says it was settled before that moment and that the time ran out before the AI could look further back; a test holds both lines apart.

### T-1030 – The practice game's dying pause is a setting
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 3, the AI smarter. Named in T-1029's report as the next thing, from Boss's log of 14 Nov.)
- **Why now:** Boss's log of 14 Nov (42 goes of Super Mario Bros. on the build of T-1028) shows going back for a way past failing 8 times of 8, after which the app stops going back for the session; every go loses its first life at the same enemy and the way it remembers stays at 33 steps. The go is paid most at step 33 and the life counter drops at step 85, every time: the counter drops about 50 steps after the hit, while the dying animation plays. The AI goes back 45 steps from the counter dropping, to a moment after the hit, and nothing it tries from there can help. The practice game has a dying pause too (T-984: "the life counter moves well after the fatal touch"), but of 48 frames, 12 steps, which the 30 steps the AI goes back cover. So every measurement on the practice game missed this, and the levels finished rose from task to task while Boss's game stayed where it was.
- **Try-out (14 Nov, a script that sets `toy_hopper.DYING_FRAMES` to 200 before the bench runs, nothing kept):** on main's code with T-1029, 48 levels, simple table, 12 goes of 300 steps: **0 levels finished (449 with the pause of 48 frames), 509 lives lost (290), 831 searches of which 296 found a way; on 41 of the 48 levels the AI stops going back** ("Going back found no way past 8 times in a row"). Level 2 reads like Boss's log: eight searches after a life lost, each "Went back 32 to 48 steps and made 120 tries: none got past" (the pause is 50 steps), and from the eighth go on nothing goes back.
- **Objective:** the pause is a setting of the game, and the bench can be run with it. (1) `ToyHopper.dying_frames`: the frames from the fatal touch to the life going, `DYING_FRAMES` (48) unless set, a whole number from 1 to 255 (the pause is counted down in one byte of the game's memory). It is the cartridge's, not the game's state: `reset()` and a game over leave it, and a pause already running runs out as it began. (2) `practice_bench.run(dying_frames=None)` sets it on the practice console's game before the scripted first go, so everything the app learns, it learns with that pause; `Report.dying_frames` keeps it and the report's first line says it when it is set; `--dying-frames` on the command line. Nothing else changes: with nothing set the game, the bench and its report are what they were.
- **Scope:** `emulator/fake/toy_hopper.py`, `tools/practice_bench.py`, tests, the documents. **Out of scope:** making going back work with a long pause (the next task, which this one makes measurable); changing the default pause (every existing test and every earlier measurement is on 48 frames); the racing game, which has no lives.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. `ToyHopper.dying_frames` is `DYING_FRAMES` on a new game. Set to 200, a fall starts a pause of 200 frames in which no button is heard and the life count stays, and on the 200th frame the life goes and the player is back at the start; set to 1, the life goes on the next frame.
  2. The setting outlives `reset()` and a game over started again; changed during a pause, the pause in hand runs out as it began and the next one has the new length. The same seed and buttons with the same setting play the same game.
  3. A value that is not a whole number from 1 to 255 is refused (a truth value, 0, 256, a fraction, text) and the setting stays what it was.
  4. `practice_bench.run(dying_frames=200)` trains on a game with that pause: `Report.dying_frames` is 200, the first line of the report ends ", with a dying pause of 200 frames", and a go of 60 steps that walks into the first gap ends before the life is counted where the same go with the default pause counts it. With nothing set the report is the one it was, word for word. `--dying-frames 200` does the same from the command line; nonsense is refused there and in `run`.
  5. Every existing test passes with no assertion changed. Measured through the setting on the 48 levels with 200 frames: the try-out's figures to the level, whatever they are, as the starting point for the next task.
