### T-1021 – A landing is no restart
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 4, a smarter learner: goes thrown away before the learner has played them. Found while measuring T-1019 and T-1020, whose runs meet it more often than main's.)
- **Why now:** in T-1020's run of sixteen levels (the simple table, twelve goes of 300 steps) two levels lost three goes each, ended "by reset" after 5 and 10 steps; in T-1019's runs two levels lost three and six. Each time the log blames the same two values: "Score at ram[8], Flag at ram[9] all went back to their starting values". On the practice game those are the fall speed and "on the ground": after a jump both are back where they began, together, and one of them is a number that went down. The rule for a restart (T-838, T-846, T-867) asks for two values home together, one fairly sure, a number that dropped, and at least half of every value that has moved; a go that begins by playing the way it remembers (T-1015) loses no life and scores nothing for hundreds of steps, so few values have moved and two is half of them. The remedy there is (T-845) marks such values as cycling only after three goes in a row have ended that way within 120 steps: three goes lost each time, and all six where the landing came at step 320.
- **What was measured before any code (a try-out that changes nothing):** the detector was watched in T-1020's runs of levels 3 and 7. At each of the six false restarts the two values blamed had already gone back to their first values 43 to 46 and 75 to 121 times earlier in the session, in snapshots where no restart was called and the game played on; three tracked values had moved in all. So the AI had seen, dozens of times over, that these two go home in play. What it also showed: the values that go home when the app itself puts the game back to the checkpoint at the start of a go (lives, score, progress) would be counted the same way unless those snapshots are told apart, and they must be: they are what a real restart is known by.
- **Tried first and dropped (13 Nov):** leaving a home-goer out of the restart rule altogether, by giving it the `cycles` mark of T-845. Two existing tests on the racing game failed, and rightly. There the next checkpoint goes home every lap and also when the game starts over; with it left out, the game starting over was no longer called (the "game over" switch going home alone is not enough), the values that only a restart sends home were then counted as coming home in play, and after three unseen restarts they were left out as well. So a home-goer keeps its say; it only cannot make a restart with nothing but other home-goers.
- **Tried second and dropped (13 Nov):** counting every return in play, however it came about, and calling a value a home-goer at three. It was built, tested and measured (T-1020's code on levels 3 and 7: goes ended by reset 3 to 0 on each, levels 5 to 11 and 6 to 11; main on the sixteen levels: goes ended by reset 11 to 2, levels 140 to 141, lives lost 106 to 104). Then the log was read: among the home-goers it named were the life count, the score and the place in the level. A restart that goes uncalled for any other reason is a return "in play" for every value it sends home, and after three of those the game starting over had nothing left to be known by. A second try-out, against the game's own account of when it starts over (three levels on main), showed how common that is: of nine real restarts none was called, on main as with the change (a fault of its own, put down below as what comes next), so the count could only ever grow.
- **Tried third and dropped (13 Nov):** counting only a return within sixty snapshots of leaving. A third try-out had measured how long each value is away in play (levels 1 and 3, 27,000 snapshots: "on the ground" 4 to 7 snapshots as a rule, the fall speed 39, the life count never under 320). Built, tested, measured the same on levels 3 and 7, and 26 deliberate breaks noticed. Then the whole suite: the first demonstration's test failed on the racing game. There a whole game is shorter than sixty snapshots while the AI is still looking about; the "game over" switch, the life count and the score were home-goers before the first go, no restart was called any more (17 goes ended by one on main, none now) and the training ran aground at a spot it stood still in (42 of 60 goes).
- **Tried fourth and dropped (13 Nov):** counting only a return at which fewer than half of the values that had moved went home with it. The racing game failed the same way. A fourth try-out showed why: when that game starts over nearly every value changes, but few land on what their watches call their first value (a watch is made anew whenever the AI learns something about its value, and takes the value of that moment for the first: the score's was 487, the life count's 1). So a real restart looks like one value home of five. What it cannot look like is a quiet snapshot: five of five had changed.
- **Objective:** (1) `EventDetector` counts, for every tracked value that changes in a snapshot in which fewer than `RESET_SHARE` (half) of the values that have moved changed at all, the value it came to; up to `HOMES_KEPT` (64) different values a variable. Such a snapshot is the game playing on: whatever the game starting over does, it changes most of what has moved. Not counted: a snapshot that is the first since the app loaded a saved state; a value marked as cycling. (2) A watched value whose first value has been come to `HOME_OFTEN` (3) times that way is a home-goer. A restart needs, besides all it needed before, at least one value going home that is not a home-goer. Home-goers still count among the values that went home and among those that moved, and are named with the rest. It goes by the value come to, not by the variable: a switch has two resting places and its watch may begin at either; a life count watched from 1 is a home-goer there and is the sign of a restart at 3. What was seen is kept by where a value is held and how it is read (region, offset, encoding, length), because a removed guess's id is taken over by the next guess. (3) `take_home_goers()` gives each home-goer out once: when its first value is come to the third time, or, where its watch was made anew at a value already counted, at the first restart that is not called because of it. (4) `MemoryObserved.put_back` says the snapshot is the first since a saved state was loaded, by whoever loaded it (the checkpoint at the start of a go, a practise spot, a go put back to a saved moment, an experiment or a search putting the game back where it was): the adapter counts its loads (`EmulatorAdapter.states_loaded`) and the observer compares. (The checkpoint's restore at the start of a go is not otherwise told to anyone: `expect_jump` is called for a practise spot and for going back only, and what it changes in the counting of bytes is left as it is.) (5) `DiscoveryService` hands the mark on to its detector and says once in the log, by name, which values it has found to be home-goers. Nothing in what the AI knows is changed.
- **Scope:** `understanding/events.py`, `emulator/base.py` (a count), `services/observer.py` (one field), `services/discovery.py`, tests, the documents. Nothing about any game is written down. **Out of scope and left as it is:** a life lost with the player put back at the level's start, read as a restart where no way past was found (the go ends with lives left: it costs the rest of a go that has been played, not a whole go, and telling it from the game starting over needs the life count); the game really starting over after the last life, which the second try-out found is not called at all on the three levels looked at, with or without this change; the first landings of a session, before any value has been seen to come home three times, and landings while so little has moved that a landing is half of it (they are not counted, and not needed once others were) (T-845's three-goes remedy still stands behind this one); what was seen is the detector's and is not saved, so it is seen again in each session's first landings.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. In a snapshot in which fewer than half of the values that have moved changed, every value that changed has the value it came to counted; with exactly half changing nothing is counted, and the share is of what has moved, not of what is watched. A watched value whose first value was come to three times is given out by `take_home_goers()`, once. Not counted: a snapshot at which a restart is called; a snapshot the detector is told is the first since a saved state was loaded (`observe(..., put_back=True)`), though its events are as before; a value marked as cycling (it is not judged at all, as before); the values a variable comes to after its first 64 different ones. The counts outlive `reset()` and a change of the value's record (its evidence, its kind). They are kept by where the value is held and how it is read, not by its id: a guess that takes over the id of a removed one has none of them, the same bytes read another way (one byte, then two) are another value, and what was seen at a place is dropped when the knowledge holds nothing there any more.
  2. Values that are all home-goers, home together with a number among them that dropped and nothing else moved, are no restart, however often. With one value among them that is not a home-goer it is a restart as before, and it names them all. The share of what has moved is counted as before, home-goers included. It goes by the value come to: a watch made anew at a switch's other resting place has what was seen of that one; a life count that comes to 1 in play and to 3 at a restart is a home-goer watched from 1 and none watched from 3; a home-goer whose watch was made anew at a counted value is given out at the first restart not called because of it. What a restart sends home is never counted there: neither where it goes uncalled for want of a number that dropped, nor where everything changes and only one value lands on its watch's first value. Every existing test of the restart rule passes unchanged.
  3. `EmulatorAdapter.states_loaded` counts the saved states loaded, and only those that loaded. `MemoryObserved.put_back` is true for the first snapshot after one or more loads and false for every other, the first after connecting included; `went_back` is as before.
  4. `DiscoveryService` says once in the log, by name, which values it has found to be home-goers; it announces nothing and changes nothing in what the AI knows. The app's own restores make no home-goer: the same jumps that make two home-goers when the game is left to itself, with a saved state loaded before every look at the memory on the way down, and nothing is said.
  5. On the practice game behind the real services, with the fall speed taken for a score and "on the ground" for a switch, as the AI's own guessing has them: after three jumps in play both are named in the log, and no restart is called at a later landing at which nothing else has moved. The same game and moves without the three jumps before: a restart is called at that landing, as it is today.
  6. Measured on the bench, old against new: T-1020's code on levels 3 and 7 (the simple table, twelve goes of 300 steps: three goes thrown away on each) with this task's change added, and main on the sixteen levels (goes ended by reset 11, levels 140, lives lost 106); on three of main's levels, against the game's own account of when it starts over, that no restart that was called before goes uncalled; and on the racing game, the run of the first demonstration that failed under the third and fourth tries (the learner's seed 2), that it plays as on main. The figures go in the results whatever they are.
  7. The whole suite passes; no assertion of an existing test is changed.
- **Expected changes:** `understanding/events.py`, `emulator/base.py`, `services/observer.py`, `services/discovery.py`, `tests/unit/understanding/test_events_home_goers.py` (new), `tests/unit/services/test_observer.py` (one test added), `tests/unit/services/test_discovery_home_goers.py` (new), `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `TASK_TRACKER.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Test plan:** written before the code (the try-out came first, as told above). `tests/unit/understanding/test_events_home_goers.py`: `test_a_value_that_goes_home_in_play_is_a_home_goer` (1), `test_what_is_not_counted` (1), `test_only_a_snapshot_in_which_little_else_changed_is_counted` (1), `test_a_roaming_number_has_only_its_first_values_counted` (1), `test_the_counts_outlive_a_reset_and_a_changed_record` (1), `test_a_value_read_another_way_is_another_value` (1), `test_home_goers_alone_are_no_restart` (2), `test_it_is_counted_by_the_value_come_to` (2), `test_a_home_goer_found_at_a_restart_that_is_not_called_is_given_out_there` (2), `test_what_a_restart_sends_home_stays_a_sign_of_one` (2), `test_nonsense_is_refused` (1). The observer's test file: `test_the_first_snapshot_after_a_saved_state_is_loaded_is_marked` (3). `tests/unit/services/test_discovery_home_goers.py`: `test_home_goers_are_said_once_and_nothing_else_changes` (4), `test_the_apps_own_restores_make_no_home_goer` (4), `test_a_landing_is_no_restart_once_it_has_been_seen` (5). Each checked against the code broken on purpose. Regression (7): the whole suite. The measurement (6) with the try-outs' scripts and the bench.
- **Results:** 7 of 7 criteria met. The whole suite: 2,020 passed, 10 skipped (2,005 and 10 before: 15 new tests), with ruff, the formatter and mypy (146 files) clean. Thirty-two deliberate breaks of the new code, each noticed by the new tests; three were not at first (what was seen being kept for a removed guess, the mark not being handed on by the service, the way a value is read being left out of where it is held) and the tests were made to. One of those runs left a stale compiled file of a broken source behind (a break of the same length, put back within the same second); the script no longer writes compiled files and every figure below was measured after that. **T-1020's code with this change, the two levels its run lost goes on (the simple table, twelve goes of 300 steps):** level 3, goes ended by reset 3 to 0, levels finished 5 to 11 (14 on main), lives lost 4 to 7; level 7, 3 to 0, levels 6 to 11 (14 on main), lives lost 14 to 4. **Main with this change, sixteen levels:** goes ended by reset 11 to 4, levels finished 140 to 136, lives lost 106 to 109, goes finishing a level 98 to 95. Eleven levels ran exactly as before. Level 1: resets 4 to 2, levels 5 and 5, lives 12 to 13. Levels 6 and 8: one reset fewer each, levels the same. Level 10: resets 2 to 0, levels 11 to 10. Level 13: one reset fewer, levels 6 to 3, lives 9 to 11: its fifth go, which ended by reset after 966 steps on main, plays on to 1,016, and the goes after it take another course (they stay about 1,010 to 1,020 steps to the tenth, where main's climb to 1,476). No level finished more. So on main, where the landing itself is seldom what is called a restart, the change removes false calls and gains nothing by it in these runs; one run a level cannot tell a loss of four levels in 140 from the runs taking different courses, and the write-up does not claim it can. **Against the game's own account of when it starts over (levels 1, 13 and 10 on main):** of nine real restarts none is called, before and after; of the restarts that are called none is real, before (10, 6 and 3 in play, and one on each level after a saved state was loaded) and after (8, 3 and none in play; one, one and two after a load). No restart that was called and real goes uncalled, there being none. **The racing game, the first demonstration's run that failed under the third and fourth tries (the learner's seed 2):** it plays as on main to the last figure (the point-lover 34.35 a go over 137.9 steps and 360.0 points, the careful one -86.5 over 133.7), and of its 42 real restarts the same 16 are called.
- **Commit:** see PR #263. **PR:** #263.
- **Completion report:** A landing no longer ends a go as "the game started over". What the AI goes by is the one thing a restart cannot do: leave most of what has moved unchanged. A value seen three times to come to the very value its watch began at, in such a quiet moment, cannot make a restart with nothing but its like. The task took five designs to get there, and the four that were dropped were not small slips: each was built whole and tested, three of them measured better on the practice game, and each was then shown wrong by something outside its own tests (two older tests on the racing game, the log's list of names, the first demonstration on the racing game, a look at what that game does when it starts over). What they had in common is what is now written down as the next task's ground: **a watch takes for a value's first value whatever it holds at the moment the watch is made, and a watch is made anew every time the AI learns something about its value.** So "went back to where it started" means less than it says: on the practice game no real restart is called at all (the life count is watched from 1 and never "goes home" at 3), and a life lost with the player put back at the level's start is what gets called instead; on the racing game 26 of 42 real restarts go uncalled. **Left for the next tasks, in this order:** (1) where a value started: the first value kept when a watch is made anew, and taken where the game is known to be at a beginning; then what is called a restart measured again against the game's own account; (2) the first look after the AI goes back to a saved moment (the camera's travel lost there); (3) T-1020, which waits for a person's word on one older test's limit, and T-1019 behind it; (4) a clock taken for progress.
### T-1020 – The camera's move, where the screen cannot tell it
- **Status:** Done (was blocked from 13 Nov on one existing assertion; Boss approved its correction the same day, see "The one older assertion")
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 2, the eyes: the bench's line on the camera, 82% and 73% of moves measured right in the long runs against a target of 90, and the ground counted to within a step in 0% and 2% of goes. What T-1017 found would settle it, and left for a task of its own.)
- **Why now:** T-1019 (a way past must leave the AI room at its end) is built and measured on its branch and cannot be merged: its ways change the pinned runs, and in two of them an older fault then shows. One is this: `test_new_ground_is_paid_as_the_game_has_it` asks that the furthest ground counted is the game's own to within a step in 11 of 12 goes, and gets 10. Go by go the count is off by 17 to 24 pixels in two goes on main and three on that branch. The test is right; the camera's measure is what is wrong. (The other fault, a landing taken for a restart, is T-1021.)
- **What was measured before any code (two try-outs that change nothing):** (1) *When is the camera's move misread?* The simple table, twelve goes of 300 steps: on level 0, 658 of 3,274 looks in which the camera moved (80% right); on level 3, 708 of 4,009 (82%). 641 and 604 of those with a walker in view; the mistake is the walker's own 4 pixels (16 read as 20 or 12), or the camera read as still (202 and 117 looks). This is T-1017's finding again: bare ground, one thing walking, one number for two unknowns. (2) *Is there something that is not the picture?* The game keeps its own count of where the camera is, as most games that scroll do. For every byte of memory the try-out counted how often its change between two looks was the move the picture gave. One byte stands out on both levels: ram[19] agrees in 85% and 84% of the looks the picture read as moving and stays put in 85% and 93% of those it read as still (it is right, and the picture wrong, in most of the rest: against the game's own figure it agrees in 99%). The player's own position, ram[2], is next (84% and 83%; 73% and 78%), since the camera follows the player. No other byte agrees in more than 5% of moving looks. By the time 20 moving and 20 still looks had been seen (look 79 and 78) ram[19] was the only byte passing 60% of each, and stayed so. So the AI can find the byte by itself, from its own partly wrong measure, within the first go.
- **Objective:** (1) `observation/camera_memory.py`, `CameraMemory`: shown the memory before and after a look and the camera's move as the picture alone had it, it keeps for every byte and each axis how often the byte changed by that move in the looks read as moving and stayed put in the looks read as still. An axis has its byte once `NEEDS` (20) looks of each kind have been seen and a byte agrees in `AGREES` (6 of 10) of each; of several, the one that agrees most often. `expect(before, after)` is then that byte's change, a roll-over counted the short way round, and None for an axis with no byte. The counts are halved past `REMEMBERS` looks, so a byte that stops agreeing is dropped. (2) `ObjectTracker.update(frame, hide=, expect=)`: the picture is measured as before (`sighted`). Where `expect` says something else within the camera's reach, it is the camera's move if the new screen laid over the old one that way differs in at most `SLACK` (one hundredth of the pixels that vote) more than under the picture's own answer, and, unless next to nothing changed at all, leaves no more of what changed unexplained than a move may (`EXPLAINS`). So a walker's own few pixels, a bare screen and scenery that repeats are settled by memory; scenery that tells, a cut to another place and a wrong byte are settled by the picture. (3) `ScreenWatch.look(frame, ..., memory=)`: learns from every look the picture measured by itself, expects from the byte once it has one, says in the log which byte it found, and takes nothing across a look at which the game was put back or a life went. `EpisodeRunner` hands it the memory read with each screen.
- **Scope:** `observation/camera_memory.py` (new), `observation/tracking.py`, `training/vision.py`, `training/episode.py` (one argument), tests, the documents. Nothing about any game is written down: which byte it is, is found each session from the looks. **Out of scope:** the tries of a search (their watch is given no memory and measures by the picture alone, as now); the memory guesses the brain sees; leaving movers out of the vote (T-1017: measured worse). **Known and left:** a game that keeps no such byte, or keeps it at another scale, gets nothing from this and loses nothing; a byte counting the other way is not looked for; in the first go, until the byte is found (about 80 looks), the measure is as before.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. Scripted memories: after 20 looks read as moving and 20 as still, the byte that changed by the move read in at least 6 of 10 of the first and stayed put in at least 6 of 10 of the second is the axis's byte; before that, and with no such byte, nothing is expected for the axis.
  2. It stands a reading that is wrong one look in five. A byte that never changes, a clock that adds the same every look, a byte of noise and a byte that moves at half the rate are never taken. Of the camera's own byte and the player's position (which moves as the camera while it is followed, and alone on a still screen) the camera's is taken.
  3. What it expects is the byte's change from one memory to the next, the short way round a roll-over; each axis has its own byte; a memory of another length starts it over; a byte that stops agreeing is dropped again.
  4. The tracker, bare ground and a lone walker, the camera moving 16 a look: without `expect` the move is misread (as it is today); with it the move is 16 in every look, `sighted` is what the picture said, and the walker's own speed in the level comes out as 4. With nothing in view that tells at all, and with scenery that repeats every 16 pixels, the same.
  5. The picture decides where it can: scenery that tells and moved 16 with 8 expected is 16; after a cut to another place what is expected is refused and as much is left unexplained as before (the watch still sees a jolt); a move expected beyond the camera's reach is refused; None, and None for one axis, change nothing for that axis; anything else is refused with the reason. Without `expect` every existing tracker test passes unchanged.
  6. ### T-1018 – A go that ends at a wall looks for a way on
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 4, "a smarter learner": it practises where it gets no further. Named as next in T-1015, T-1016 and T-1017.)
- **What was found before any code, on practice level 0 with the simple table, goes of 300 steps with the remembered way:** from its fifth go to its eighth the AI walked to the third wall (2,244 of 2,496) from memory and stood against it until the go ran out; it got over by chance in the tenth go. Going back and looking for a way (T-1007) happens only when a life is lost, and at a wall none is. A try-out in the runner (described here because it came first, to find out whether the idea could work at all): where the go stays about one spot, go back and try small changes to the plain way, as after a loss. Three things were learnt from it. (a) What tells a standstill is where the AI is, not what it is paid: something is nearly always paid a little while it stands (a jump on the spot reaches a new height, and a clock taken for progress ticks: "Progress (2nd guess) goes up" paid 24 times in one go at a wall). Nor is it "no new ground": put back to the start after a life lost, the AI walks over old ground and is not standing. (b) Going back as far as after a loss (30 steps) leaves half the standing in the story, and the changes are tried from the end of what it did backwards, so the way found was "stand for 32 steps, then jump": the next go stood there again. (c) Going back to the moment before it came to the spot, the way found begins where the standing did, and the table's seven goes finish the level in the fifth.
- **Found while building it, and part of this task:** (d) The watch's "place" is the camera's travel and nothing else: pacing 80 pixels on a screen whose camera stood still read as no move at all. The runner now goes by `ScreenWatch.spot`, the camera's travel plus where on the screen the AI last saw itself. (e) On a screen where nothing changes for the brain (a wall with nothing else in view) the go ends "stuck" after 25 steps, or presses the wake button, which forgets the saved moments: before the 60 steps were up. A go about to end that way now looks for the way on first. (f) With goes of 150 steps a walk-right brain came to a fixed point: every go stood at the wall, searched, got over, fell into the next gap, went back for the way past and ran out of steps on ground it had already been paid for, so nothing of either way was remembered and the next go was the same go again, search for search. A way a search has found is now played to its end before the go may end for its length. (g) The first cut of "where the standing began" was 16 steps after the anchor was set, which is up to 64 pixels before the spot: later goes waited at the wall for up to 24 steps, and on a slow game the way would have jumped short of the wall. It is now the first look that saw the AI where it stands. (h) A search at a standstill was slow. After a life lost most changes lose the life again and cost one blind play (about 20 ms on the practice game); at a standstill nearly all stay alive, and I had every one played under the screen watch (about 400 ms): in the bench's short run one search took 50 seconds for 114 tries. Now a change is played blind first, as after a loss, and the blind play also takes the screen it ends on: a change that ends on the very screen a play that got nowhere ended on (holding the plain move, or an earlier change that was looked at) is not looked at. A standstill search may make twice the plays of one after a loss (`STAND_TRIES`), because a change that does end somewhere new costs two. The same three searches then take 0.7, 4.6 and 8.1 seconds (1.0, 12.7 and 50.0 before) and find the same ways. In the app a search is cut off at 15 seconds either way. (i) The first full run failed nine older tests, none of them for a fault in the old code. Three used a stand-in for the screen watch without the new `spot`, and two expected a runner that stands still to end "stuck" with nothing searched: the runner's new behaviour is now off unless asked for (`stand_after=0`, as pressing on is `press_after=0`), the training service asks for it, and those five pass unchanged. One was the bench's line, which this task rewords. Three were the bench's tests of the eyes on its short runs: with the standstill search the same five goes of 80 steps get over the first wall (1,004 with the search as it now is, where they got to 421) and past the first walker, where the camera's measure is known to be wrong (T-1017), and it reads 82% right there against the 90% the test asks; the twelve goes on level 3 met a walker for the same reason. Those tests are about the first screens of a level, so they are kept on the goes they were written for with a switch (`stand=False` in the bench, `--no-standstill`), exactly as T-1015 kept them with `remember=False`. No assertion in them was changed. The weakness further in is not hidden by this: it is in the long runs' figures below and stays the next task but one. (j) The first measurement (twelve goes of the simple table) reached the flag from the fourth go, and its log showed two faults in what was found. Where the brain dithers at a wall rather than stands, the changes, tried from the end of what it did backwards as after a loss, gave ways with up to 64 steps of waiting in them ("from step 64 of that"). They are now tried from the start forwards at a standstill (`changes(..., early=True)`): the earliest that gets on has the least standing in it. And two steps of new ground, which put a try past a place a life was lost, are no way on from a standstill: a small hop and standing again counted (the bench's short run got to 64, 196, 196, 356 and 360 on ways like that). (k) Asking for four steps of new ground instead found nothing at all near a level's start: the short run got to 37, 73, 192, 192 and 348, worse than without the search, in five searches of which one found a way. Printing every try of those searches showed why. The trace handed over ends 4 steps after it came to the spot (g), a hold was cut off at the trace's end, so the longest run any change could make was 7 steps, 56 pixels; and new ground is the wrong measure of leaving a spot, since it counts next to nothing until the camera moves. So a hold is now played out whole at a standstill, past the trace's end (`whole=True`), and a way on is a try that stays alive on new ground and ends out of the spot, more than 64 pixels from where the go came to stand, by `ScreenWatch.spot`, the measure the standing was told by (`find_way(..., enough=...)`, `Outcome.spot`). The same short run then gets to 160, 421, 441, 884 and 1,004, with a way found in all five of its searches. (l) Stopping after three searches in a row with nothing would have switched the whole thing off in a brain's first goes, when it dithers near the start, before it ever met a wall. It now stops after as many as the searches after a life lost do (`give_up_after`: eight in the app, never where that is not set), counted apart from theirs. (m) With the goes getting further, T-1016's `test_lives_lost_to_a_walker_are_put_down_to_it` failed: 6 falls, 4 put down to a fall, where it allows one short. Listing each death showed the eyes were right. The two were deaths that had begun in the last steps of a go and cost no life: a way found over a wall is played to its end, carries on for 20 steps and ended in the next gap (the furthest the two goes got, 1,044 and 1,577, is inside a gap), the go ended in the dying pause of 12 steps, and the next go starts from its save. The bench counted a death when the pause began. It now counts those apart (`Report.unfinished`, said in its "Deaths" line), and of the lives that did go, 4 of 4 falls and 3 of 3 walkers are put down to their cause (3 of 3 and 2 of 2 in the same run without the search, which had one such death too: that is what the test's allowance of one was for). The test's assertions are unchanged and two stricter ones are added. What it shows about the search is left for its own task: a try counts as alive while its life has not gone, so a way can end already dying in the next gap. (n) The bench's fixed short run is made with `stand=False` and its first line says so: `test_the_report_reads_in_words` expected the old line and expects the new one.
- **Objective:** in `training/episode.py`, the runner notes at each look where the screen watch has the AI (`ScreenWatch.spot`). A go that has counted new ground at some point and has then stayed within `STAND_WITHIN` (64) pixels of one spot for `STAND_AFTER` (60) steps, with no list of moves being played, goes back and looks for a way on, once for that standstill; so does a go about to end "stuck" at a standstill, without waiting for the count. It goes back to the newest saved moment at or before the step it came to about the spot (`Moments.since`), and the search is given what it did from there up to `STAND_REACH` (4) steps past the first look that saw it within `STAND_NEAR` (8) pixels of where it now is. `find_way(..., stood=True)`: the plain way first, as after a loss; where that stays alive and gets nowhere new, the small changes to the plain way are tried (after a loss they are not: there the changes to what it did come next), and then the changes to what it did; both lists from the start forwards (`early`) with every hold played out whole (`whole`), and a try is a way only where it also ends out of the spot (`enough`, the runner's `_left_the_spot` against `Outcome.spot`). With `stood` the blind play of each change takes the screen it ends on (`play(..., end=True)`, `Outcome.screen`), and a change that ends on a screen a play that got nowhere ended on is not looked at. A way found is played through the ordinary step from the moment gone back to, so the standing is not in the story and not in what the next go remembers, and it is played to its end even where the go's length runs out first. With none found the game is put back to where it was, the moments are kept (no loss stands), and that spot is not searched again; `give_up_after` such searches in a row with nothing found (eight from the service, counted apart from the searches after a life lost) and the runner stops looking at standstills for this game and says so. The searches are the go's own three (`ways_per_go`), counted with the others and apart (`ways_stood`). Going back for any reason starts the count of standing afresh. It is switched on by `EpisodeRunner(..., stand_after=60)` (0, the default, never looks); `TrainingService(..., stand_after=STAND_AFTER)` passes it where the go can go back and says so in the log once; the bench's `run(..., stand=True)` and `--no-standstill` switch it off for comparing.
- **Scope:** `training/episode.py`, `training/search.py`, `training/trial.py` (the screen a try ends on, and the spot), `training/ways.py` (the order and the whole hold), `training/moments.py`, `training/vision.py` (one property), `training/service.py` (the switch and a log line), `tools/practice_bench.py` (a count, its wording and the switch; deaths that cost no life counted apart), tests, the documents. **Out of scope (later tasks):** a clock taken for progress pays for standing still (recorded above; its own task); a way that ends in the dying pause of the next gap (m); the camera's move from the AI's own position in memory; the ground count; tidying a remembered way. **Known and left:** a standstill costs 60 steps, or the 25 of "stuck", the first time a go meets it; a go that has not yet got anywhere is not searched (there is no telling a standstill from a game that has not begun); where the screen watch cannot follow the camera there is no place to stand at and nothing is searched; "about one spot" is measured from where the spot was entered, not from its middle.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. `find_way(stood=True)`, scripted: where the plain way stays alive and gets nowhere new, the small changes to the plain way are tried from its start forwards with every hold played out whole, each blind first and asked for the screen it ends on; one that ends on the screen the plain way ended on, or on the screen of an earlier change that was looked at and got nowhere, is not looked at; the first that reaches new ground under the watch is the way, with every play counted. The same game without `stood` goes on to the changes to what it did, as before, and no play is asked for its screen.
  2. `find_way(stood=True)`: a plain way that gets on is the way, in two plays as before; where no change to the plain way gets on, the changes to what it did are tried, the plain way's changes with half the tries, and nothing is played twice; with a plain way that loses a life, or none, there is no screen of standing still and every change that stays alive is looked at; `stood` must be true or false. `play(..., end=True)` gives the screen after the last move (none where a life went first), the same for moves that come to the same, and is no part of what two outcomes are compared by; a watch is still shown its own looks only.
  3. `Moments.since(step)`: the newest moment at or before the step with the moves made since it; the oldest kept where every moment is later; nothing where none is kept; a step that is no whole number is refused.
  4. A go on the practice game that only walks right stands at the first wall for 60 steps, then in one step looks, goes back to a moment from before it came there and plays the way found without asking the learner: it is over the wall with every life, having stood against it for at most 4 more steps. The record counts the search with the others and apart, and the log says in plain words that it stayed about one spot, how far it went back and what the way is.
  5. The next go is over that wall from memory: no search, no going back, at most 4 steps against the wall.
  6. No standstill: a go that paces to and fro over old ground, further than 64 pixels each way, is not searched in 300 steps; a go that has never counted new ground is not searched, and is once it has. Pacing inside 64 pixels and jumping on the spot are standstills.
  7. A search at a standstill that finds nothing puts the game back where it was, keeps the go's moments, and is not made again at that spot however long the go stands there; it is at another spot. After as many in a row with nothing as it is told to give up after (three in the test, eight from the service) the runner makes no more of them, in later goes too, and the log says so once; told no number it never stops; a way found in between starts the count again; going back after a life lost is not stopped by it.
  8. Nothing is searched, saved or loaded with going back switched off, without saved moments, without a screen watch, or with a watch that cannot follow the camera; with all of them the same go is searched.
  9. A go about to end "stuck" at a standstill looks first, before 60 steps are up; a way found is played and the go goes on; with none found it ends stuck as before, with its moments.
  10. A way a search has found is played to its end before the go may end for its length: a go four steps longer than it takes to walk into the first gap ends only after every move of the way across, the way is remembered, and the next go is across from memory with its own steps unused. A go that finds no way ends at its length as before.
  11. The go's record counts the searches made at a standstill (`ways_stood`), is saved and read back with it, and a record saved before reads as none; the go's line and the bench's line say how many, and with none their words are what they were.
  12. In training, behind the real services, with a brain that only walks right and goes of 150 steps: the second go stands at the wall, finds the way on and is over it; the third does not stand there and gets further; every life lost on the way is got back.
  13. The switches: the runner looks only with `stand_after` above 0 (nonsense refused); the service passes 60 where the go can go back, says so once, after the line on what it remembers, and passes 0 and says nothing with `stand_after=0`, with going back off, or without save states; the bench's `stand=False` and `--no-standstill` say so in its first line. A standstill search may make twice the plays of one after a life lost.
  14. Measured on the bench: the simple table, twelve goes of 300 steps on level 0, and the neural network, 40 goes of 700 steps on levels 0 and 3, set against T-1016's figures. The figures go in the results whatever they are.
  15. `changes(..., early=True)` lists the same places as the usual list, the shortest hold first and within a hold from the first place forwards. `Change.apply(..., whole=True)` plays a hold out past the end of the trace and carries on after it, and is the same as without for a hold that fits; `changes(..., whole=True)` lists every hold at every place, where the usual list drops those the trace's end makes the same. Anything but true or false is refused for either.
  16. `find_way(..., enough=...)` asks it of every try that stayed alive on new ground and of no other, and a try it says no to is not the way; with nobody asking, past the place is enough, as before; something that cannot be called is refused. A watched try says where the watch last had the AI (`Outcome.spot`), an unwatched one cannot, and it is no part of what two outcomes are compared by. At a standstill the runner asks that the try ended more than 64 pixels from where the go came to stand, either way or up or down (129 pixels each way are "about the spot"), and says no to a try that was not watched; after a life lost it asks nothing.
  17. The bench counts a death that had begun when its go ended, with the life not gone, apart from the falls and walkers the eyes are asked to explain, and says how many in its "Deaths" line (nothing more than before where there are none). In T-1016's run of three goes every life that went is put down to its cause. The bench's short run with the search on gets further than without in every go, and over the first wall by the fifth.

Now the goes get to 633, 1,285, 1,825, 1,836, 1,977, 2,244 and then to the flag (2,477) in every go from the seventh; 9 levels finished, in 6 goes, each before any life was lost. It stood still 8 times and a way on was found all 8 times, in 0.4 to 1.2 seconds each; of 34 searches in all, 32 found a way (94%). **The bench's short run (five goes of 80 steps):** 37, 73, 192, 192 and 421 without the search; 160, 421, 441, 884 and 1,004 with it, over the first wall, with a way found in all five searches. **The neural network, 40 goes of 700 steps (T-1016's figures in brackets; without the search the run is the same run, so those are the comparison).** Level 0: 153 levels finished (160); at the flag from go 4 (3), a level finished in 37 goes (38); lives lost a go 2.50 in the first ten and 1.20 in the last (2.50, 1.30); it stood still 10 times and a way on was found 7 times; the camera measured right in 82% of its moves (84%), the ground counted right in 0% of the goes (2%), 100% of deaths explained (99%). Level 3: 141 levels finished (75); at the flag from go 4 (3), in 37 goes (38); lives lost a go 2.60 then 1.30 (2.30, 0.80); it stood still 20 times and a way on was found 8 times, the longest search 10.6 seconds; camera 78% (82%), ground 10% (0%), 98% explained (99%). So for the network: nearly twice the levels on level 3, a few fewer on level 0, a go later to the first flag on both, and more lives lost a go on level 3 while it plays about twice as many levels in a go. One run each, and they swing: an earlier cut of this task, different only in how the way over a wall was found, measured 229 and 65 levels on the same two runs. The network seldom stands still (10 and 20 times in 40 goes), so most of the difference is what the goes did afterwards, not the searches themselves. The eyes' two weak measures (camera, ground) are where they were and stay the tasks after next. **A brain that only walks right, behind the real services, six goes of 150 steps:** 633, 1,044, 1,412 and 1,833, each over a wall or a gap more than the last, with every life got back; then 1,843 twice. In the fifth go it loses a life to the third walker 14 steps after the remembered way ends (12 of them the dying pause), the search finds no way past in 109 tries, and a brain that never varies does the same again in the sixth. The earlier cut, with other timing at that walker, reached the flag in its sixth go. That limit is not this task's and is the next task (below).

- **Completion report:** A wall no longer ends a go's progress: the AI notices by where it sees itself that it is getting no further, goes back to before it came there, and finds the way on, usually in about a second; the way has no waiting in it and the next go plays it from memory. What took the time was not the idea but what the first measurements showed about it: ways full of waiting, hops taken for ways, nothing found near a level's start, a give-up rule that would have switched it off in a brain's first goes, and a bench that counted deaths which cost no life. Each was found by reading what the searches actually did, not by the totals, and each is fixed and tested. For the simple table the gain is plain (the flag three goes sooner, and no go spent at a wall). For the neural network one run a level cannot show a gain or a loss, and the write-up says so. **Left for the next tasks, in this order:** (1) a try counts as alive while its life has not gone, so a way a search finds can end in the dying pause of the next gap, and a remembered way can end two steps before a touch that cannot be avoided any more: seen here in the bench's three-go run (two ways ending in a gap) and in the walk-right trial (the same life lost go after go); (2) a clock taken for progress pays for standing still; (3) the camera's move from the AI's own position in memory; (4) the ground count.


### T-1017 – The camera's move near a thing that moves: tried, measured, not built
- **Status:** Closed, not built
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 2; the bench's line on the camera, 84% and 82% of moves measured right against a target of 90; named as next in T-1016's report.)
- **The idea:** the camera's move between two looks is the shift under which the most of the new screen equals the old one. Since T-1016 the kinds seen to move are known by their colours before that is measured, so their patches could be left out of the vote, and given their say back when they are all that changed.
- **Where the measure goes wrong, counted first (practice level 0, twelve goes of 300 steps, the simple table, as merged in T-1016):** of 4,214 looks in which the camera moved, 328 were measured wrong. 243 of them (74%) with a walker in view and nothing else that tells: plain ground either side, the coin there already collected. 77 (23%) with a walker and an edge of scenery both in view, mostly an edge about to leave the screen. 8 with no walker at all. The mistake is the walker's own 4 pixels a look, one way or the other.
- **What was built and measured:** the patches of kinds known to move, on the new screen and where the tracks of those kinds were on the old one, were given no say unless nothing else changed. The same twelve goes: the camera's move measured right in **76%** of looks (92% without it). Two causes. (a) A kind is "seen to move" by a patch that stood elsewhere a look ago *as the camera's move was measured*: when that measure is wrong, a piece of scenery no bigger than a thing (a short stretch of ground between two gaps, a wall) passes for a mover, and its kind is then known by its colours. Seeing such a piece as a thing does no harm (T-1016), but leaving it out of the vote takes away exactly the edges that tell the camera's move: 524 looks with only scenery in view went wrong where one had before. This is what T-992 warned of, and T-1016's check does not escape it, because the check itself rests on the measure. (b) With the walker left out, what is left to tell is often one small thing, and the rule that one small thing changing is no camera move (T-992, needed for a thing that moves on a still screen) then reads the camera as still: 229 looks measured 0 where the walker's vote had at least come within 4 pixels.
- **What the picture can and cannot say:** with a walker and nothing else in view, the screen shows one thing moving against nothing: one number (how far it moved on the screen) for two unknowns (the camera's move and its own). No rule on the picture alone can settle the 74%. Without them the target of 90% is out of reach whatever is done about the rest (it would come to about 94% in the twelve-go run and under 90% in the long runs).
- **What would settle it (not built, for a later task):** something that is not the picture. The AI already has a guess at its own position in memory; the change in that between two looks, less its own move on the screen, is the camera's move. The guess is sometimes wrong (the bench's line on memory says when), so it would have to prove itself first: agree with the picture's measure over the looks in which nothing known to move is in view, where the picture is right 99.7% of the time, and only then be taken where the picture's own evidence is only things known to move. And for the vote itself, a kind would lose its say only once it was seen to move on a screen where nothing else changed at all, which no wrong measure can fake.
- **Scope of what is merged:** no change to the app. Four tests that hold what the camera's measure does near a mover today, so a later change is made knowingly; this record.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. The idea is measured on the bench before it is kept, and is not kept if the camera's figure is worse. (It was worse; nothing of it is in `src/`.)
  2. Tests hold today's behaviour: a gap in view outvotes a walker; where only a walker tells, its move is taken for the camera's, with and without T-1016's seeing; a walker on a still screen is no camera move; a known kind standing still tells when nothing else does.
  3. The finding, the figures and what would settle it are written down here.
- **Expected changes:** `tests/unit/observation/test_tracking.py`, `TASK_TRACKER.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Test plan:** `tests/unit/observation/test_tracking.py`: `test_a_gap_in_view_outvotes_a_walker`, `test_where_only_a_walker_tells_its_move_is_taken_for_the_cameras`, `test_a_walker_on_a_still_screen_is_no_camera_move`, `test_a_known_kind_standing_still_tells_when_nothing_else_does` (2). The tests were first written for the change (a walker and a small sign in view, the walker left out); that one showed cause (b) before the bench did, and went with the change.
- **Results:** the tracker's tests 59 passed (55 before: the four new ones), ruff, format and mypy clean; `src/` is unchanged from T-1016, whose full run was 1,980 passed, 10 skipped. The measurements are above.
- **Commit:** see PR #261. **PR:** #261.
- **Completion report:** The fix named as next in T-1016 does not work, and measuring it before keeping it is what showed that: 92% down to 76%. The larger finding is that three quarters of the camera's mistakes cannot be put right from the picture at all, so the target for the camera, and with it the count of new ground on plain stretches, needs the AI's own position from memory, checked against the picture where the picture can tell. That is a task of its own and is not started; it changes nothing the person sees until the ground count is right, so the next task is the one that does show: goes that end at a wall (T-1018). **Still open, as before this task:** the camera's move measured right in 84% and 82% of looks on the two practice levels (target 90), and the ground counted to within a step in 2% and 0% of goes.


### T-1016 – A thing that moves is seen whole, and a life lost to it is put down to it
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 2, "it knows what the things on the screen are", measured by the bench's line on deaths; named as next in T-1015's report.)
- **What was found before any code, on practice level 0, twelve goes of 300 steps with the remembered way:** eleven lives were lost to a walker and none was put down to touching it; no kind was found to hurt. At the look in which the player touched the walker the watch had either no track near the player at all, or one or two slivers two to four pixels wide beside it. Two causes, both in how a thing standing on the ground is seen. (a) Such a thing is one patch with the ground on a still screen, so it is cut out by its motion: the pixels that differ from the look before. Of a thing drawn in flat colour that is only the edge it leads with (and the strip of backdrop it left behind, which has no kind): the walker, 14 pixels wide, was a sliver 4 wide, and with the player's own box left out of the picture the sliver next to the player was often gone too. (b) Where the walker is the only thing in view that can tell how far the camera moved (plain ground either side), the camera's measure takes the walker's move for the camera's own, nothing is left that moved, and the walker is not seen at all. A thing that stops moving is not seen either, for the same reason. The second cause is also why the camera's move is measured wrong there (84% of looks in T-1015's runs): that part is the next task; this one makes the thing seen regardless.
- **Objective:** in `observation/tracking.py`, a patch cut out of the scenery by its motion is filled out by its colours: the whole thing is what is drawn in the same colours and joined to the part that moved. It is taken only if it is no bigger than a thing may be (else its colours run on into the scenery, and the part that moved is all that can be told apart, as before), and only if it stood somewhere else a look ago: laid over the old screen it fits better a little way off than where it is now. That second check is what keeps scenery a thing walked in front of (a hill it uncovers a strip of) from being taken for the mover. A kind taken this way is remembered by its colours (at most 16 kinds, kept from go to go like the kinds themselves), and at every later look every patch in those colours that is no bigger than a thing is a thing of that kind, whether or not anything moved: so a walker stays seen when it stands still and when the camera's measure has swallowed its move, and another of its kind is known the moment it comes into view. (The try-out first found a thing again only near where its own track should be; the second walker of a level then went unseen, because by the time it was in view the camera's measure had already taken its move for its own and it was never seen to move at all. Knowing the kind fixes that.) What the caller hides (the player) is in no patch. `ObjectTracker(whole=False)` is the tracker as it was; the player finder uses that, because it compares paths between runs and a thing half off the screen's edge is a patch that grows or shrinks there.
- **Scope:** `observation/tracking.py`, `observation/objects.py` (one field), `understanding/player.py` (one argument), tests, the bench's test, the documents. **Out of scope (next tasks):** the camera's move where only a mover is in view; goes that end at a wall. **Known and left:** a thing that never moves and stands on the ground (spikes) is still not seen; a mover drawn in colours its ground also has is still seen only by its moving edge; the player finder does not use the new seeing.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. A flat-coloured thing walking on plain ground is one track with a kind whose box is its whole body at every look from the first it moves in; with `whole=False` no track is.
  2. It stays the same track, seen at every look, when it stops for longer than a track survives unseen; with `whole=False` it is lost.
  3. With the camera moving and nothing else in view to tell by, it is still seen where it is at every look. Another thing of a kind once seen to move is seen at once, standing still, also at the first look of the next go; a thing in other colours is not until it is seen to move; no more kinds are known this way than the tracker may keep.
  4. Scenery it walks in front of is not taken for a thing; the older test of a textured walker in front of hills passes unchanged.
  5. A mover in its ground's own colours is cut out exactly as before (the same tracks as `whole=False`).
  6. What the caller hides is not part of it: half behind the hidden box, its box is the part that shows.
  7. `whole` must be true or false; the player finder's tests pass unchanged.
  8. In the watch, on plain ground with the camera moving: the player touches a walker, a life goes a few looks later, and the life is put down to the touch; the walker's kind is found to hurt and the brain is given where the nearest thing that hurts is. Seen the old way, the same go puts nothing down to it.
  9. On the bench, a run that loses lives to walkers puts them down to touching (all but at most one, which a run's end can cut off) and finds a kind that hurts; measured on both practice levels over 40 goes, whatever the figures are.
- **Expected changes:** `observation/tracking.py`, `observation/objects.py`, `understanding/player.py`, `tests/unit/observation/test_tracking.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_vision.py`, `tests/integration/test_practice_bench.py`, `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `TASK_TRACKER.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Test plan:** written before the code was finished (a try-out of the idea came first, to find out whether it could work at all; it is described above). `tests/unit/observation/test_tracking.py`: `test_a_flat_coloured_walker_on_the_ground_is_seen_whole` (1), `test_it_is_still_seen_when_it_stops` (2), `test_it_is_still_seen_where_only_it_tells_the_cameras_move` and `test_another_of_its_kind_is_known_the_moment_it_is_in_view` (3), `test_scenery_walked_in_front_of_is_not_the_mover` (4), `test_colours_that_run_on_into_the_scenery_are_not_filled_out` (5), `test_what_is_hidden_is_no_part_of_it` (6), `test_whole_must_be_true_or_false` (7). `tests/unit/training/test_vision.py`: `test_a_life_lost_to_a_walker_on_the_ground_is_put_down_to_it` (8). `tests/integration/test_practice_bench.py`: `test_lives_lost_to_a_walker_are_put_down_to_it` (9). Regression: the whole suite, with the tracker's, the watch's and the player finder's existing tests unchanged.
- **Results:** full suite 1,980 passed, 10 skipped (1,970 before: eight new tests of the tracker, one of the watch, one of the bench), ruff, format and mypy clean; no existing test was changed. A look costs about a millisecond more with two kinds known (14.7 ms to 15.7 ms on the test screens). **Measured, 40 goes of 700 steps of their own, the neural network, as the app now is.** Level 0: 145 lives lost, 96 by falling and 49 to a walker; the eyes put 94 down to a fall and 49 to touching something: 99% explained (70% before, with none of 28 walker deaths put down to a touch), and one kind found to hurt (none before). Level 3: 69 lives lost, 54 falls and 15 walkers; 54 put down to a fall and 14 to a touch: 99% (79% before, none of 17). Itself followed in 99% of looks and the floor read right in 100% on both, as before. The camera's move is measured right in 84% and 82% of the looks in which it moved (84% and 84% before; target 90): unchanged, and the next task. The ground counted is the game's own to within a step in 2% and 0% of goes (38% and 0% before): it follows from the camera's measure and from how far the goes now get, on level 0 up to eight levels in a go where it was three. **And the learner, which is now told where the nearest thing that hurts is:** level 0 is finished from the third go on (the sixth before), in 38 of the 40 goes, every one before any life was lost, 160 levels in all (92 before); level 3 from the third go on, in 38 of 40, every one before any life was lost, 75 levels in all (98 before). Lives lost a go, first ten goes then last ten: 2.50 then 1.30, and 2.30 then 0.80 (2.20 then 0.80, and 2.60 then 0.70, before); those are lost in the levels played over again beyond the flag. A twelve-go run with the simple table on level 0 got to the flag in its tenth go where it had in its sixth: goes five to eight ended at the wall at 2,264, which is the task after next.
- **Commit:** see PR #260. **PR:** #260.
- **Completion report:** The eyes now see a walking enemy as a thing. The cause was not in the blaming, which was sound, but one step earlier: a thing that stands on the ground was only ever seen by the pixels that changed, and of a thing in flat colour that is a sliver, or nothing where the camera's measure swallows its move. Three parts make the fix, each general and none about any game: the part that moved is filled out by its colours; the filled patch is taken only if it really stood elsewhere a look ago, which is what tells a mover from scenery it walked in front of; and a kind once taken is known by its colours from then on, wherever it is and whether it moves. The third part was not in the first try-out and came from measuring it: the second walker of a level was never seen to move at all. **Known and left:** the camera's move is still misjudged where only a mover is in view, and with it the ground counted (next task: now that movers are known by their colours they can be told from scenery before the camera's move is measured); a thing that never moves and stands on the ground is not seen; a mover in its ground's colours is seen only by its moving edge; a mover half off the screen's edge is a patch that grows or shrinks there, which is why the player finder keeps the old seeing; a piece of scenery no bigger than a thing can be taken for a mover while the camera's measure is wrong, and is then a thing that stands still, of a kind of its own; only the practice games are measured. Next: T-1017, the camera's move where only a thing that moves by itself is in view; then goes that end at a wall.


### T-1015 – The remembered way, switched on in training
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's "it practises where it dies", Stage 4 item 3; T-1014 built the runner's part and left it unused.)
- **What was found before any code, with the runner patched from a script outside the app (goes of 700 steps, 40 goes):** on practice level 0 the remembered way grows go by go, the level is finished in the seventh go and every go after it plays the level through without losing a life; on level 3 the way grows 498, 591, 641, 652, 661, 687 steps, the furthest reached goes from 2,152 in the first ten goes to 2,460 in the last ten and the lives lost a go from 0.20 to none. Without it the same goes averaged 989 and 1,106 and ended on game over. The try-out also showed the one thing in the service that works against it: two goes that begin by playing the same way look the same for their first steps, the service took that for a game that ignores the AI, and its remedy (make wherever the game is the new start) threw the level's start away.
- **Objective:** `TrainingService` keeps one `Route` for the connected game and passes it to each runner it builds where the runner goes back (save states and `ways_per_go` above 0), so the way outlives a runner being rebuilt (a brain promoted, a setting changed). A go that began with steps from memory is not compared with the go before it for "the game ignores the AI", and is not kept for comparing with the next: goes that begin with the same way begin alike by design. The direct question to the game (asked at the first go after Start and after a go that ends stuck or by a reset) and "stuck from its first step" stay as they are. The way is forgotten when the person starts the AI from scratch, and with a new connection; a start that moves is already a way forgotten (T-1014), and the log now says so. The go's line in the log says how many steps it began with from memory, and the line that says the AI goes back says it remembers too. The practice bench counts a level finished in every go that finishes one (it counted only the first, because it read the level before the go was put back to its start) and says in how many goes the level was finished before any life was lost.
- **Found while switching it on, and part of this task:** a remembered way used up the go. With the simple table on the practice game (150 steps a go) the first go wandered to the first gap in 143 steps, and every go after it played those 143 steps again and had 7 steps of its own left: it never got any further. In the app a go is 600 steps, and a level takes more than that. So the steps a go plays from memory no longer count towards its length: `EpisodeRunner.own_steps`, and `max_steps` is counted in those.
- **Also found while switching it on:** with the way remembered the simple table gets three times as far into practice level 3 in twelve goes of 200 steps (1,587 of 2,496 by the twelfth; it got to about 600 before), and three older tests of the eyes, which run exactly those twelve goes, failed: they were written for goes that stay on the first screens of the level and never meet a walker. Further in, the eyes have gaps that were already there and already showed in every long run of the bench (T-1013's runs without any remembered way: the camera's move measured right in 80 to 89% of looks against a target of 90, the ground counted to within a step in 20 to 38% of goes against 90, lives lost to a walker put down to touching it in 0 to 6 of 33 to 58). Where only a walker is in view (flat ground, plain sky: level 3 from about 640 to 750) nothing on the screen but the walker says how far the camera moved, and the measure is off by the walker's own 4 pixels: 254 of the 274 looks there were wrong. That is the eyes' work, not this task's, and it is next (T-1016). So that the three tests go on measuring the goes they were written for, the service and the bench get a switch, `remember=False`, and those three runs use it; nothing they assert is changed.
- **And the practice racing game showed the measure was wrong** (`tests/integration/test_first_demonstration.py`, six learner seeds, two sets of rewards each, failed on the first full run). (a) With every reward that pays switched off (the careful child: only crashing costs), the AI still kept the way that covered the most new ground, played it every go and then sat still: all of one seed's last 23 goes were the same 27 steps and a standstill. The way overrode the person's rewards. (b) With the usual rewards, on another seed, the furthest way was 11 steps into a spot the brain could do nothing from: 24 goes in a row ended "stuck" there with nothing paid, where without any memory the same seed settles on +43.5 a go. Getting far is not what that game pays for, and the eyes count hardly any ground on it. So the way is now measured by what the go was paid (the person's rewards added up; pay for steps gone back over is taken out), kept up to the step it had been paid the most, and replaced by a go paid more; a go that played the whole way is compared with what the way was paid in that same go, because a reward paid once (a goal reached the first time) would otherwise set a mark no later go reaches. Nothing paid above zero, nothing remembered. (c) That alone left the second seed with a way that ended three steps before a crash it found no way past, every go. A loss that stands already ends the go's own story 30 steps before it (T-1014); the same now goes for the way, when the life went within 30 steps behind the way's end.
- **Scope:** `training/route.py` (the measure), `training/service.py`, `training/episode.py` (the go's length counted in its own steps, a standing loss cuts the way, two log lines), `tools/practice_bench.py`, the README. **Out of scope (later tasks):** goes that end at a wall with no life lost, tidying a remembered way, keeping it between sessions, the bench's default of 300 steps a go.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. In training on the practice game, with save states: a go that goes back and gets across the first gap leaves a way, and the next go begins by playing it: its record counts the steps, the learner is not asked for them, and it is across the gap with every life and no search.
  2. Two goes that begin from memory and look the same for their first steps do not make the service wake the game or move the start: the checkpoint is not taken again. Two goes with nothing remembered that look the same still do, as before.
  3. The way outlives the runner being rebuilt; starting the AI from scratch forgets it; a console without save states, or going back switched off, has no route and trains as before.
  4. When the start moves the way is forgotten and the log says so in plain words, once.
  5. The go's line in the log says how many steps it began with from memory (nothing where it did not), and the line about going back says the AI remembers its furthest way.
  6. The bench counts a level finished in each go that finishes one and says in how many of them no life was lost first; a go that finishes none counts none.
  7. Measured: 40 goes of 700 steps on levels 0 and 3, set against the same without it (989 and 1,106 on average, goes ending on game over). The figures go in the results whatever they are.
  8. The steps a go plays from memory do not count towards its length: a way longer than a go is played to its end, the go then has its whole length of its own steps, and its record counts them all. A go with nothing from memory is as long as before.
  9. `TrainingService(remember=False)` and the bench's `remember=False` (`--no-memory`) train without the remembered way, exactly as before this task: no route, nothing said about one, the bench's first line says so; anything but True or False is refused. In the bench, a go that finishes a level carries the camera's travel over into the next for its own count of the ground.
  10. The way is the best-paid go: `Route` keeps the story up to its highest running total of pay, replaces the way only for more, measures a go that played the whole way against that go's own total at the way's end, and keeps nothing where nothing was paid above zero. In training with every paying reward switched off, nothing is remembered. T-1014's tests of the bookkeeping hold with pay in the place of ground; the one change to them is that a fraction and a negative amount are no longer refused (pay can be both), while anything that is not a number still is.
  11. A life lost that the go does not get back, within 30 steps behind the end of the way it began with, cuts the way to 30 steps before the loss and the log says so; further behind, or once the go has left the way, or once its story is over, nothing is cut. The first demonstration on the racing game passes unchanged.
- **Expected changes:** `training/route.py`, `training/service.py`, `training/episode.py`, `tools/practice_bench.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_route.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_remembered_way_in_training.py` (new), `tests/unit/training/test_remembered_way.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_service.py` (one more line left out of a list of lines that are not about the brain), `tests/integration/test_practice_bench.py`, `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `TASK_TRACKER.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Test plan:** written before the code. `tests/unit/training/test_remembered_way_in_training.py`, on the practice game behind the real services: `test_the_next_go_in_training_begins_with_the_way` (1), `test_goes_that_begin_from_memory_are_not_a_game_that_ignores_the_ai` and `test_goes_with_nothing_remembered_are_still_compared` (2), `test_the_way_outlives_the_runner_and_is_forgotten_from_scratch` and `test_no_route_without_save_states_or_with_going_back_off` (3), `test_a_start_that_moves_forgets_the_way_and_says_so` (4), `test_the_log_says_what_it_began_with` (5). `tests/integration/test_practice_bench.py`: `test_every_go_that_finishes_a_level_is_counted` (6). `tests/unit/training/test_remembered_way.py`: `test_the_steps_from_memory_do_not_count_towards_the_gos_length` (8). The switch (9): the third case of `test_no_route_without_save_states_or_with_going_back_off`, and `--no-memory` in `test_the_command_line`. The measure (10): in `tests/unit/training/test_route.py`, `test_the_way_is_the_best_paid_go_up_to_where_it_was_paid_the_most` and `test_a_go_that_played_the_whole_way_is_measured_against_this_go`; in training, `test_nothing_is_remembered_that_the_rewards_do_not_pay_for`. The cut (11): `test_a_loss_close_behind_the_way_cuts_it_only_while_the_go_is_still_on_it` (bookkeeping), `test_a_life_lost_close_behind_the_way_with_no_way_past_cuts_it` (runner), and `tests/integration/test_first_demonstration.py` as it stands. Then the measurement (7), the full suite, ruff, format, mypy.
- **Results:** full suite 1,970 passed, 10 skipped (1,954 before: sixteen new cases), ruff, format and mypy clean. **Measured, 40 goes of 700 steps of their own, the neural network, as the app now is.** Level 0: the end of the level is reached from the sixth go on, in 35 of the 40 goes, and in every one of them before any life was lost; the furthest reached averages 2,075 in the first ten goes and 2,481 (the flag) in the last ten; lives lost a go 2.20 then 0.80 (those are lost beyond the flag, in the level played over again); 92 levels finished in all, three a go by the end. Level 3: from the third go on, in 38 of 40, every one before any life was lost; 2,304 then 2,481; lives lost 2.60 then 0.70; 98 levels. Without the memory the same goes averaged 989 and 1,106 and ended on game over (T-1013's measurement). The simple table, twelve goes of 200 steps on level 0: the end of the level from the eighth go on (it never got beyond the first quarter). **The racing game** (`test_first_demonstration`, six seeds, both sets of rewards): passes unchanged; on the seed that froze, the point-lover's last ten goes average +41.2 against +43.5 without any memory, and the careful one, paid nothing above zero, remembers nothing and plays as before. **What is not right, and was not before:** the eyes further into a level. In the 40-go runs the camera's move is measured right in 84% of the looks in which it moved (target 90), the ground counted is the game's own to within a step in 38% and 0% of goes (target 90; over thousands of pixels the small errors add up), and of 28 and 17 lives lost to a walker none was put down to touching it (70% and 79% of deaths explained, target 80). Those figures were 80 to 89%, 20 to 38% and 0 to 6 before this task; they are the next work, not this task's. Tests: eight new of the service, ten cases (the next go begins with the way; goes that begin from memory are not a game that ignores the AI, and goes with nothing remembered still are; the way outlives the runner and is forgotten from scratch; no route without save states, with going back off or with the switch off; a start that moves; the log; nothing remembered that the rewards do not pay for), three new of the bookkeeping, two of the runner, one of the bench. **Existing tests changed, each for a stated reason and none loosened:** in `test_route.py` and `test_remembered_way.py` the measure's name (`ground` to `paid`) and the log's sentence ("did better" for "got further"), and in the list of nonsense `did` must refuse, a fraction and a negative amount were taken out (pay can be both) and a word, not-a-number and infinity put in; in `test_service.py` one more line added to a list of log lines that are not about the brain; in `test_practice_bench.py` the three runs of twelve goes on level 3 for the eyes (T-988, T-992, T-993) are made without the memory, so that they measure the goes they were written for. One new test of mine was wrong as first written (it expected the way kept from a go to be its whole story, where the design keeps it up to the last step that was paid for) and was corrected to the design. The bench itself was corrected in four places that only showed once goes got this far or went back in its short run: a level finished in every go that finishes one; the camera's travel carried over a finished level; a look after which the game was put back in the same step no longer counted as followed; and the first look after the game was put back, which it never compared, is now counted (`camera_skipped`), so that the test's sum of the looks compared is exact again (it was exact only for a run that never went back).
