- **Completion report:** The memory built in T-1014 is switched on, and it took three corrections to make it safe to switch on, each found by measuring rather than foreseen: a long way used up the whole go (the go's length now counts only its own steps); the furthest way was the wrong thing to remember on a game whose point is not getting far, and overrode the person's rewards where they pay for nothing (it is now the best-paid go, and nothing where nothing is paid); and a way that ended a few steps short of a loss with no way past brought every go to the same end (it is now cut back there). On the practice platform game the plan's first proof holds on two levels: the level is finished without losing a life, from the sixth and the third go on, by the neural network and by the simple table. Said plainly: (a) that is memory, not skill. The brain is taught the same steps each go and still loses lives once it is past the end of what it remembers; whether it comes to play the way by itself is not measured here. (b) It is one game. The second half of the plan's proof, a second game with no change to the code, has the racing game only as far as "does no harm"; the person's own game is not measured at all until a log of it arrives. (c) It relies on the game doing the same again from the same save with the same buttons. Where it does not, the cut after a life lost while playing the way is the remedy, and how often that happens on a real emulator is unknown. (d) The way is played from the level's start every go, at the speed of ordinary steps, so goes grow as long as the way; it is not kept when the app closes or when Start is pressed again; it keeps every detour of the go it came from. (e) A false "the game started over" during the way is repeated each go until the three-in-a-row rule stops reading it as one: three goes lost, seen once on the practice game. (f) The eyes' figures further into a level are below their targets, as above, and three tests of the eyes were held on the goes they were written for rather than on the new, further goes. That is the honest state: the tests still say what they said, and they do not yet say the eyes are right at the far end of a level. Next: T-1016, the camera's move where only a thing that moves by itself is in view; then lives lost to an enemy put down to it; then goes that end at a wall.


### T-1014 – The furthest way played is remembered and played again
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's "it practises where it dies", Stage 4 item 3, and what T-1011 to T-1013 each named as open: a way found does not last.)
- **What was found, with goes of 700 steps in place of the bench's 300:** on both practice levels the goes now end "stuck" on the game-over screen after six lives: three losses searched and got past, three more with no search left. Nothing found in one go helps the next, because the brain does not learn the jumps (T-1011) and a go may search only three times, so every go spends its three searches on the same first three places: 989 and 1,106 on average, best 1,809 and 1,616 of 2,496. A try-out outside the app (the runner patched from a script, nothing in the repository changed): the runner keeps the moves of the go that counted the most new ground, up to where it last got somewhere new, and the next go, which starts from the same saved spot, begins by playing them. On level 0 the remembered way grows 187, 342, 400, 407, 453 steps, the level is finished in the seventh go, and each of the 33 goes after it plays the whole level without losing a life. Played again from the same save the game does exactly the same, step for step. Two things the try-out ran into are part of this task and the next: a way that had stood still for 25 steps before pressing on ended the next go "stuck" when played again (level 3: every go after the first stopped at the first wall), and two goes that begin alike made the training service think the game was ignoring the AI (next task).
- **Objective:** a new `training/route.py` with `Route`: the bookkeeping only, no emulator. It holds the remembered way (moves, and the new ground counted after each) and the story of the go being played. `begin(start)` gives the moves to play first (none when `start` is None, and a way remembered from another start is forgotten); `did(move, ground)` adds a step (`move=None` is a step that cannot be played again: the story stops there); `went_back(steps)` drops the last steps of the story; `lost(lead)` ends the story `lead` steps before a loss that stands; `failed(lead)` cuts the remembered way `lead` steps before a life lost while it was being played; `end()` keeps the story, up to where it last counted new ground, if it counted more than the remembered way, and says whether it did. `EpisodeRunner(..., route=None)`: with a route, a screen watch and a go begun from the checkpoint, the go begins by playing the remembered way through the ordinary step (looked at, paid, learned from, the learner not asked), tells the route each step and each going back, and offers its story at the end. A list of moves being played is no longer ended by "nothing changes for 25 steps": the list goes on, and the standstill counts again once it is used up. The go's record says how many steps it began with from memory, and the log says when the remembered way grows.
- **Why moves and not a saved spot further on:** the proof the plan asks for is a level played from its start without losing a life, and only moves from the start are that. The moves also go through the learner each time, as practice on what works.
- **Scope:** `training/route.py`, `training/episode.py`, and in `services/experiments.py` the harness counting the checkpoints it has taken. **Out of scope (next task):** switching it on in the training service, forgetting the way when the service moves the spot goes start from, the service's check for a game that ignores the AI, the README, the measurement in training. **Later:** tidying a remembered way (it plays the standing about again too), keeping it between sessions.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. `Route` alone: the story kept is the moves up to the last step that counted new ground; it replaces the remembered way only if it counted more; `went_back`, `lost`, `failed` and a step that cannot be played again do what the objective says; a way from another start is forgotten; nonsense is refused.
  2. A go with a route and nothing remembered plays as before and leaves its way remembered: after walking into the first gap, going back and getting across, the remembered way is the moves that got across, without the steps that fell in.
  3. The next go begins by playing it: the learner is not asked for those steps, they are learned from like any step, the player is across the first gap with every life, and no search was needed.
  4. A go that gets further replaces the remembered way; one that does not leaves it as it was.
  5. A loss that stands ends the story before it: the remembered way stops short of the place and the next go arrives there alive.
  6. A life lost while the remembered way is being played cuts the way before that place, and the go carries on as any go would (it may go back and search).
  7. Without a route, without a watch, or begun without the checkpoint, nothing is remembered or played, and the runner is as it was. A step somebody else drove ends the story.
  8. A list of moves that stands still for longer than ends a go "stuck" is played to its end; a go standing still with no list still ends "stuck" as before. The go's record counts the steps it began with from memory, saves and reads them (an older record reads 0), and its line says so.
- **Expected changes:** `training/route.py` (new), `training/episode.py`, `services/experiments.py` (a count of the checkpoints taken, so a way knows the start it belongs to), `tests/unit/training/test_route.py` (new), `tests/unit/training/test_remembered_way.py` (new), `tests/unit/services/test_experiments.py`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `TASK_TRACKER.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Test plan:** written before the code. `tests/unit/training/test_route.py`: `test_the_story_is_kept_up_to_where_it_last_got_somewhere_new`, `test_only_a_story_that_got_further_replaces_the_way`, `test_going_back_and_a_loss_that_stands_shorten_the_story`, `test_a_life_lost_while_it_was_played_cuts_the_way`, `test_a_step_that_cannot_be_played_again_ends_the_story`, `test_another_start_forgets_the_way_and_nonsense_is_refused` (1). `tests/unit/training/test_remembered_way.py`, on the practice game behind the real services: `test_a_go_leaves_the_way_that_got_across` (2), `test_the_next_go_begins_with_it` (3), `test_only_a_go_that_gets_further_replaces_it` (4), `test_a_loss_that_stands_ends_the_way_before_it` (5), `test_a_life_lost_while_it_is_played_cuts_it` (6), `test_nothing_is_remembered_where_it_cannot_be_played_again` (7), `test_a_list_of_moves_is_not_ended_by_standing_still` and `test_the_record_counts_the_steps_from_memory` (8). Then the full suite, ruff, format, mypy.
- **Results:** full suite 1,954 passed, 10 skipped (1,939 before: six new tests of the bookkeeping, eight of the runner, one of the harness's count), ruff, format and mypy clean; no existing test was changed, the stuck rule's change included (no test had a queued list ended by a standstill). One more test than planned, `test_it_counts_the_checkpoints_taken`, for the count the harness now keeps. One of my new tests was wrong as first written and was corrected to what the runner does: I looked at what the learner had been taught straight after the way was played, but the last few steps of a go are learned when it ends (the lookahead), so the test now looks after `finish()` and states the count exactly. On the practice game behind the real services: a go that falls into the first gap, goes back and gets across leaves a way of 19 steps of walking, 4 of the jump and walking on, with none of the 36 steps that fell in; the next go plays it without asking the learner and is across with every life and its search unused; a way of forty steps of walking planted by hand is cut to six when the life goes on its 36th step, the go finds the real way and remembers that instead.
- **Commit:** see PR #258. **PR:** #258.
- **Completion report:** The runner can now remember the furthest way a go has played and begin the next go with it, with the rules for what may be remembered (only the AI's own moves, only from a saved start, never the steps into a loss) in a small module of their own. Said plainly: (a) nothing in the app uses it yet: the training service does not pass a route, so a build made from this task plays exactly as before; switching it on is the next task, with the measurement. (b) It is memory of one way through one start, not skill: the brain is taught the same steps again each go, and whether that makes it play them itself is not measured here. (c) The way keeps the standing about and the detours of the go it came from. (d) It relies on a game doing the same again from the same save with the same moves; where it does not, the life lost while playing it cuts it back and the go searches as before, which is tested, but how often that happens on a real emulator is not known. Next: T-1015, switch it on in training (pass a route where the runner goes back, do not take two goes that begin alike for a game that ignores the AI, say it in the go's line and the README) and measure both practice levels with goes long enough to finish.

### T-1013 – A life lost that reads as a restart is searched before the go ends
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (follow-up of T-1012, found in its measured runs.)
- **What was found:** on level 0, from the eighth go of 40 on, 19 goes end "reset" a little past x 400, where the first walker patrols, having lost two lives and gone back once. Followed step by step (every `_settle` and `_seek` of 14 goes written down): the second life is lost in the same step in which the engine reports a restart (the values it has by then learned to watch all return to their starting values, because the game puts the player back at the start of the level). `_settle` sets the go's end to "reset" and returns False, and `step()` returns before it reaches `_seek`: two searches are left unused. The first death of a go is searched because early in a go those values have not moved yet, and the first seven goes are searched because the engine has not yet learned them. So the better the engine knows the game, the less the AI goes back.
- **Objective:** in `EpisodeRunner`, a restart noticed in a step of the AI's own in which a life was also lost does not end the go at once where a search can follow (moments kept with one far enough back and marked, a search left this go, a screen watch, a life value known, and not the go's last step). The step is settled as before: counted, paid, learned as the end of that story. Then the search runs. A way found: the game is back before the loss and the go carries on. No way found: the go ends "reset", as it did, with the game put back to where it was. Everything else that ends a go is unchanged: a restart with no life lost, a restart where nothing can be searched, a step somebody else drove.
- **Scope:** `training/episode.py`, README. **Out of scope:** whether a way past the walker holds (T-1011 saw ways there end inside its beat; measured here, fixed in its own task if needed), walls, making ways last.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. A go that loses a life in a step that also reads as a restart, and can search, is not ended: it goes back, finds the way and gets across with its lives; the step of the loss was learned once, as final, with its penalty.
  2. With no way found the go ends "reset" in that same step, the search counted and the game where it was after the loss; the reset's detail is still what the log names.
  3. Where nothing can be searched the go ends "reset" as before and nothing is saved, loaded or searched: no moments, `ways_per_go=0`, the go's searches used up, the runner having given up, the go's last step.
  4. A restart with no life lost ends the go as before, whatever could be searched. A step somebody else drove is not held.
  5. A restart reported a step after the life went (the search already ran at the loss) is handled as before: after a way found there is none; with none found it ends the go.
  6. Measured, 40 goes on levels 0 and 3, against T-1012's figures: the goes of level 0 that end "reset" with searches unused (19), furthest reached (833 then 996, 745 over all; 826 then 704, 712 over all), and the racing game's first demonstration still holds with its assertions unchanged.
- **Expected changes:** `training/episode.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_restart_with_a_life_lost.py` (new), `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `TASK_TRACKER.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Test plan:** written before the code. `tests/unit/training/test_restart_with_a_life_lost.py`, on the practice game behind the real services, with a restart published on the bus in the step a life goes: `test_a_life_lost_that_reads_as_a_restart_is_searched_first` (1), `test_with_no_way_found_the_go_ends_as_a_restart` (2), `test_where_nothing_can_be_searched_it_ends_as_before` (3), `test_a_restart_with_no_life_lost_ends_the_go` and `test_a_step_somebody_else_drove_is_not_held` (4), `test_a_restart_a_step_after_the_loss` (5). Then the full suite, ruff, format, mypy, and the two 40-go runs (6).
- **Results:** full suite 1,939 passed, 10 skipped (1,933 before: six new tests), ruff, format and mypy clean; no existing test was changed, and the racing game's first demonstration holds on its six seeds with its assertions untouched. One of my new tests was wrong as first written and was corrected to what the game does, not loosened: I had the go, after its one search, running to its end "like any other"; it walks on into the first walker, loses a second life with nothing left to search with, and that restart ends it, which is criterion 3's "searches used up" and is now what the test states (it replaced a weaker, conditional check of the same thing in another test). Measured, 40 goes each, against T-1012: level 0, 3 goes end "reset" (19), and those three after a search that found nothing or with all three used; a way in 101 of 110 searches (75 of 78); furthest in the first ten goes then the last ten 1,020 then 936 (833 then 996), 950 over all 40 (745), best 1,317 (1,406), lives lost a go 0.10 then 0.30, 227 s (158: there is more to search now); level 3, 861 then 1,413 (826 then 704), 1,074 over all (712), best 2,020 of the 2,496 to the flag (1,020), a way in 88 of 95 (67 of 75), 188 s (191). One run each. 37 and 33 of the 40 goes end because the bench's 300 steps are up.
- **Commit:** see PR #257. **PR:** #257.
- **Completion report:** A life lost in the step the game is read as starting over is now searched before the go ends, and the go only ends there if no way is found. The first level's goes no longer stop at the first enemy, and both levels' averages are up by a quarter and a half. Said plainly: (a) nothing here makes the AI better at the enemy itself: the search gets it past, three times a go at most. (b) One run each, and the spread is wide. (c) What limits the runs now is mostly the bench: 300 steps a go is 2,400 pixels at the very best and the flag is at 2,496, so no go could finish however well it played. (d) On level 3 eight of the 40 goes still end at one of the two walls (452 and 996), where no life is lost and so nothing is searched. Next: let a practice go last long enough to finish, and treat getting nowhere at a wall like a life lost (go back, look for the way past); then making ways last.

### T-1012 – The search tries the plain way first
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (follow-up of T-1011, which named "the search cannot make a jump out of two-button moves" as the next thing.)
- **What was found, by writing down what each of the 179 searches of T-1011's two measured runs was given:** 54 found no way (23 of 88 on level 0, 31 of 91 on level 3). Only seven of those had mostly been holding "right + b". Most were given a wander: left for eleven steps and then a jump too early, a button held that does nothing, standing about. No single small change to a wander gets across a gap, and 33 of the 54 ran out of changes before they ran out of tries. Two fixes were measured on those 54 without changing the runs: (a) also exchanging one button for another (the fix T-1011 had in mind): finds a way in 14, some only after 140 to 300 tries; (b) forgetting what it did and holding "right" from the same save, cut where that loses the life, with the ordinary small changes: finds a way in 48, on try 14 to 52. Then (b) was tried on all 179: it finds a way in 154 (86%) where changing what it did finds 125 (70%), together 173 (97%), and it finds it sooner (median try 19 and 43 on the two levels, against 42 and 54). Tried first, with what it did second, the two levels would have cost 3,569 and 5,355 tries in place of 5,349 and 6,528. The 19 searches only "what it did" solves are where the plain walk stops at a wall it had jumped (alive, nothing new) or loses a life to something earlier that the go had got past.
- **Objective:** `find_way(..., plain=None)`. With `plain` (a move), the search begins with the plain way: that move held from the save for as long as the trace and the carry-on. Alive and on new ground, that is the way. If it loses a life at step k, the small changes of `ways.changes` are tried on k steps of the plain move, using at most half the budget. Alive but nowhere new, or nothing found in that half, the search goes on as before with small changes to what it did, with the tries that are left; moves already played are not played again and cost no try. `Way` says which it was (`plain`, and `lost_at`, the step the plain way lost the life). The runner passes the one-button move of its best-paid button (the same pick as pressing on, T-1011); with nothing paid yet, none. The log line of a way says how it was made.
- **Why not the exchange of buttons:** measured, it solves a quarter of what the plain way solves and costs three times the tries at every place; every search it solved the plain way solved too. It is set aside, not built.
- **Why the plain way first and not second:** it is the cheaper and the likelier of the two (above), and its cost when it fails is small: two tries at a wall, and never more than half the budget. What it did keeps the rest, and is what gets past where an earlier jump has to stay in.
- **Scope:** `training/search.py`, `training/episode.py`, README. **Out of scope:** making a way found last (next task), the walker on level 0, a real emulator's cost per try (not known until a log comes back), more than three searches a go.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. With `plain`, a plain way that stays alive and reaches new ground is the way, found in two tries, and nothing else is played.
  2. Where the plain way loses a life, the changes are tried on the plain moves up to that step; the way found is a change to those, says the move held and the step the life went at, and plays alive past the gap in the game itself.
  3. The plain way uses at most half the budget (the two plays of the plain way itself included). After it the search carries on with changes to what it did; a list of moves already played is skipped at no cost; the budget and the time limit hold over the whole search.
  4. A plain way alive but nowhere new (a wall) costs two tries and the search goes straight on to what it did.
  5. Given a wander (left, then a jump too early) at the first gap, changes to what it did find nothing and the search with `plain` finds the way within half the budget.
  6. Without `plain` every search is as it was (the existing tests of the search pass untouched); a plain move the controls do not have is refused, and so is a trace with such a move, before anything is played.
  7. The runner gives the search its best-paid button's own move, none while nothing has been paid, and the log says how the way was made. Measured, 40 goes on levels 0 and 3, against T-1011's figures (a way in 65 of 88 and 60 of 91 searches; 703 then 574 and 599 then 512), and the racing game's first demonstration still holds with its assertions unchanged.
- **Expected changes:** `training/search.py`, `training/episode.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_search_plain_first.py` (new), existing runner tests where the way found is now the plain one, `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `TASK_TRACKER.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Test plan:** written before the code. `tests/unit/training/test_search_plain_first.py`: with scripted tries, `test_a_plain_way_that_gets_on_is_the_way` (1), `test_where_the_plain_way_loses_the_life_its_changes_are_tried` (2), `test_the_plain_way_has_half_the_tries_and_nothing_is_played_twice` (3), `test_at_a_wall_it_goes_straight_on_to_what_it_did` (4), `test_the_time_limit_holds_over_both_parts` (3), `test_nonsense_is_refused_before_anything_is_played` (6); on the practice game itself, `test_the_plain_way_across_the_first_gap` (2) and `test_a_wander_before_the_gap_is_got_past` (5); on the runner, `test_the_runner_gives_its_best_paid_button` (7). The existing `test_search.py` untouched (6). Then the full suite, ruff, format, mypy, and the two 40-go runs (7).
- **Results:** full suite 1,933 passed, 10 skipped (1,923 before: ten new tests), ruff, format and mypy clean; `test_search.py` passes untouched, and the racing game's first demonstration holds on its six seeds with its assertions untouched. One more test than planned: `test_with_nothing_paid_yet_there_is_no_plain_way` (7), which also pins that the search and its log line are then exactly as before. Three existing tests in `test_search_at_a_loss.py` pin the play a way is found on and the sentence the log says; where the go walked plainly into the gap the same change is now found on play 19 instead of 18 (the plain way's own play comes first) and the sentence names the plain way, so the two constants they share were moved to that. Nothing else in them changed and no assertion was loosened. Two of my new tests were wrong as first written and were corrected to what the game does: I had the wander down as "mostly not walking right" (it is 35 of 58 steps right; the test now states the wander exactly), and I asked where the player was after the life went (it is back at the start by then; the test now looks one step before). One thing the tests' design found in the code before any ran: a change that stayed alive blind when the plain way's tries ran out had been marked as played without ever being looked at, so the second part would have skipped it; a play is now marked only once its fate is known. Measured, 40 goes each, against T-1011: level 0, a way in 75 of 78 searches (65 of 88), 3,350 tries in all (5,349), median try of a way 19 (42), furthest in the first ten goes then the last ten 833 then 996 (703 then 574), 745 over all 40 (605), best 1,406 (1,165), lives lost a go 0.30 then 0.70 (0.60 then 1.60), 158 s (202); level 3, 67 of 75 (60 of 91), 3,618 tries (6,528), median 43 (54), 826 then 704 (599 then 512), 712 over all (588), best 1,020 (1,179), no go short of the first gap (7), lives 0.50 then 0.40 (0.90 then 0.90), 191 s (285). ### T-1011 – A brain turned timid presses on
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (follow-up of T-1010: on the gaps level the last ten of 40 goes were no better than the first, 212 against 417, with many goes ended standing still.)
- **What was found, by recording every choice of the brain over 40 goes on level 3:** from go 22 on it stops a few steps short of the first gap and waits or dithers (the moves it rates best there are "nothing", "b", "b + up", "b + down"). The cause is in what it has learned, and is sound arithmetic: a step of waiting is worth 0.99 of what the place is worth (the discount), going on has cost a life there more often than not (-7.5 against +1 a step of new ground), and its own jump is unreliable, so waiting rates highest by a hair and, the situation not changing, is chosen again for ever. A timid brain loses no life, so nothing is searched and nothing new is learned. Three things were tried before this task was written: (a) never repeating a move that changed nothing: it dithers instead of standing (258 then 306 on level 3), set aside; (b) 60 goes of practice from a spot 88 pixels before the first gap, with the search on (51 ways found): the share of goes that cross falls from 8 in 10 to 0 to 4 in 10, so more practice at the spot does not teach this brain the jump, which has to start within about 10 pixels of the edge and be held six steps; (c) pressing on, below: 236 then 905 on level 3.
- **Objective:** `EpisodeRunner(..., press_after=0, press_for=PRESS_FOR)`. The runner counts the steps since anything was paid, and keeps, over its goes, what each button has been paid (every button of a paid move gets the pay). When `press_after` steps have paid nothing, no list of moves is being played, and the go can still go back (it keeps moments and has a search left), it plays the one-button move of the best-paid button for `press_for` steps without asking the learner. A press that was paid nothing and cost no life is followed, next time, by the next-best-paid button; any pay starts again from the best. The training service passes `press_after=PRESS_AFTER` (24, one short of the 25 unchanged steps that end a go "stuck") wherever its runner goes back. The go's record counts the presses and the go's line says so; the first press of a runner says in the log what it is doing and why.
- **Why only where it can go back:** pressing on walks into what the brain was avoiding. With a search to follow, the life lost there is how the way past is found (T-1007) and the go carries on beyond; without one it would only cost lives.
- **Scope:** `training/episode.py`, `training/service.py`, README. **Out of scope:** the search finding no way from a trace of two-button moves (a jump cannot be made of "b + right" by holding one button more: seen on level 0, own task next), the walker on level 0 that the ways found do not get clear of, turning ways into lasting skill of the brain, a wall (pressing on changes nothing there and the go ends stuck as before).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. A go that has walked a little and then stands still presses on after `press_after` unpaid steps: the next `press_for` moves are the best-paid button's, the learner is not asked for them, and they are learned from like any step.
  2. Pressed on into the first gap of the practice game, the go loses the life, goes back, finds the way and gets across with its lives.
  3. It does not press on where it cannot go back: with no moments, with `ways_per_go=0`, once the go's searches are used up, and once the runner has given up going back. `press_after=0` switches it off. Such a go ends "stuck" as before. Where it can go back, a go about to end "stuck" presses on first, whatever the count of unpaid steps says (the last pay can come a step or two after the last change, and the go ended one step before the press was due), once for each standstill; a press that changes nothing leaves the go stuck as before.
  4. Pay starts the count again: a go that keeps being paid is never pressed on. A list of moves being played (a way) is not interrupted.
  5. A press that was paid nothing and lost no life is followed by the next-best-paid button; after any pay the best is used again. A button with no move of its own is passed over; with nothing paid yet there is nothing to press.
  6. Nonsense is refused with a `ConfigurationError`; the go's record counts the presses, saves and reads them (an older record reads as 0), and the go's line says ", pressed on N times".
  7. Through the training service: on a console with save states the runner presses on after 24 steps; without save states, or with going back switched off, never.
  8. Measured, 40 goes on levels 0 and 3, against T-1010's figures (410 then 440, and 417 then 212), and the racing game's first demonstration still holds with its assertions unchanged.
- **Expected changes:** `training/episode.py`, `training/service.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_pressing_on.py` (new), `tests/unit/training/test_going_back_in_training.py`, `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `TASK_TRACKER.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Test plan:** written before the code. `tests/unit/training/test_pressing_on.py`, on the practice game behind the real services: `test_a_go_paid_nothing_presses_on_with_the_best_paid_button` (1), `test_pressed_on_into_the_gap_it_goes_back_and_gets_across` (2), `test_it_does_not_press_on_where_it_cannot_go_back` and `test_a_go_about_to_end_stuck_presses_on_first_once` (3), `test_pay_starts_the_count_again_and_a_way_is_not_interrupted` (4), `test_a_press_that_got_nothing_is_followed_by_the_next_best_button` (5), `test_nonsense_is_refused_and_the_record_counts_the_presses` (6). In `test_going_back_in_training.py`: `test_training_presses_on_where_it_goes_back` (7). Then the full suite, ruff, format, mypy, and the two 40-go runs (8).
- **Results:** full suite 1,923 passed, 10 skipped (1,915 before: seven new tests of the runner and one of the service), ruff, format and mypy clean; the racing game's first demonstration holds on its six seeds with its assertions untouched. Three of my new tests were wrong as first written and were corrected to what the game does, not loosened: pay does not come "every step or two" while walking (there are five unpaid steps where the measure of progress changes over, and twelve while falling and dying), so the tests' `press_after` is 8 or 13 instead of 5; a way across the first gap carries the player on into the walker's beat, where standing still costs a life, so the test of the gap no longer claims the go ends with every life; and the test lab's brain is told its place in wide steps, so a go pottering about one spot ends "stuck" there. One thing the tests found in the code: a brain standing still was ended as "stuck" one step before its press was due, which is why a go about to end stuck now presses on first (criterion 3). Measured, 40 goes each, furthest reached in the first ten then the last ten: level 3, 599 then 512, all 40 on average 588, best 1,179, 7 goes short of the first gap, lives lost a go 0.90 then 0.90, a way in 60 of 91 searches, 303 s (T-1010: 417 then 212, 392, 1,197, 21 goes, 0.90 then 0.20, 32 of 56, 389 s); level 0, 703 then 574, 605 on average, best 1,165, lives lost 0.60 then 1.60, a way in 65 of 88, 217 s (T-1010: 410 then 440, 463, 912, 0.80 then 0.50, 40 of 64, 470 s). One run each: two earlier runs of a first version gave 522 then 857 and 620 then 435, so the spread between runs is wide and the firm part is that the late goes no longer collapse.
- **Commit:** see PR #255. **PR:** #255.
- **Completion report:** A go that is paid nothing for 24 steps, or is about to end stuck, now presses on with its best-paid button where it can go back, and the life that may cost is searched for a way past. On the gaps level the late goes reach two and a half times as far as before and two thirds fewer goes stop short of the first gap. Said plainly: (a) this goes round the brain, it does not teach it. The brain still does not learn the jump (60 goes of practice at one gap made it worse, not better), so every go finds the same ways again by searching; making a way found last is the next thing, and is where "practise where it dies" in the plan belongs. (b) It costs lives, about one a go; that is what it is for where a search follows, and why it is not done where none can. (c) Later goes are still no better than early ones; they are no longer worse. (d) Found on the way and not fixed here: the search cannot make a jump out of two-button moves; a way past the walker on level 0 ends inside its beat; five steps without pay where the measure of progress changes over; the AI takes scenery for itself when the camera already follows the player at its first look. Next: the search and two-button moves (it is small and costs level 0 its first search of every go), then making ways last.

- **Status:** Done

The go's line in the log says how often it went back and what it found, and one line when training first builds such a runner says that it will. ### T-1009 – Going back gives up in a game where it finds nothing
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (step 6 of working out a way past where it died. Switching the search on in training was started as this task and set aside as a patch, because the racing practice game showed what it costs where it does not work. Measured there over six learner seeds, two trainings of 30 goes each: about 270 searches, 11 found a way (4%, against 24 of 31 on the platform game), and the runs took five times as long. The reason is in the game, not the search: a way past is told by new ground, and on that game the eyes count hardly any. How much ground the go had counted when the life went does not tell the two games apart (0 to 8 steps and more on the racing game, 7 and more on the platform game), so the search cannot know beforehand. What does tell them apart is what the searches come to.)
- **Objective:** `EpisodeRunner(..., give_up_after=None)`. The runner counts the searches that found no way, in a row and across its goes; a way found starts the count again. When the count reaches `give_up_after` the runner has given up: for as long as it lives it makes no more searches and saves no more moments, its goes run as they did before going back existed, and the log says so once. `gave_up` tells.
- **Scope:** `training/episode.py`. **Out of scope:** switching it on in training (next task, with the patch set aside), a better test of having got past for games where the eyes count no ground, starting to search again later.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. With `give_up_after=3`, the third search in a row that finds nothing is the last: `gave_up` is true, the rest of that go and every later go of that runner make no search and no save, and their results count none.
  2. The count runs across goes, and a way found starts it again: nothing, a way, nothing is not three in a row.
  3. A search that ran out of time counts as one that found nothing. One that ended with the link dropping is not counted.
  4. The log says it once, in plain words, with the number.
  5. Without `give_up_after` a runner never gives up. Nonsense is refused with a `ConfigurationError`: zero, a negative number, not a whole number.
- **Expected changes:** `training/episode.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_search_at_a_loss.py`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `TASK_TRACKER.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Test plan:** written before the code, in `test_search_at_a_loss.py` on the practice game: `test_it_gives_up_when_searches_keep_finding_nothing` (1, 4), `test_a_way_found_starts_the_count_again` (2, 3), `test_it_never_gives_up_unless_told_when` (5), and nonsense added to `test_nonsense_is_refused` (5). Then the full suite, ruff, format, mypy.
- **Results:** 5/5. `tests/unit/training/test_search_at_a_loss.py`, 14 tests now, on the practice game through the real services. (1, 4) `test_it_gives_up_when_searches_keep_finding_nothing` (two searches for nothing in one go and a third in the next: `gave_up`; the second fall of that go and the whole of the go after make no search, no save and no load; the results count 2, 1 and 0 searches; the log line once, word for word); (2, 3) `test_a_way_found_starts_the_count_again` (five goes with the search's outcome scripted: nothing, a way, out of time, the link dropping, nothing; only the last gives up); (5) `test_it_never_gives_up_unless_told_when` (six goes of searches for nothing, still searching) and four more refusals in `test_nonsense_is_refused`. Full suite 1908 passed, 10 skipped; ruff, format and mypy clean. Tried in a copy with the search switched on and `give_up_after=8`: on the racing game a training stops going back after its first 8 to 10 searches (52 searches over six trainings, from about 130), and the time lost is halved.
- **Commit:** see PR #253. **PR:** #253.
- **Completion report:** Done as planned. Nothing passes `give_up_after` yet. Decisions: giving up lasts as long as the runner, the simplest thing that bounds the cost; it goes by outcomes because nothing known before a search tells a game where searching works from one where it does not. Corrected: T-1007's note that ground walked again after going back is paid twice was wrong (`Ground.put_back` keeps what was reached); ARCHITECTURE.md now says so. Known limit: a game in which a way is found now and then (the racing game: 4%) keeps starting the count again, so there it can take more than `give_up_after` searches to give up. Carried to the next task: with the search on, the racing game's first demonstration (T-606) no longer holds on its three seeds, although its claims hold over all six seeds measured and for 17 of the 20 threes of them (20 of 20 without the search); the one seed that turns it has a point-lover that learned to brake from two ways found early. Next: switch the search on in training with this count set, and settle that test.

### T-1008 – A search has a time limit and says how long it took
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (step 6 of working out a way past where it died, third part. Measured with the search switched on by hand, 40 goes on each practice level, against the same runs on main: furthest reached in the first ten goes 410 from 242 on level 0 and 417 from 222 on level 3, in the last ten 440 from 194 and 212 from 151; best go 912 from 449 and 1,197 from 244; a way was found in 24 of 31 searches on level 0. On the practice emulator the 40 goes took three and a half times as long. On a real emulator a try is played at the emulator's top speed, which depends on the machine, and a step is held under the service's lock, so Stop waits for a search in flight: 120 tries of 40 steps could be most of a minute. Nothing in the log says how long a search took.)
- **Objective:** `find_way(..., seconds=None, clock=time.monotonic)`: with `seconds`, no play is started once that long has passed since the search began (a play in flight is finished: it is at most the trace and `carry_on` steps). `Search` gains `seconds` (how long it took) and `out_of_time`. `EpisodeRunner(..., way_seconds=None)` passes it on, and the log line of a search says how long it took and, when it ran out of time, that it did.
- **Scope:** `training/search.py`, `training/episode.py`. **Out of scope:** switching it on in training (next task), stopping a play in flight, a limit that adapts to the machine.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. With a limit, no play starts once the time is up: the search ends with `out_of_time`, the plays it made counted, and no way. The check is made before every play, the second (looked at) play of a change included.
  2. A way found within the limit is the same way in the same number of tries as without one, and `out_of_time` is false. A search that ends because the tries or the changes ran out is not out of time.
  3. Without a limit nothing changes from T-1006, and `Search.seconds` still says how long it took.
  4. The runner passes `way_seconds` on, and a search that ran out of time is a loss that stands like any other with no way found: the game is put back where it was.
  5. The log line of a search says how long it took, and for one that ran out of time that it did.
  6. Nonsense is refused with a `ConfigurationError` before anything is played: a limit of zero or less, one that is not a number, a clock that cannot be called.
- **Expected changes:** `training/search.py`, `training/episode.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_search.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_search_at_a_loss.py`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `TASK_TRACKER.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Test plan:** written before the code. In `test_search.py`, on the practice game with a clock the test moves: `test_no_play_starts_once_the_time_is_up` (1), `test_a_way_found_in_time_is_the_same_way` (2, 3), and nonsense added to `test_nonsense_is_refused` (6); with a script of outcomes, `test_the_time_is_checked_before_the_second_play_too` (1) and the time added to `test_every_play_counts_and_the_list_can_run_out` (2). In `test_search_at_a_loss.py`: `test_a_search_out_of_time_leaves_the_loss_standing` (4, 5), the time in the lines of `test_the_result_and_the_log_say_what_was_found` (5), and nonsense added to `test_nonsense_is_refused` (6). Then the full suite, ruff, format, mypy.
- **Results:** 6/6. In `test_search.py` (12 tests now), on the practice game with a clock the test moves a second a play: (1) `test_no_play_starts_once_the_time_is_up` (a limit of 5 s: five plays and no more, `out_of_time`, 5.0 s taken; a limit of a quarter of a second still finishes the play it started) and, with a script of outcomes, `test_the_time_is_checked_before_the_second_play_too`; (2, 3) `test_a_way_found_in_time_is_the_same_way` (with exactly the time it needs the same way in the same tries as with no limit; a second less and the change that stayed alive is not looked at; with no limit the time it really took is reported; the time taken is not part of a search's equality) and the time added to `test_every_play_counts_and_the_list_can_run_out` (tries or list running out is not out of time); (6) five more refusals in `test_nonsense_is_refused`. In `test_search_at_a_loss.py` (11 tests now): (4, 5) `test_a_search_out_of_time_leaves_the_loss_standing` (the limit reaches the search; the game is put back, the moments are forgotten, the go carries on; the log line word for word; no limit asked for, none passed on); (5) the time in both lines of `test_the_result_and_the_log_say_what_was_found`; (6) three more refusals. Full suite 1905 passed, 10 skipped; ruff, format and mypy clean.
- **Commit:** see PR #252. **PR:** #252.
- **Completion report:** Done as planned. Nothing sets a limit yet. Decisions: the time is checked where the budget is, before a play, so a play is never cut short and a search can overrun by one play; how long a search took is always measured and reported but is not part of what it found. Known limit: with a limit set a search depends on the machine's speed, so the practice bench and the tests must not set one they can reach. Found while measuring, for later tasks: late in training the brain still turns timid and stands still (on level 3 the last ten goes fall back to 212, still above the 151 without the search); the camera's move is measured 4 pixels short over a stretch of level 0 the AI never used to reach (73% right, from 98%), which also spoils the ground count there; a death far into the level sends the player back to the start, is taken for a restart, ends the go and so is not searched; walkers' touches are still not blamed. Next: switch the search on in training, with the bench told about rewinds.

### T-1007 – A go that loses a life goes back and looks for a way past
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (step 6 of working out a way past where it died, second part. The search (T-1006), the saved moments (T-1003) and going back (T-1005) are in place; nothing joins them yet.)
- **Objective:** `EpisodeRunner(..., ways_per_go=0, way_tries=BUDGET, flat_out=None)`. With `moments`, a screen watch and `ways_per_go` of 1 or more, a step of the AI's own in which a life goes (and the go does not end) is followed, inside the same `step()`, by a search: the game as it is now is saved into its own slot (`NOW_SLOT`), `find_way` is run from `moments.before_loss()` with the values the go counts lives on and `watch.trial(mark)`, and then either `go_back(moment, then=way.moves)` (a way was found) or the save of now is loaded again and the moments are forgotten (the loss stands). The life lost stays lost to the learner and to the count: only the game goes back. `EpisodeResult` says how many searches were made and how many found a way, and the log says what was found.
- **Scope:** `training/episode.py`, `training/moments.py` (a `slots` property). **Out of scope:** switching it on in training and measuring (next task), anything shown in the window, remembering a way from one go to the next, a search at a loss that ends the go (a game over).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. On the practice game, a go that walks into the first gap with moments, a screen watch and one search allowed: on the step the life goes it searches and goes back; the game has all its lives again; playing on, the player comes out alive beyond the gap; the changed move is among the moves played, and they are learned from like any step.
  2. The loss is real to the learner and to the count: the step it went on is learned with its penalty and as final before the jump, `setbacks` and the step of the first count it. The tries of the search are nobody's: nothing is learned from them, nothing is paid, no step is counted and the understanding engine sees no event.
  3. With no way found the game is exactly where it was when the life went, the go carries on from there, the moments are forgotten and a new one is saved with the next step.
  4. A go searches at most `ways_per_go` times. Once they are used up it makes no more saves. The next go has them again.
  5. No search is made, and the loss stands, without a screen watch or without a moment far enough back. With `ways_per_go=0` (the default) a go does what it did before this task: moments are kept and nothing is searched.
  6. A life lost while a way is being played drops the rest of its moves: the learner is asked again.
  7. The search runs inside `flat_out()` when one is given: entered before the save of now, left before the way is played.
  8. A link that drops during a search ends the go "disconnected".
  9. `EpisodeResult.ways_sought` and `ways_found` are saved and read back (a result saved before them reads as 0), and `describe_ways()` puts them in plain words; the log has one line a search, naming the step, how far it went back, the tries and, for a way, the move in the controls' own words and how long it is held.
  10. Nonsense is refused with a `ConfigurationError`: a negative `ways_per_go`, `way_tries` under 1, moments kept in the slot the present is saved in.
- **Expected changes:** `training/episode.py`, `training/moments.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_search_at_a_loss.py` (new), `tests/unit/training/test_moments.py`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `TASK_TRACKER.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Test plan:** written before the code, on the practice game through the real services (the lab of `test_going_back.py`): `test_a_go_that_falls_in_goes_back_and_gets_across` (1), `test_the_loss_is_real_and_the_tries_are_nobody_s` (2), `test_no_way_found_leaves_the_game_where_it_was` (3), `test_only_so_many_searches_a_go` (4), `test_no_search_without_what_it_needs` (5), `test_a_life_lost_on_the_way_drops_the_rest` (6), `test_the_search_runs_flat_out` (7), `test_a_dropped_link_in_the_search_ends_the_go` (8), `test_the_result_and_the_log_say_what_was_found` (9), `test_nonsense_is_refused` (10), and `test_the_slots_can_be_read` in the moments tests. Then the full suite, ruff, format, mypy.
- **Results:** 10/10. `tests/unit/training/test_search_at_a_loss.py`, 10 tests on the practice game through the real services, and one more in `test_moments.py`. (1) `test_a_go_that_falls_in_goes_back_and_gets_across` (the life goes on step 36; in the same step the go saves the present, plays 18 tries from the moment at its start and goes back; the 56 moves it then plays without asking the learner are its own with right + A for 4 steps from step 19; the player ends beyond the gap with all its lives; the moves are learned from); (2) `test_the_loss_is_real_and_the_tries_are_nobody_s` (36 steps learned, the last with -10 and as final; the engine's only event in that step is the life going; the way played costs nothing and loses nothing); (3) `test_no_way_found_leaves_the_game_where_it_was` (against the same go without a search: the game, the state, the reward and everything learned are the same at every step before and after, the present was saved as the game stood when the life went, the moments are forgotten and a new one is saved with the next step); (4) `test_only_so_many_searches_a_go`; (5) `test_no_search_without_what_it_needs`; (6) `test_a_life_lost_on_the_way_drops_the_rest`; (7) `test_the_search_runs_flat_out` (the exact order of speed, saves and loads, with and without a way); (8) `test_a_dropped_link_in_the_search_ends_the_go` (the speed is put back as well); (9) `test_the_result_and_the_log_say_what_was_found` (both log lines word for word, the wording of every case, a result saved and read back, an older record); (10) `test_nonsense_is_refused`; and `test_the_slots_can_be_read`. Full suite 1901 passed, 10 skipped; ruff, format and mypy clean.
- **Commit:** see PR #251. **PR:** #251.
- **Completion report:** Done as planned. Nothing passes `ways_per_go` yet, so training is unchanged. Decisions: the life lost stays counted and penalised, because the learner should know that walking on there costs a life, and the way played after it shows what does not; a loss that stands forgets the moments, since every try from before it would lose that life again first; a go with no searches left stops saving. Known limits: ground walked a second time after going back is paid a second time (the watch goes back with the game), so the reward of a go that went back is higher than its distance alone would make it; a loss that ends the go (the last life, or a game that starts over at once) is not searched; a way is not remembered from one go to the next, the learner has to learn it from having been played through it; the cost on a real emulator is still to be measured. Next: switch it on in training with the search at full speed, put it in the go's line in the log, and measure 40 goes on both practice levels.

### T-1006 – Try the small changes until one gets past
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (step 6 of working out a way past where it died, in three parts: the search, the go that uses it at a life lost, and switching it on and measuring. The parts it is made of are in place: the list of changes (T-999), a try played off the record and judged (T-1001), the screen watch lent to a try (T-1000). The prototype's search found a way in 9 to 142 tries when there was one.)
- **Objective:** `training/search.py`. `find_way(connection, slot, trace, space, frames_per_step=, lives=, watch=, budget=BUDGET, carry_on=CARRY_ON, look_every=)` takes the changes of `ways.changes(trace, space)` in their order. Each is applied to the trace with `carry_on` steps more on the end and played from the save in `slot` with `trial.play`, first without the screen (cheap: one read a step). One that loses a life is done with. One that stays alive is played once more with a fresh screen watch from `watch()` (the go's `ScreenWatch.trial(mark)`), and is the way if that try is alive too and counted new ground (`Outcome.past`). Every play counts against `budget`. Returns a `Search(way, tries)`; `way` is a `Way(moves, change, tries, ground)` or `None`. The game is left wherever the last try ended.
- **Scope:** `training/search.py` (new). **Out of scope:** when to search, going back and playing the way (T-1005 did the going back; the go using the search is the next task), a budget in seconds, any change that is not in `ways.changes`.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. On the practice game, for a go that walked right into the first gap: a way is found; it is the first change, in the list's order, that the game itself lets across; its moves played again from the save stay alive and count new ground; the go's own watch is unchanged.
  2. The same search twice finds the same way in the same number of tries.
  3. With fewer tries allowed than the way needs, none is found and exactly the budget is spent, never more; a search always ends.
  4. Where no change can help (the save is from after the fall began), none is found.
  5. Alive is not enough: a change that stays alive but counts no new ground on the screen is not the way, and the search goes on to the next.
  6. A change that stayed alive without the screen but loses a life when played again with it is not the way.
  7. Nonsense is refused with a `ConfigurationError` before anything is played: no life or health value, nothing it did, a budget under 1, a negative `carry_on`, a `watch` that cannot be called. An emulator error comes out as it is.
- **Expected changes:** `training/search.py` (new), `tests/unit/training/test_search.py` (new), `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `TASK_TRACKER.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Test plan:** written before the code. On the practice game through the real connection service, with the go of `test_trial.py` that walked into the gap: `test_it_finds_the_first_change_that_gets_across`, `test_the_same_search_twice_is_the_same`, `test_the_budget_is_never_overspent`, `test_no_way_when_the_fall_has_begun`. With `trial.play` replaced by a script of outcomes: `test_alive_is_not_enough`, `test_a_try_that_fails_under_the_screen_is_not_the_way`, `test_every_play_counts_and_the_list_can_run_out`. And `test_nonsense_is_refused`. Then the full suite, ruff, format, mypy.
- **Results:** 7/7. `tests/unit/training/test_search.py`, 8 tests. On the practice game through the real connection service: (1) `test_it_finds_the_first_change_that_gets_across` (the way is one button more than it was holding; played again from the save the game has the player alive beyond the gap; every change before it in the list loses the life when played, and the tries are those plus two); (2) `test_the_same_search_twice_is_the_same`; (3) `test_the_budget_is_never_overspent` (one try short: nothing found, exactly the budget played, the last blind; a budget of one plays once); (4) `test_no_way_when_the_fall_has_begun`. With `trial.play` replaced by a script of outcomes: (5) `test_alive_is_not_enough`; (6) `test_a_try_that_fails_under_the_screen_is_not_the_way`; (3 again, and the error of 7) `test_every_play_counts_and_the_list_can_run_out`; (7) `test_nonsense_is_refused` (nothing is played). Measured outside the tests: on level 0 the way is right + A for 4 steps from step 19 of 36, found in 18 plays and a third of a second on the practice emulator; on level 3 the same held 8 steps, in 50 plays. Full suite 1890 passed, 10 skipped; ruff, format and mypy clean.

Known limits: a search costs up to 120 plays of up to the trace's length plus 20 steps each, which on a real emulator at full speed may be most of a minute (to be measured when it is switched on); it only tries the changes of T-999 (one move, one button away, held 4, 8 or 16 steps), so a place that needs two things changed is not got past; where the game is not the same twice from a save, a way found blind can fail when looked at and is then passed over. Next: the go searches when it loses a life, plays the way it found, and says so in its result and the log.
### T-1005 – A go keeps saved moments and can go back to one
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (step 5 of working out a way past where it died, second half; see T-999. The memory of T-1003 has to be fed by a real go, and a go has to be able to step back into its own past without anything else in the app taking the jump for something the game did: no reward or life counted for it (T-1004), no "the game restarted", the screen watch put back with it, and the steps still waiting to be learned settled first. The prototype did all of this by reaching into the runner from outside; this task gives the runner the two things itself. Its code and tests were written before T-1004, whose problem they found, and set aside until that was merged.)
- **Objective:** `EpisodeRunner(moments=None)`: with a `Moments` (T-1003) and a life or health value being watched, the runner saves the game into `moments.next_slot()` whenever a save is due, before it chooses its move, records the save with the screen watch's mark (T-1000), and tells the memory every move it makes. `go_back(moment, then=())` loads that moment's save and carries on from it: the observation service is told the game went back (T-1004), what the signals collected across the jump is dropped, the steps still waiting for their lookahead are learned as final (the story they belonged to ended with that life), the state is read again, the screen watch is told of a life no look came for and put back to the moment's mark, the memory goes back, and the moves in `then` are played next, one a step, through the ordinary step (looked at, paid, learned from) without asking the learner. Without `moments` nothing changes.
- **Scope:** `training/episode.py`. **Out of scope:** deciding when to go back and which moves to play (the search, next task), switching it on in training, counting and wording it in a go's result and the log (next task), the child's own play (a step somebody else drove is a hole in the list of moves and forgets the moments).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. Without `moments`, and with `moments` while no life or health value is watched, a go makes no save; with moments kept a go plays exactly as the same go without them.
  2. With both, a save is made before the first step and then every `every` steps, each into the slot the memory named; the memory holds the moves the go made, in order, and each moment carries the screen watch's mark when there is a watch.
  3. After `go_back(moment)` the game is exactly where it was at that moment, the runner's state is the one it had then, the memory is back at that moment, and the go carries on: the jump is not counted as a life lost or gained, pays nothing, and does not end the go as a restart.
  4. The steps waiting to be learned when it goes back are learned as final, before the jump, and nothing learned afterwards reaches back across it.
  5. `go_back(moment, then=moves)` plays exactly those moves next without asking the learner, each learned from like any step, then asks the learner again; playing the moves the go made from that moment brings the game to the same place as before.
  6. A step the runner's own unstick press made, and a step somebody else drove, forget the moments and any moves still to be played. On a console without save states the go carries on without moments and says so once; a link lost at a save ends the go as disconnected.
  7. Misuse is refused with a `ConfigurationError`: no go running, a go that is over, no `moments`, a moment that is not kept, a move the controls don't have; and nothing is changed by a refused call.
- **Expected changes:** `training/episode.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_going_back.py` (new), `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `TASK_TRACKER.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Test plan:** written before the code, on the practice game through the real connection, observation, discovery and reward services, with a learner whose moves the test scripts. `test_no_saves_without_moments_or_without_a_life_count`, `test_nothing_is_saved_while_no_life_or_health_value_is_known`, `test_a_go_saves_moments_and_remembers_its_moves`, `test_going_back_puts_the_game_and_the_go_where_they_were`, `test_the_jump_is_nobody_s_loss_gain_or_restart`, `test_steps_waiting_to_be_learned_are_settled_before_the_jump`, `test_the_moves_given_are_played_next_and_learned_from`, `test_the_screen_watch_goes_back_too`, `test_holes_and_consoles_without_save_states`, `test_misuse_is_refused`. Then the full suite, ruff, format, mypy.
- **Results:** 7/7. `tests/unit/training/test_going_back.py`, 10 tests on the practice game through the real connection, observation, discovery and reward services, with a learner whose moves the test scripts: (1) `test_no_saves_without_moments_or_without_a_life_count` (the same go with and without moments gives the same result, the same game state and the same lessons) and `test_nothing_is_saved_while_no_life_or_health_value_is_known`; (2) `test_a_go_saves_moments_and_remembers_its_moves` (each save loads to the game as it was before that step's move) and `test_the_screen_watch_goes_back_too`; (3) `test_going_back_puts_the_game_and_the_go_where_they_were` (ten steps replayed after the jump match the first time state for state) and `test_the_jump_is_nobody_s_loss_gain_or_restart` (the life is back in the game, no event is announced, the next step pays nothing, and the second fall is one more life lost, counted once); (4) `test_steps_waiting_to_be_learned_are_settled_before_the_jump` (the seven waiting steps are learned as final, each paid the life it led to discounted by how far off it was; the three steps after the jump are paid nothing and look ahead only to where the go then is); (5) `test_the_moves_given_are_played_next_and_learned_from` (its own moves again lead to the same death without asking the learner; a jump at the edge gets across the first gap, then the learner is asked again, and the memory holds the way across); (6) `test_holes_and_consoles_without_save_states`; (7) `test_misuse_is_refused`. Three expectations in the tests as first written were wrong about the practice game, not about the criteria, and were corrected with the reason beside each: the save at step 20 is at the very edge of the gap, so only an immediate jump crosses; the life goes again six steps after going back to step 30; the watch has not yet seen the respawn at the step the life goes. Four loosely written assertions (an `or` that was always true) were replaced by exact ones before the suite was run. Full suite 1882 passed, 10 skipped; ruff, format and mypy clean.
- **Commit:** see PR #249. **PR:** #249.
- **Completion report:** Done as planned. Nothing asks a go to go back yet. Decided here and to be carried into the next task: a go's steps, reward and lives lost are what was really played and do not go back with the game (`times_back` counts the goings back), so the next task must decide how a life lost and then undone is counted and worded for the person. Known limits: if the read after the load fails, the go's state is one step stale and the jump is announced with the next snapshot; an emulator error from the load is the caller's to handle. Next: the search itself (try the small changes of T-999 from the moment with T-1001's `play` until one gets past), then the go using it at a life lost, then switching it on in training and measuring.
### T-1004 – A jump back within a go is nobody's event
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (step 5 of working out a way past where it died, split in two. The first test of a go being put back to a saved moment (the runner's part, now T-1005, written and set aside) failed on something outside the runner: the life the jump gave back was announced as a life gained, with a new relationship learned from it. T-935 taught only the byte statistics that a restore is not a change. The event detector, and through it the relationships, the rewards and goals, the long look and the watch on what rises after a loss, still take a restore for something the game did. At the start of a go that is old behaviour the runner works around, and the restart it shows is used on purpose (T-904). A jump back in the middle of a go, right after a death, several times a go, would teach the app that lives come back after they are lost and pay for it.)
- **Objective:** `ObservationService.expect_jump(back=True)` says the game was put back to an earlier moment of the go; the next `MemoryObserved` carries `went_back=True` (and only that one). On such a snapshot `DiscoveryService` raises no event and learns no relationship: `EventDetector.rebase(snapshot)` takes the values as they now are without judging the move, `LongLook.rebase(snapshot)` likewise, `RelationshipFinder.forget_recent()` pairs nothing across it, and the aftermath watch begins again as at the start of a go. What a value's first value was, and everything counted so far, is kept. A plain `expect_jump()` (checkpoint and practise-spot restores) does exactly what it did.
- **Scope:** `services/observer.py`, `services/discovery.py`, `understanding/events.py`, `understanding/longlook.py`, `understanding/relationships.py`. **Out of scope:** the runner's `go_back` (T-1005), treating every restore this way (the restart a checkpoint restore shows is used by T-904; changing that needs its own measurement), the rewards' own memory of a go's best values (kept on purpose: ground walked a second time is not paid a second time).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. `EventDetector.rebase`: after it, a value that moved across the jump raises nothing, and its next real move is judged from the value it was put back to; first values, typical gains and whether it ever moved are kept; a value not yet watched starts being watched.
  2. `LongLook.rebase`: no step up or down, no place and no starting over is counted across the jump, and the next real step is counted from the new value.
  3. `RelationshipFinder.forget_recent`: an event after it is not paired with one before it; the counts so far are kept.
  4. `expect_jump(back=True)` marks exactly the next snapshot `went_back`; a plain `expect_jump()` marks none; before the first snapshot there is nothing to mark.
  5. On the practice game: after a life is lost, loading a save from before it with `back=True` raises no event, no relationship and no reward, and the life lost again afterwards is one setback, paid once.
  6. A plain restore is seen as before (the same events as on main).
- **Expected changes:** as in the scope, plus tests in `tests/unit/understanding/test_events.py`, `test_longlook.py`, `test_relationships.py`, `tests/unit/services/test_observer.py`, `tests/unit/services/test_discovery.py`, and `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `TASK_TRACKER.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

### T-1003 – Remember saved moments and what it did since each
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (step 4 of working out a way past where it died, see T-999. To try small changes at a death the app must have somewhere to go back to: a save from well before the death, and exactly what it did from that save to the death. The prototype saved every 20 steps into 6 slots and went back to the newest save at least 30 steps before the life went; every way it found began 15 to 33 steps before. This task is that memory and nothing else.)
- **Objective:** `training/moments.py`. `Moments(slots, every=EVERY, lead=LEAD)` is told what happens and never touches the emulator. `due()` says a save should be made before the next step (at once in a fresh story, then every `every` steps); `next_slot()` names the slot for it (a free one, else the oldest moment's, which is then forgotten); `saved(mark=None)` records that the save was made there now and returns the `Moment(slot, step, mark)` (`mark` is whatever the caller wants back with it: the screen watch's mark of T-1000). `did(move)` records one step played; a step that cannot be replayed (`None`: the runner's own unstick press) forgets everything, because a list of moves with a hole in it cannot be replayed. `before_loss()` gives the newest moment at least `lead` steps back together with the moves made since it, or `None`. `went_back(moment)` says the story is at that moment again: newer moments and the moves since it are dropped and the step count is the moment's. `forget()` drops everything (a loss that stands: what was saved before it is from a story that no longer leads here).
- **Scope:** `training/moments.py` (new). **Out of scope:** making and loading the saves, the runner keeping moments during a go (next task), the search itself (the task after), anything about which changes to try (T-999) or how a try is judged (T-1001).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. A fresh story is due a save at once; after a save the next is due exactly `every` steps later, not before, and stays due until it is made.
  2. Slots are used in the order given until all are in use; then the oldest moment's slot is reused and that moment is forgotten, and the moves kept begin at the oldest moment still kept.
  3. `before_loss()` names the newest moment at least `lead` steps back and exactly the moves made since it, in order; `None` when no moment is that old or none is kept.
  4. `went_back(moment)` drops the newer moments (their slots are free again) and the moves since, sets the step count to the moment's, and the next save is due `every` steps after it; a moment that is not kept is refused.
  5. A step that cannot be replayed, and `forget()`, drop every moment and move; a save is then due at once and the step count carries on.
  6. Nonsense is refused with a `ConfigurationError`: no slots, a slot named twice or not a name, `every` or `lead` under 1, a move that is not a whole number of 0 or more, `saved()` when the same step is already saved.
- **Expected changes:** `training/moments.py` (new), `tests/unit/training/test_moments.py` (new), `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `TASK_TRACKER.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Test plan:** written before the code. `test_a_save_is_due_at_once_and_then_every_so_many_steps`, `test_slots_go_round_and_the_oldest_moment_is_forgotten`, `test_the_moment_before_a_loss_and_what_it_did_since`, `test_going_back_drops_what_came_after`, `test_a_hole_in_what_it_did_and_forgetting`, `test_nonsense_is_refused`, and `test_a_long_story_against_a_plain_record` (a few thousand random saves, steps, losses and goings back checked against a full list of everything done). Then the full suite, ruff, format, mypy.
- **Results:** 6/6. `tests/unit/training/test_moments.py`, 7 tests: (1) `test_a_save_is_due_at_once_and_then_every_so_many_steps`; (2) `test_slots_go_round_and_the_oldest_moment_is_forgotten`; (3) `test_the_moment_before_a_loss_and_what_it_did_since`; (4) `test_going_back_drops_what_came_after`; (5) `test_a_hole_in_what_it_did_and_forgetting`; (6) `test_nonsense_is_refused`; and over all of them `test_a_long_story_against_a_plain_record` (4000 random saves, steps, losses, goings back and forgettings checked at every turn against a plain list of everything done). One of the tests as first written counted a save as due a step early, against criterion 1; the test was wrong and was corrected before the code was changed. Full suite 1865 passed, 10 skipped; ruff, format and mypy clean.
- **Commit:** see PR #247. **PR:** #247.
- **Completion report:** Done as planned. Nothing calls it yet. A moment is known by being the same object, so a save made after a going back is never mistaken for one that was dropped. Known limits, all by design and for the caller to respect: a life lost within 30 steps of the oldest moment has no moment to go back to; the memory does not know whether a save really exists in the emulator; the step count goes back with the story, so it is not the length of a go. Next: a go that keeps these moments (saves when one is due, tells it each move) and can go back to one.
