### T-1001 – Play a try from a saved moment and tell whether it got past
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (step 3 of working out a way past where it died, see T-999. The prototype knew from the game itself whether a try got past. The app has two things to go by: the values it reads as lives or health, and the new ground its watch of the screen counts. A try must also leave nothing behind: nothing learned, no reward counted, no statistics of the game's memory moved by a death that is only a try.)
- **Objective:** `training/trial.py`. `play(connection, slot, moves, space, frames_per_step=..., lives=..., watch=None, look_every=DEFAULT_LOOK_EVERY)` loads the save in `slot`, holds each move's buttons for `frames_per_step` frames (one bundled request a step, reading only the bytes of the `lives` variables), and stops at the first step in which one of those values is lower than the step before. With a `watch` (a `ScreenWatch.trial`, T-1000) it takes a screenshot every `look_every` steps, on the steps a go would, and shows it to the watch. It lets go of the pad at the end and returns an `Outcome(steps, lost, ground)`: steps played, whether a value went down, and the steps of new ground the watch counted (0 without one). `Outcome.past` is true when nothing was lost and at least `PAST` (2) steps of new ground were counted: alive, and somewhere the go had not been. It talks to the emulator only: the observation, discovery, reward and learning services hear nothing of it. The game is left where the try ended; putting it back is the caller's.
- **Scope:** `training/trial.py` (new). **Out of scope:** which moves to play (T-999), saving during a go, going back and the search itself (next tasks), a loss the app can only see on the screen (no life count: every try looks alive, and the caller must not search then).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. On the practice game from a save at the start: walking right into the first gap is `lost`, and stops at the step the game's own life count drops; it is not `past`.
  2. With the watch of a go that walked into the gap: the same walk with a jump at the edge is not lost and counts at least 2 steps of new ground (`past`); standing still, and walking to the edge and stopping, are alive with no new ground (not `past`); the go's own watch is unchanged by all of them.
  3. The same moves from the same save give the same outcome every time, and the pad is let go at the end, also when the emulator fails part-way.
  4. Without a watch the ground is 0 and losses are still seen; a watched value that only goes up is no loss; one that goes down ends the try at that step.
  5. Nothing is published on the event bus and the observation service's frame count does not move.
  6. Nonsense is refused with a `ConfigurationError`: no moves, a move the controls don't have, frames or look_every under 1, a watch that is not a `ScreenWatch`.
- **Expected changes:** `training/trial.py` (new), `tests/unit/training/test_trial.py` (new), `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `TASK_TRACKER.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Test plan:** written before the code, on the practice game through the real connection service. `test_walking_into_the_gap_is_a_life_lost`, `test_a_jump_at_the_edge_gets_past_and_standing_still_does_not`, `test_the_same_try_twice_is_the_same_and_the_pad_is_let_go`, `test_values_that_rise_and_values_that_fall`, `test_a_try_is_off_the_record`, `test_nonsense_is_refused`. Then the full suite, ruff, format, mypy.
- **Results:** 6/6. `tests/unit/training/test_trial.py`, 6 tests on the practice game through the real connection service: (1) `test_walking_into_the_gap_is_a_life_lost`; (2) `test_a_jump_at_the_edge_gets_past_and_standing_still_does_not` (every 8-step jump that stays alive counts 2 or more steps of new ground; standing still and stopping at the edge count none); (3) `test_the_same_try_twice_is_the_same_and_the_pad_is_let_go`; (4) `test_values_that_rise_and_values_that_fall`; (5) `test_a_try_is_off_the_record`; (6) `test_nonsense_is_refused`. Full suite 1848 passed, 10 skipped; ruff, format and mypy clean. The first full run did not finish: one test failed in `tests/ui` (about the 265th, among the stall-watch tests, which time the window's own thread) and thirteen tests later the run died of a segmentation fault inside Qt's event processing during a window test's setup. No window test loads the new module. It happened as the machine was taking in an upload; the run was repeated in full and passed, and the window tests around it were run five more times, all passing. Recorded as it happened, with the cause not proven.
- **Commit:** see PR #245. **PR:** #245.
- **Completion report:** Done as planned. Nothing calls it yet. Next: remembering saved moments and what the AI did since each; then a go that keeps them and can go back; then the search at a death. Known limits: with no life or health value known nothing can be seen to be lost, so the search must not run then; a death that shows only on the screen is not seen; a try with the watch costs a screenshot and about 15 ms every other step, so the search should play each change without the watch first.
### T-1000 – The screen watch can be put back to a saved moment, and lent to a try
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (step 2 of working out a way past where it died, see T-999. When the game is put back to a save from a moment before, the watch must go back with it. As it is, a jump of the screen with a life lost near it is read as "put back at the start of the go": the place becomes where the go began and the furthest reached is kept, so getting past the gap from the saved moment would pay nothing until it was as far from the *start* as the go's furthest. And a try that is only a try must be able to count the ground it would be paid without the go's own count changing.)
- **Objective:** (a) `observation/ground.py`: `Ground.keep()` returns where it is (`Kept`: the camera's travel, where the player was first seen on the screen and where it stands from there); `Ground.put_back(kept)` makes that the place again, with the furthest reached and the steps counted left as they are; `Ground.copy()` is a separate `Ground` in the same state. (b) `training/vision.py`: `ScreenWatch.mark()` returns a `Mark` (the ground's `Kept` and where the player was last seen); `ScreenWatch.back_to(mark)` says the game was put back to that moment: the tracker starts afresh so the jump is not measured as a move of the camera or taken for a cut, what was waiting from the last looks (a jolt, a life lost, a fall, touches not yet blamed) is dropped, the ground is put back, and the counts kept for the summary stay; `ScreenWatch.trial(mark)` is a new watch on the same player, standing at that moment with a copy of the ground, whose looks change nothing in this one and whose `take_new_ground()` is what the try would be paid.
- **Scope:** `observation/ground.py`, `training/vision.py`. **Out of scope:** saving and loading the game, playing a try (next task), the runner and the service.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. `Ground`: put back, the place is the one kept; the reach and the steps are unchanged; the same ground walked again pays nothing and the first step past the furthest pays. Something that is not a `Kept` is refused.
  2. `Ground.copy()`: looks on the copy leave the original as it was, and the step's size and whether the screen scrolls come along.
  3. `ScreenWatch.back_to`: after walking on and being put back, the next look measures no move of the camera, is not a jolt, the place is the marked one, and nothing is counted until it is past the go's furthest; a life lost told just before is not taken for a respawn at the start.
  4. `ScreenWatch.trial`: the try's new ground is counted from the mark against the go's furthest; this watch's place, ground, looks and what it has learned are untouched by the try's looks.
  5. A mark that is not one is refused; a watch that has not seen the player yet can still be marked and put back.
- **Expected changes:** the files in Scope, `tests/unit/observation/test_ground.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_vision.py`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `TASK_TRACKER.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Test plan:** written before the code. Ground: `test_put_back_it_pays_only_past_its_furthest`, `test_a_copy_is_its_own`. Watch: `test_put_back_to_a_marked_moment`, `test_a_trial_counts_without_changing_the_watch`, `test_marks_before_it_is_seen_and_nonsense`. Then the full suite, ruff, format, mypy.
- **Results:** 5/5. (1) `test_put_back_it_pays_only_past_its_furthest`, and `test_put_back_on_a_screen_that_does_not_scroll` added for the place counted off the player itself. (2) `test_a_copy_is_its_own`. (3) `test_put_back_to_a_marked_moment`, which also shows the same jump back without `back_to` leaves the place wrong. (4) `test_a_trial_counts_without_changing_the_watch`. (5) `test_marks_before_it_is_seen_and_nonsense`. Full suite 1842 passed, 10 skipped; ruff, format and mypy clean.
- **Commit:** see PR #244. **PR:** #244.
- **Completion report:** Done as planned. Nothing calls these yet, so the app behaves as before. Next: play one change from a save and tell from the lives read and the ground counted whether it got past. Known limits: a trial's watch learns nothing that is kept (what things are, which hurt); the kind the player was learned as is not handed to a trial, so a player known only by its track and not by its colours is found again by where it was last seen.
### T-999 – The small changes to what it did that might get it past where it died
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 4, a smarter learner. T-998 made each try better and the AI still stops short of the gaps: trying costs a life nine times in ten, so a learner that only ever stumbles across is right to stay away. Tried outside the app first (scratch prototypes on the practice bench, 40 goes, both levels). Putting the game back to a moment before each death for six more tries, with or without exploring more there and going over a lucky crossing ten times: no better, it learns sooner to keep away (last ten goes 140 to 188 on level 0, 164 to 173 on level 3; no crossing at all on level 3). What worked: at a death, go back to a save from a moment before, replay what it did with one small change (at one moment, hold a move one button from the one it made, for 4, 8 or 16 steps), without learning anything from those tries, until a change gets it past alive; then play that way through for real and carry on. Furthest in the first and last ten goes went from 242 and 194 to 340 and 302 on level 0 (best 630) and from 222 and 151 to 393 and 350 on level 3 (best 805); late goes cross the first gap unaided. 60 ways found in the two runs: every one was a move one button from the move made, 4 to 16 steps long, 15 to 33 steps before the life went, found in 9 to 142 tries. That prototype knew from the game itself whether a try got past; the app must tell from the lives it reads and the screen. It is built in steps. This is the first: the list of changes, with nothing of the emulator in it.)
- **Objective:** `training/ways.py`. `Change(at, move, hold)`: from step `at` of what it did, make `move` for `hold` steps. `Change.apply(trace, carry_on)`: the moves to play, the trace with that stretch replaced, cut or padded with the trace's commonest move (`carry`) to the trace's length plus `carry_on` steps, so a try runs on past where the life went. `changes(trace, space, holds=HOLDS, stride=STRIDE, most=None)`: every change worth trying, in order: shortest hold first (4, 8, 16), within a hold from the end of the trace backwards every `stride` (2) steps, at each place the moves near the one it made (`ActionSpace.near`, T-998). A change that comes to the same moves as an earlier one (a long hold cut off by the end of the trace) is left out. `most` caps the list. Nothing about any game or button is named.
- **Scope:** `training/ways.py` (new). **Out of scope:** playing a change on the emulator and telling whether it got past (next task), keeping saves during a go and going back (after that), learning from the way found, moves that are not near the one made (none of the 60 ways found needed one).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. `Change.apply` replaces exactly `hold` steps from `at`, keeps the rest of the trace, and returns `len(trace) + carry_on` moves, the extra ones the trace's commonest move (the later of two as common); a hold that runs past the end is cut there.
  2. `changes` gives them in the order stated, only moves near the one made at that step, each within the trace, and none twice.
  3. A trace of moves with nothing near (controls with no combinations, or holding nothing throughout) gives no changes; an empty trace gives none.
  4. `most` stops the list; a bad `most`, `stride`, hold, step or move is refused with a `ConfigurationError`.
  5. Counted on a trace like the prototype's (40 steps of walking right on the pad): the change that jumps 17 steps before the end for 8 steps is in the list within its first 100.
- **Expected changes:** `training/ways.py` (new), `tests/unit/training/test_ways.py` (new), `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `TASK_TRACKER.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

Then the full suite, ruff, format, mypy.

### T-998 – When the AI tries something new, it changes one button of what it would have done
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 4, a smarter learner. With the rewards honest (T-994, T-996, T-997) the AI on the practice bench stops short of the first gap. Recorded go by go (scratch probe, seed 0): it crossed once, in go 1, by luck; from go 13 on its own best move near the start is to stand still, because every walk to the gap ended in a life lost. To learn the jump it has to make it a few times. Measured on the practice game from a spot 6 or 12 steps of walking before the first gap, 400 tries each, with the AI's own move taken to be "hold right": exploring as it does now, any of its 15 moves held for 1 to 8 steps, got across in 2 to 3% of tries on level 0 (a gap of three tiles) and under 1% on level 3 (four tiles). Exploring by changing one button of the move it would have made (right becomes right and A, right and B, or nothing) and holding that got across in 12 to 17% and 5 to 7%. A jump over a gap is "what I was doing, plus one button", held: a random pick from every combination almost never keeps the run-up.)
- **Objective:** `ActionSpace.near(index)`: the moves one button away from a move (one button more or one fewer; narrowed while building to those that still hold a button the move holds, see Results). `ActionSpace.sample_near(rng, index)`: half the time (`NEAR_SHARE`) one of those, the other half any move at all, as before, so nothing becomes unreachable and a brain that knows nothing yet still tries everything. The table learner and the network learner explore with it, around the move they would otherwise have made at that step; the run a tried move is held for (T-983) is unchanged. Nothing about any game or button is named.
- **Scope:** `learning/actions.py`, `learning/qlearning.py`, `learning/dqn.py`; added while building, the practice bench's own figure for a go that begins before the camera has moved (`tools/practice_bench.py`, see Results). **Out of scope:** practising from a saved spot just before where it died (the next task: this one makes each try better, that one puts the tries where they are needed), how long a run is, the schedule of how often it explores.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. `near` gives exactly the moves one button away that keep a button held (as built, see Results), each way round (if b is near a, a is near b), never the move itself; a move with nothing one button away has none.
  2. `sample_near` returns a near move about half the time and any move the rest, reaches every move, and where there is no near move is the plain pick.
  3. Both learners, exploring at every step with a known best move, pick a move one button from it far more often than chance would (over half of picks, where chance gives 2 in 15), and still pick every move sometimes; the best move itself is what they do when not exploring, as before.
  4. Exploring still comes in runs of the same length, as often as before (T-983's tests unchanged).
  5. Measured on `practice_bench --goes 40`, seeds 0 and 3, and recorded as it is.

### T-997 – What goes up when a life is lost is not progress
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the third wrong reward T-993 measured, and after T-996 the one that decides what the AI does on the practice game: "Progress goes up" is ram 0x11, the game's mode, 0 while playing, 1 during the dying pause, 2 at game over. It goes up at every death and pays 10 points, past the go's best so once a go; a life costs 7.5. Each late go walks to the first gap, falls in and comes out 2.5 points ahead for the fall. The guess is High confidence: rare, few values, up more often than down (two ups for each down when the last life goes), "steps up at the same few places" (the gaps). Nothing in the byte's own statistics tells it from a checkpoint. What does: when it goes up. Every rise comes within a second of a life going, and every life that goes has such a rise.)
- **Objective:** (a) `understanding/aftermath.py`: `Aftermath` is told every event the detector finds. It counts, for each value, its rises (`PROGRESS` events), how many of them came as something was lost (a `SETBACK` or a `RESET` up to `BEFORE` frames after the rise, planned as 240 and built as 90, see Results, or up to `AFTER`, 30, before it), how many losses there have been since the value first rose, and how many of those had a rise of that value at them. Losses within `AFTER` frames of each other are one. `verdict(var_id)` is true when rises and losses are each at least `MIN_COUNT` (5) and both shares are at least `SHARE` (60%): most of its rises are at a loss, and most losses have its rise. A new go (`begin()`), or frames running backwards, forgets what was waiting to be matched; the counts are kept. (b) `DiscoveryService` feeds it from `_observe_memory`, calls `begin()` in `begin_go()`, starts a new one with each knowledge, and `doubt_bouncing` gives a progress guess with that verdict the reason `at-loss`: doubted at one review, dropped by the AI at the next, and a confirmed guess is kept and questioned, exactly as "busy" and "bounces" are.
- **Scope:** `understanding/aftermath.py` (new), `services/discovery.py`. **Out of scope:** scores and flags (a flag pays once a go since T-994 and a score that jumps at a death is another finding), a loss the app only sees on the screen (no memory guess, no events), what the brain does once the reward is honest (the learner, next).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. `Aftermath`: a value that rises 40 frames before each of six losses, or in the same step, has the verdict; one that rises 31 frames after a loss, or one frame more than `BEFORE` ahead of it, is not matched; two kinds of loss in one step are one loss; only `PROGRESS` events are rises.
  2. Both ways are needed: progress that is often followed by a loss, among many losses that had no such rise (a page crossed just before a hard jump), has no verdict; nor has progress whose rises mostly come with no loss near.
  3. Fewer than five rises, or five losses since it first rose, say nothing; losses from before the value first rose do not count against it.
  4. A new go, and frames running backwards, forget pending rises and the last loss; counts stay.
  5. In the service: such a guess is doubted at the first `doubt_bouncing` and dropped at the second, with evidence saying how many of its rises came as a life was lost; a confirmed one is kept and questioned; a real checkpoint on the same events is untouched; the events reach `Aftermath` from observed memory.
  6. Measured on `practice_bench --goes 40`, both seeds: the row on the mode value is gone by the end and a late go earns nothing for dying; furthest reached and deaths recorded as they are.
- **Expected changes:** the files in Scope, `tests/unit/understanding/test_aftermath.py` (new), `tests/unit/services/test_discovery.py`, `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `TASK_TRACKER.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Test plan:** written before the code. `test_aftermath.py`: `test_a_value_that_rises_as_lives_are_lost`, `test_the_window_has_edges`, `test_progress_followed_by_a_loss_now_and_then_is_left`, `test_too_few_to_say_and_losses_before_it_rose`, `test_a_new_go_forgets_what_was_waiting`, `test_nonsense_is_refused`. Service: `test_progress_that_rises_as_a_life_is_lost_is_doubted_then_dropped` (events through `MemoryObserved`), with the existing bounce and busy tests unchanged. Then the full suite, ruff, format, mypy and the bench on seeds 0 and 3.
- **Results:** 6/6, with the rule changed from the plan after an existing test caught it. As first built (a rise up to 240 frames before a loss, and nothing about how often losses come) it dropped the toy racer's real checkpoint in `test_a_lives_guess_that_bounces_is_doubted_then_dropped`: at full speed that game has a checkpoint every 16 frames and a life lost every 20, so every rise is near a loss and every loss near a rise by chance. The test was right and is unchanged. As built: `BEFORE` is 90 frames, and nothing is said unless the time near a loss (losses times `BEFORE + AFTER`) is at most a third (`QUIET`) of the frames watched since the value first rose; `note(events, frame)` is told the frame of every observation so the time watched is known. (1) to (4) `tests/unit/understanding/test_aftermath.py`, 7 tests, with `test_where_losses_come_thick_and_fast_nothing_is_said` added for the racer's case. (5) `test_progress_that_rises_as_a_life_is_lost_is_doubted_then_dropped`. (6) Bench, 40 goes, suggested rewards: on both seeds the mode value is dropped and no "Progress" row is left at the end; a late go earns only new ground, one or two switches and sometimes the jump's "score", and loses 7.5 for a life. Level 0: furthest reached in the first and last ten goes 202 (best 421) then 121 (best 188), was 198 then 208; lives lost a go 0.90 then 0.00 (was 0.40 then 1.10); 20 deaths (was 59). Level 3: 209 (best 276) then 172 (best 217), was 203 then 42; lives lost 1.70 then 0.30 (was 1.80 then 0.00); 27 deaths (was 53). Full suite 1825 passed, 10 skipped; ruff, format and mypy clean.
- **Commit:** see PR #241. **PR:** #241.
- **Completion report:** Done, with the window and the crowding rule changed as recorded. The three wrong rewards T-993 measured are gone: nothing pays for jumping on the spot, for time passing or for dying. What the measurement now shows is the learner alone: paid honestly, the AI walks towards the first gap and stops short of it, losing no lives and getting no further (it crossed in early goes, best 421, and does not keep it). That is the next task. Known limits: a value that rises more than a second and a half before the life goes (a long death tune) is not matched; a loss seen only on the screen makes no event and is not counted; scores and flags are not judged by this.
### T-996 – The top of a clock is not progress
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the second of the wrong rewards T-993 measured. On the practice game "Progress (3rd guess) goes up" is ram 0x16, the upper byte of the level's clock at 0x15/0x16: it goes up every 256 frames whatever the AI does and pays 10 points each time past the go's best, 40 for a go spent standing still, three times what walking to the first gap earns. How it got there: the lower byte was proposed early as a position and stayed one (it stops during the dying pause, so it changes in 87% of steps, short of the 90% the "steady" rule asks), so the pair was never joined; the upper byte, two values at first, was a flag, then reached a third value and "goes up each time the value below starts over", which is what a lap counter does over a track position, and became progress, High confidence. The statistics know better: 101 of its 111 changes fell in the step the byte below rolled over (`carry_ins`), and the byte below moved by the same hop as the time before in 99% of its changes. The idle probe at the start of a go (T-855) already sees the lower byte move with nothing pressed, and doubts only guesses on the bytes it saw move; the upper byte moves once in 64 steps and is not caught moving.)
- **Objective:** `understanding/variables.py` gains `clock_top(low, high)`: `high` is the upper byte of a 16-bit number whose lower byte is `low` (the pair rule the classifier already uses), it has changed at least 3 times, and `low` ticks at one pace (the same hop as the change before in 95% of its changes, however often it pauses). `DiscoveryService.doubt_self_moving` also looks one byte above each byte the probe saw move by itself: a progress, score or flag guess there that is the top of a clock by that rule is doubted the first time and dropped by the AI the second (its own evidence kind, `clock-top`, and its own log line), as a guess on the moving byte itself already is. A confirmed guess is left alone; lives and health are not judged by it.
- **Scope:** `understanding/variables.py`, `services/discovery.py`. **Out of scope:** joining the two bytes into one 16-bit counter after the fact (the guesses are already separate and one is dropped; the brain loses nothing it used), a clock that counts down (its borrow is not counted as a roll-over by the tracker), the value that rises when a life is lost (next task), the learner.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. `clock_top` is true for the upper byte of a clock that ticks at one pace, pauses now and then and is reset at each go; false for the page byte of a position that moves by varying amounts; false before the upper byte has changed 3 times; false for two unrelated bytes.
  2. A progress guess on the top of a clock whose lower byte the probe saw move is doubted at the first probe and dropped at the second, with evidence that says why; the announcement and the log name it.
  3. Not touched: the page of a position that moves by itself at varying pace; a top of a clock whose lower byte was not seen to move by itself; a confirmed guess; a lives guess.
  4. The existing self-moving behaviour and its log line are unchanged.
  5. Measured on `practice_bench --goes 40`, level 0 (seed 0): the row on the clock's upper byte is gone from the rewards by the end and what a late go earns from it is 0; furthest reached and deaths recorded as they are.
- **Expected changes:** the files in Scope, `tests/unit/understanding/test_variables.py`, `tests/unit/services/test_discovery.py`, `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `TASK_TRACKER.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Test plan:** written before the code. `test_the_top_of_a_clock_is_told_from_a_page_count` (synthetic bytes: a clock with pauses and resets, a position at varying speed, a short run, unrelated bytes); `test_the_top_of_a_clock_is_doubted_then_dropped` (four pairs fed to the tracker: a clock under a progress guess, a position and its page, a clock under a confirmed guess, a clock under a lives guess; a probe that did not see the clock move; two probes that did); the existing `test_self_moving_guesses_are_doubted_then_rejected` unchanged. Then the full suite, ruff, format, mypy and the bench on seeds 0 and 3.
- **Results:** 5/5. (1) `test_the_top_of_a_clock_is_told_from_a_page_count` (its "short run" was first 140 steps, which with a tenth of the steps paused is one turn of the clock and not two; set to 150). (2) to (4) `test_the_top_of_a_clock_is_doubted_then_dropped`, and `test_self_moving_guesses_are_doubted_then_rejected` unchanged. (5) Bench, 40 goes, suggested rewards. Level 0: ram 0x16 is dropped and its row gone; a late go earns 10 from "Progress goes up" (the mode byte, at the death), 8 from new ground, 3.75 from the "score" that is the jump's speed, 1.5 from each of two switches, and loses 7.5 for the life; furthest reached in the first and last ten goes 198 (best 421) then 208 (best 216), was 198 then 144; lives lost a go 0.40 then 1.10 (was 0.40 then 0.40); 59 deaths (was 48). Level 3: unchanged, 203 then 42, 53 deaths: the row was never there on that seed. So with the clock gone the AI walks to the first gap again and falls in each go, for a net gain of 2.5 points from the fall itself. Full suite 1817 passed, 10 skipped; ruff, format and mypy clean.
- **Commit:** see PR #240. **PR:** #240.
- **Completion report:** Done as specified. The rule joins two things the app already measured (what moves with nothing pressed, and which byte carries into which) and asks one new question of the lower byte, whether it ticks at one pace. Next: the value that rises when a life is lost, which now pays the AI to fall into the first gap.
### T-995 – A start that gets stuck, crashes or fails says where
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (a report from Boss, 12 Nov 19:15: "the app doesn't open, the process starts but nothing". His log holds two lines, the "starting" line of two launches 18 seconds apart, and nothing after: not "Qt application created", which a normal start of his writes 0.6 seconds later. The same commit's build opens on the Windows runner (smoke test green on 82ae19d) and from source here, and between those two log lines the app reads nothing from the data folder (checked with an audit hook: no file, process or socket), so what stops it on his machine cannot be told from here. The log was meant to answer exactly this, "a start that never shows a window still leaves a trace", and it does not: it has no line between the first and the Qt application, a hang writes nothing, a crash inside a library writes nothing, and in the windowed build an exception that ends the script never reaches `sys.excepthook` (the bootloader shows its own dialog instead), so it is not logged either.)
- **Objective:** (a) The start logs each stage before it begins: loading Qt, loading the app's own code, creating the Qt application, building the main window. The last line in the log is then the stage that did not finish. (b) `logbook.watch_start()`: Python's `faulthandler` writes to a trace file of this run (`logs/start-<pid>.txt`) the stack of every thread if the window is not up after `STUCK_AFTER` (10) seconds, and at any later crash inside a library; `logbook.started()` calls the timed dump off once the window is shown. The file is removed when the run ends with nothing in it. (c) The next start copies what earlier runs left in such files into the log ("An earlier start left a trace (it took over 10 seconds to open, got stuck or crashed); this is where it was") and removes them, so the one log file Boss sends carries it. (d) An exception that ends the launch is written to the log before it is raised again, once.
- **Scope:** `core/logbook.py`, `cli.py`, `ui/app.py`. **Out of scope:** the cause on Boss's machine (not knowable until his next log; this task is what makes it knowable), a splash screen, changing what the start does.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. A run whose start is still not finished after the limit leaves a trace file naming the function it is in; a run that starts in time leaves no file.
  2. A crash inside a library after the watch began leaves a trace naming where.
  3. The next start writes the earlier traces into the log, each with its file's name, and removes the files; with none, it writes nothing about them.
  4. Where the logs folder cannot be written, nothing is watched and nothing is raised; watching twice is one watch.
  5. The launch logs its stages in order, and an exception from the launch is in the log once (the uncaught-exception hook does not write it again) and is still raised.
  6. The built app still passes the launch smoke test, and a normal start's log reads: starting, loading Qt, loading the app's code, creating the Qt application, Qt application created, building the main window, main window shown.
- **Expected changes:** the files in Scope, `tests/unit/core/test_logbook.py`, `tests/unit/test_cli.py`, `tests/ui/test_main_window.py` (the stages of a real start), `README.md` (troubleshooting), `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `TASK_TRACKER.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Test plan:** written before the code. Each watch test runs a child Python process, because `faulthandler` belongs to the whole process (and pytest uses it). `test_a_start_that_gets_stuck_says_where_and_the_next_start_logs_it` (a child sleeps past a 0.3 s limit inside `stuck_here`; its trace names it; a second child's log carries it and the file is gone), `test_a_start_in_time_leaves_nothing`, `test_a_crash_in_a_library_says_where`, `test_an_unwritable_place_watches_nothing`; cli: `test_the_launch_logs_its_stages`, `test_a_launch_that_fails_is_logged_once_and_raised`; ui: the existing real start asserts the full sequence of lines. Then the full suite, ruff, format, mypy, and the Windows build's smoke test in CI.
- **Results:** 6/6, the sixth shown by CI on the PR (the smoke test now reads the built app's log). (1) and (3) `test_a_start_that_gets_stuck_says_where_and_the_next_start_logs_it`, `test_a_start_in_time_leaves_nothing`. (2) `test_a_crash_in_a_library_says_where`. (4) `test_an_unwritable_place_watches_nothing` and the one-watch check in the in-time test. (5) `test_the_launch_logs_its_stages`, `test_a_launch_that_fails_is_logged_once_and_raised`, and the real start in `test_real_entry_point_launches_headless_and_exits_zero`. Rehearsed by hand: a start made to hang 11.5 seconds where the Qt application is created, then killed; the next start's log carried "Timeout (0:00:10)!" and the stack naming that line, and the trace file was gone. The carried-over message was first worded "where it stopped"; a start that is only slow leaves the same trace, so it now says "it took over 10 seconds to open, got stuck or crashed". Full suite 1815 passed, 10 skipped; ruff, format and mypy clean. CI then failed the stuck-start test on Linux: the child printed its trace file's name and left by `os._exit`, which flushes nothing, and it had passed here only because this machine runs Python unbuffered; reproduced with that switched off, and the child now flushes the line.
- **Commit:** see PR #239. **PR:** #239.
- **Completion report:** Done as specified. This does not fix what stops the start on Boss's machine, which nothing here could reproduce: it makes the next log say which stage did not finish and, after one more start, the exact line. Known limits: a trace file still open in a run that is still going cannot be removed on Windows, so it is logged again at each start until that run ends; a start that hangs before Python itself is up (the bootloader unpacking, an antivirus holding the exe) writes nothing, and the log's absence of even the "starting" line is then the finding.
### T-994 – A switch pays the first time it goes on in a go
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 4, made urgent by T-993's measurement. On the practice game a go earns about 80 points from "Something switches on" and "Something (2nd guess) switches on": the on-the-ground flag and the jumping flag, each worth +1.5 and each flipped about 25 times a go by the AI's own jump button. Getting further earns about 14. The AI is being taught to jump on the spot. The rule that suggests the points means a switch as an event: something opened, something was picked up. Progress and score already pay only past the go's best, T-878; a switch has no "further", only a first time.)
- **Objective:** `RewardService` pays a `FLAG_ON` or `FLAG_OFF` event the first time that switch goes that way in a go and not again until the next go (`ONCE_A_GO_KINDS`, kept per event key and cleared on `GoStarted` and on connecting). An event that does not pay is not tallied either, as with past-best. The suggested rows for a switch say so in their note. Nothing else changes: the suggested points, the game-over rule, a person's own "goes up" and "goes down" rows (which pay every time, as before).
- **Scope:** `services/rewards.py`, `rewards/suggestions.py` (the note). **Out of scope:** what a switch is worth (the suggestion stays), the clock's top byte read as progress and the value that rises when a life is lost (the next two tasks), the learner.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. A switch going on pays its row once in a go; going off and on again pays nothing more; another switch pays its own first time; a new go pays again. The same holds for going off, counted apart from going on.
  2. A flip that does not pay is not tallied, and no `RewardEarned` is published for it.
  3. A person's own row on the same value pays at every change; progress and score pay past the go's best as before; a row a person gave points to (a switch worth +5) still pays once a go.
  4. The note of a suggested switch row says it counts the first time in a go; the other rows' notes are unchanged.
  5. Measured on `practice_bench --goes 40`, level 0: what a go earns from the switch rows falls from about 80 points to at most 2 a row; furthest reached and deaths recorded here as they are.
- **Expected changes:** the files in Scope, `tests/unit/services/test_rewards.py`, `tests/unit/rewards/test_suggestions.py`, `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `TASK_TRACKER.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Test plan:** written before the code. Service: `test_a_switch_pays_the_first_time_in_a_go` (on, off, on again; a second switch; a new go; off counted apart; nothing tallied or published for the unpaid flips; a person's points on the row; a reconnect), `test_a_persons_own_row_on_a_switch_pays_every_time`; the existing `test_progress_and_score_pay_only_past_the_best_of_the_go` unchanged. Suggestions: `test_a_switch_row_says_it_counts_once_a_go`. Then the full suite, ruff, format, mypy, and the bench on seeds 0 and 3 with what each row paid.
- **Results:** 5/5. (1) to (3) `test_a_switch_pays_the_first_time_in_a_go` and `test_a_persons_own_row_on_a_switch_pays_every_time`; the reconnect part was first written to expect the row to pay straight after connecting again and failed for a reason that is not this task's (a row a person gave points to is kept switched off when its value is not yet known again after connecting, and stays off): the test now has the person switch it back on, and was checked to fail with the reset on connecting taken out. (4) `test_a_switch_row_says_it_counts_once_a_go`. (5) Bench, 40 goes, suggested rewards. Level 0: each switch row pays 1.5 a go (was about 40 a row); furthest reached in the first and last ten goes 198 (best 421) then 144 (best 217), was 198 then 206; lives lost a go 0.40 then 0.40 (was 0.50 then 1.40); 48 deaths (was 38). Level 3: 203 (best 224) then 42 (best 96), was 206 then 207; lives lost 1.80 then 0.00 (was 1.20 then 1.40); 53 deaths (was 50). The AI gets less far, not further, and this is recorded as it is: the pay for jumping was also what kept it moving. With that gone, on level 0 a go that stands still for its 300 steps earns 40 from "Progress (3rd guess) goes up" (the top byte of the level's clock, the next task), and on level 3 the last goes jump once (6.75 points: the two switches and a "score" that is the jump's speed) and stand still, because walking to the first gap earns about 13 and falling in costs 15. Also seen: the first 48 pixels from the start pay no new ground on this game, since the camera does not move until the player is at its holding place (T-993 counts only the camera once the screen has ever scrolled). Full suite 1809 passed, 10 skipped; ruff, format and mypy clean.
- **Commit:** see PR #238. **PR:** #238.
- **Completion report:** Done as specified. One rule, in the one place every row is scored: a switch pays the first time it goes that way in a go. Nothing about any game is in it. The measurement says plainly that this alone does not make the AI play better; it removes a wrong reason to jump. What is left to fix, in order: the clock read as progress, the value that rises when a life is lost, and then the learner, which with honest rewards finds that not walking is safest because it has not learned that a jump crosses the gap.
### T-993 – The AI is paid for getting somewhere new, measured off the screen
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 3: the brain reads the screen, and is paid by what the screen shows. After T-989 the AI on the practice bench falls far less and gets no further: nothing pays it for getting further. Its rewards come from memory guesses, and on the practice game those pay for jumping (two flags at +1.5 each), pay +7.5 for dying (the mode byte read as progress), and pay nothing for walking on, so the later goes earn 0 by standing still. T-992 gave the ruler: the camera's move between two looks, right in 98 to 100% of looks.)
- **Objective:** (a) `observation/ground.py`: `Ground` keeps, for one go, the place the player is at (as planned: the camera's moves summed, plus where it stands on the screen counted from where it was first seen; as built, see Results: the camera's moves summed once the screen has ever scrolled, and where it stands until then), the furthest that place has been to the right, left, down and up of where the go began, and how many steps of the player's own size of that have been paid; `look(moved, me, size)` returns the new steps, at most 4 a look; `back()` says it is back where the go began (the furthest stays, so the same ground does not pay twice); `begin()` starts a go. Nothing names a direction or a game. (b) `ObjectTracker.unexplained`: the share of the voting pixels the camera's move left differing at the last look (0 when nothing had to be searched for). (c) `ScreenWatch` owns a `Ground`: at every look it hands over the tracker's move and where it saw itself; a look in which a quarter of the screen or more is left unexplained is a cut and puts it back; so does a life lost within a few looks of a look in which no move explained 2% or more of the screen (a respawn; as built it must also find the player somewhere else on the screen, and where the camera cannot be followed nothing is counted, see Results). `take_new_ground()` gives the steps since the last take. (d) `EventKind.NEW_GROUND`, a `GroundCovered` bus event, and the row `screen:new_ground` ("Getting somewhere new", Progression, suggested 1 point a step): `RewardService` adds the row the first time ground is reported (not when a person removed it) and scores each step against it, like any row. (e) `EpisodeRunner` looks before it collects the step's reward and publishes the ground the look found, so the pay lands in the step that earned it. (f) The practice bench reports the ground paid for against the game's own furthest.
- **Scope:** `observation/ground.py` (new), `observation/tracking.py` (`unexplained`), `training/vision.py`, `training/episode.py`, `understanding/events.py`, `rewards/ground.py` (new), `services/observer.py` (the event), `services/rewards.py`, `tools/practice_bench.py`. **Out of scope:** the memory guesses that pay for jumping and dying (next task), rooms and doors (a cut starts again from where the go began, which under-pays a new room and never pays the same ground twice), a game with no memory to read (the reward service is off there), telling up from down (falling into a pit pays its two or three steps once a go; recorded).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. `Ground`: walking one way pays a step for each of the player's own size covered, once; standing, walking back and walking the same ground again pay nothing; each of the four directions is counted on its own; a jump of more than 4 steps in one look pays 4 and the rest is not owed; after `back()` nothing pays until it is past the go's furthest; `begin()` forgets the go; on a still screen the place is where it stands, and once the screen has scrolled only the camera's travel counts (a jump and a fall pay nothing); a look in which it is not seen counts the camera alone; nonsense is refused.
  2. `ObjectTracker.unexplained` is 0 on a still screen and after a move that explains everything, the share that differs after a cut, and 0 again after a reset.
  3. `ScreenWatch`: scrolling scenery with the player held still pays the camera's travel; walking across a still screen pays the same; a cut to another scene, and a life lost with a jump of the screen that finds it somewhere else, put it back (the walk after pays nothing until past the furthest); a life lost with no jump of the screen (a hit), or with one that leaves it where it was (a crash), does not; where a fifth of the camera's last moves could not be measured nothing is paid, and the summary says so; a new go starts from nothing; `take_new_ground()` empties what it gives.
  4. Rewards: the first `GroundCovered` adds the row with its suggested value under Progression and announces it; each step pays the row's value; a changed value and a switched-off row are respected; a dismissed row stays away until suggestions are asked for again; nothing happens while no game is connected; the row survives save and load, and `apply_suggestions` leaves it alone.
  5. The runner: ground found at a look is paid in that same step's reward, and a go with no watch publishes nothing.
  6. The exploit detector counts the row as progress (its category), so a go that earns from it alone raises no warning.
  7. Measured on `practice_bench --goes 40`, seeds 0 and 3: the ground counted to the right is within one step of how far the game's own camera went in at least 90% of goes; the brain's furthest reached before and after recorded here as it is, with the deaths.
- **Expected changes:** the files in Scope, `tests/unit/observation/test_ground.py` (new), `tests/unit/observation/test_tracking.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_vision.py`, `tests/unit/rewards/test_ground.py` (new), `tests/unit/services/test_rewards.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_episode.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_service.py` (one assertion, see Results), `tests/integration/test_practice_bench.py`, `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `TASK_TRACKER.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Test plan:** written before the code. Ground: `test_walking_on_pays_a_step_for_each_of_its_own_size`, `test_the_same_ground_pays_once`, `test_each_direction_is_counted_on_its_own`, `test_a_jump_pays_no_more_than_four_steps`, `test_back_where_the_go_began_nothing_pays_until_past_the_furthest`, `test_a_new_go_starts_from_nothing`, `test_on_a_still_screen_it_is_where_it_stands`, `test_once_the_screen_scrolls_only_the_cameras_travel_counts` (these two replaced the planned `test_the_camera_and_the_place_on_the_screen_add_up`), `test_unseen_it_counts_the_camera_alone`, `test_the_step_is_its_own_size`, `test_nonsense_is_refused`. Tracking: `test_what_the_move_leaves_unexplained`. Vision: `test_scrolling_scenery_pays_the_cameras_travel`, `test_walking_across_a_still_screen_pays`, `test_a_cut_puts_it_back_where_the_go_began`, `test_a_life_lost_with_a_jump_of_the_screen_puts_it_back`, `test_a_hit_does_not_put_it_back`, `test_a_camera_it_cannot_follow_pays_nothing` (added with the second design move), `test_new_ground_is_taken_once_and_a_go_starts_from_nothing`. Rewards: `test_the_row` (id, name, category, trigger, not automatic), `test_the_row_is_added_once_and_not_when_dismissed`; service: `test_new_ground_adds_its_row_and_pays_each_step`, `test_new_ground_respects_the_persons_value_and_switch`, `test_a_dismissed_ground_row_stays_away`, `test_new_ground_is_progress_to_the_exploit_detector`, `test_the_ground_row_is_saved_and_left_alone_by_suggestions`. Episode: `test_new_ground_is_paid_in_the_step_that_found_it`, `test_a_go_without_a_watch_finds_no_ground`. Bench: `test_new_ground_is_paid_as_the_game_has_it`. Then the full suite, ruff, format, mypy (also under Python 3.11's numpy), and the bench on seeds 0 and 3.
- **Results:** all seven criteria met. `practice_bench --goes 40`, level 0: 282 steps of new ground counted, and the furthest counted to the right was as far as the game's own camera went, to within a step, in 98% of the 40 goes; level 3: 288 steps, 100%. The eyes and the camera as before. The design moved twice on what was measured. First: as planned the place was the camera's travel plus where the player stands on the screen, and the first bench runs counted 579 and 648 steps, right in 95 and 98% of goes against the player's own position: but a fall into a gap then paid its two or three steps down at once, about what the life costs a second later once that is discounted, and so did every first jump. Now, once the screen has ever been seen to scroll, only the camera's travel counts (kept from go to go); the place on the screen counts only on a screen that never has. Second: the full suite's `test_first_working_demonstration` failed on "the point-lover drives faster than the careful one", and it was right to: on the Toy Racer (64 by 48, scrolling up to 32 rows a look) the tracker can measure only slow driving, so the new row paid for driving slowly, and every crash that came with a change of lane was taken for being put back at the start. Measured over learner seeds 1 to 4, the point-lover's mean speed fell from 0.80 on main to 0.43, below the careful one's on two seeds. Guessing the unmeasured moves (taking the camera to go on as it was) was tried and dropped: it would pay for standing in front of anything that keeps changing. As built: a jolt is put down to a respawn only when it also finds the player somewhere else on the screen; and the watch judges whether it can follow the camera at all (`follows_camera`: not when 20 or more, and over a fifth, of the last 200 looks in which the camera moved could not be measured), counts nothing while it cannot, and says so in the summary. With that the point-lover's speed is 0.66 over the four seeds and above the careful one's on each (0.48 and 0.35, 0.90 and 0.40, 0.41 and 0.31, 0.86 and 0.47), every other claim holds on each seed, and the practice bench numbers are unchanged. The brain, as it is: level 0 furthest reached 198 (best 372) in the first ten goes and 206 (best 217) in the last ten, lives lost a go 0.50 then 1.40, 38 deaths (before, on T-992: 183 then 155, best 204 in the last ten, 0.40 then 0.20, 11 deaths); level 3 furthest 206 (best 280) then 207 (best 219), lives lost 1.20 then 1.40, 50 deaths (before: 188 then 204, best 460, 0.70 then 0.80, 24 deaths). So it now walks to the first gap every go, where it used to stand about, and falls in. Two causes, both measured and neither this task's. (1) The rewards suggested from memory drown the new one: in a go on level 0 "Something switches on" pays about 80 points (the on-the-ground and jumping flags, +1.5 each of 25 times), "Progress (2nd guess) goes up" 40 (the high byte of the level's clock, +10 every 256 frames) and "Progress goes up" +10 for dying (the mode byte), against about 14 for new ground and -12.5 for a life. (2) With those rows made to pay nothing, in an experiment outside the repository, the AI learns to stop short of the gap (level 0: furthest 189 then 158, lives lost 0.50 then 0.00): it has been across (best 415) and does not keep it. One existing assertion was restated: `test_a_loss_a_held_button_avoids_leaves_the_start_where_it_is` checks that go 4 starts where the others did, and for that asserted the car was strictly past the start after the go's first step and at most one step's drive on; how far that step drives is the AI's choice of button (the comment already said so when T-988 moved it from 12 to 3), and paid for new ground it now stops dead, 0 on. The bound is now "at the start or at most one step on", which is the claim the test is about; lives and the game's clock are checked as before. Full suite: 1,806 passed, 10 skipped. ruff, format and mypy clean (also under Python 3.11's numpy for the two observation files).
- **Commit:** see PR #237. **PR:** #237.
- **Completion report:** the AI is now paid for getting somewhere new by what the screen shows, with no guess about memory in it: the camera's travel, a step of its own size at a time, each step once a go, through a reward row a person can see and change. The count agrees with the game's own camera in 98 to 100% of goes on the practice bench. The brain does not yet get further for it: it walks to the first gap and falls in, because the rewards guessed from memory pay ten times as much for jumping on the spot and for a clock, and pay for dying; and with those silenced it stops short of the gap instead of learning the jump. Next: those rewards (a switch that flips all the time, a value as regular as a clock, a value that rises when a life is lost), then the learner. Limits recorded in the modules and ARCHITECTURE: where the camera cannot be followed (the racer's small fast screen) nothing is counted, and the summary says so; no reward on a game without memory access; a new room is under-paid; a respawn the tracker takes for a small camera move is not caught; on a screen that never scrolls a jump and a fall pay their steps.
### T-992 – The camera's move between two looks is measured right
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 2 and 3. Wanted next: pay the AI for new ground, measured off the screen as the camera's travel plus where it stands. Measuring for that showed the tracker's camera is wrong: in a 12-go bench run the scroll between two looks was right in 94 of the 351 looks in which the camera moved. Causes, each seen in the recorded looks: (1) `estimate_scroll` tries shifts up to 8 pixels, a limit meant for one frame, and the AI looks every 8 frames, in which the practice game's camera moves up to 16 and a faster game's more; (2) the camera holds the player still on the screen, so the player votes for "nothing moved", and the tracker already knows where it is; (3) so does the strip of lives and score, and it outweighs a thin feature, and its evenly spaced squares pull the answer to a multiple of their spacing; (4) a walker pacing on plain ground, the only thing in sight, reads as the camera moving the other way once nothing contradicts it; (5) a walker outweighs a coin. The same wrong scroll also spoils the tracks of things and what counts as moving. T-990 and T-991 were set aside for another thread; this thread numbers on from T-992 by agreement with the coordinator, T-991 kept for the outlines on the Game panel)
- **Objective:** (a) `estimate_scroll` takes masks of pixels to leave out of either screen, and past 8 pixels of reach searches coarse then fine (every fourth pixel and shift over the whole reach, then every shift round the best three), so a reach of 32 costs no more than 8 did. (b) `ObjectTracker.update` leaves out of the vote: the hidden box (the player) where it is and where it was, and rows it has found to be painted on the glass (leaving out the things known to move as well was planned and dropped, see Results); a thing wholly on the glass is followed as standing still on the screen. A row is glass once, in two looks in which the camera moved, nothing in it changed although the move would have changed it; it stops being glass the moment it is seen to move; glass is kept over a go like the kinds. (c) No move is believed without wide evidence: when all that changed on the screen fits in a box of half a thing's largest size (32 pixels), the camera stood still. (d) `ScreenWatch` lets the camera move 32 pixels between two looks. (e) The bench measures the camera's move at every look against the game's.
- **Scope:** `observation/tracking.py`, `training/vision.py` (the reach), `tools/practice_bench.py`; and, forced by the full suite, `tests/integration/test_first_demonstration.py` and one assertion of `tests/unit/emulator/bizhawk/test_lua_script.py` (see Results). **Out of scope:** the reward for new ground (next task), a cut to another scene (the camera's place is then unknown; the next task deals with it), a panel down the side of the screen, layers that scroll at different speeds.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. A scroll of up to 32 pixels either way, across, up, down or both, is found exactly on a textured scene; the small reach still tries every shift (the existing tests pass unchanged); masks of another shape are refused.
  2. Pixels left out do not vote: a strip that stands still no longer holds a thin scrolling feature still.
  3. The tracker: with the player hidden and held still by the camera the scroll is right; a lone mover on plain ground leaves the camera still and is itself found to move; a still screen costs no search.
  4. Glass: a strip that stood still through two camera moves is left out from then on, over a reset too; a row seen to move is no longer glass; a thing on the glass does not move in the level and is not cut out as a mover.
  5. The watch follows a camera moving 16 pixels a look.
  6. Measured on `practice_bench --goes 40`, seeds 0 and 3: the camera's move right in at least 90% of the looks in which it moved and 99% of those in which it stood still (before: about 27% and 100%); a look costs no more time than before. Recorded here.
- **Expected changes:** the files in Scope, `tests/unit/observation/test_tracking.py`, `tests/unit/training/test_vision.py`, `tests/integration/test_practice_bench.py`, `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `TASK_TRACKER.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Test plan:** written before the code. Tracking: `test_a_wide_scroll_is_found_coarse_then_fine`, `test_pixels_left_out_do_not_vote`, `test_bad_masks_are_refused`, `test_the_hidden_player_does_not_hold_the_camera_still`, `test_a_lone_mover_is_not_a_camera_move`, `test_a_strip_that_stands_still_is_learnt_as_glass` (kept over a reset), `test_what_is_on_the_glass_does_not_move`, `test_glass_is_unlearnt_when_the_row_moves_with_the_scenery`, `test_a_still_screen_costs_no_search`, `test_the_tracker_follows_a_camera_faster_than_eight_pixels_a_look`, `test_a_wide_search_costs_no_more_than_the_narrow_one` (the planned `test_a_known_mover_does_not_outvote_the_scenery` was dropped with that part of the design). Vision: `test_the_watch_follows_a_fast_camera`. Bench: `test_the_camera_is_followed`, `test_the_report_reads_in_words` (extended). Then the observation and training suites, the full suite and the two 40-go bench runs.
- **Results:** all six criteria met. `practice_bench --goes 40`: level 0, the camera moved between two looks 1,339 times and was measured right in 98%, stood still 3,621 times and was read as still in 100%; level 3, 1,166 moves, 100% right, 4,479 still, 100% (before, on a 12-go run: 94 of 351 moves right, 27%). A 40-go run takes 67 seconds instead of 92: a still screen needs no search. Eyes otherwise as before (itself in 98 to 99% of looks, floor 100%, 4 kinds). The design moved four times on what was measured. (1) Leaving out the things known to move, as planned, made it worse (35% of moves right): after one misread the scenery's own edges are cut out as "movers", are then left out of the vote, and the scroll stays wrong. Dropped; the planned test for it went with it. (2) The racer (a 64 by 48 screen) showed that "small" and "far" in fixed pixels are wrong on a small screen: both are now also bounded by the screen's size, and every shift is tried whenever that is cheap, because the coarse search cannot see features thinner than 4 pixels (the racer's obstacles are 2 rows). (3) Garbage estimates (a move past the reach, a cut) were believed and taught glass: a move must now explain at least half of what changed. (4) Glass by "the move would have changed the row" marked the empty rows a strip would have slid into and the tops of lines running down the screen; a row must now hold something and fail both ways, and counts decay so a mistake is let go. A thing wholly on the glass is followed as standing still (`Track.glass`), or a right scroll would make the life counter a moving thing for the brain. Two tests outside the plan changed, both recorded as owed or found here. (a) `test_first_working_demonstration`: with the first version of this task its "twice as fast" claim failed on all of seeds 1 to 5 and 7 (0.82 to 1.54 times), the third time that claim moved with an unrelated change. Measured over those six seeds and five versions of the code, the single-run claims held on between none and all of them. The test now walks steps 1 to 9 for learner seeds 1, 2 and 3 and makes step 10's claims about the three together: rewards' signs on every seed; more points per step and faster for the point-lover; at least a quarter fewer crashes per step late than early for the careful one (the same bound as before). With the final code these hold on each of the six seeds alone and on every three of them (points per step 1.7 to 2.7 times; crashes down to 0.47 to 0.69). "Twice as fast" is no longer claimed: it never was a property of the learner. This settles the item owed since T-988. (b) `test_free_run_leaves_the_real_controller_alone_between_watched_steps` failed once in a full run: it asserts the car's speed at an instant while the game free-runs in another thread, and on a loaded machine the car had by then hit something and stood still (frame 16, a life gone). It passed 3 of 3 alone; the cause is the instant, not this change. It now asserts the car has driven on since the person's Up, which is what the comment claimed. Tests: 26 new (13 of them shifts of one parametrised test), 3 extended. Full suite: 1774 passed, 10 skipped; ruff, ruff format and mypy (137 files, also checked under Python 3.11's numpy) clean.
- **Commit:** see PR #236. **PR:** #236.
- **Completion report:** the tracker now knows how far the camera moved between two looks, at the pace the AI looks, by the scenery alone: on the practice game in 98 to 100% of the looks in which it moved, and never when it did not. What stands still on the glass is learnt and left out. That makes "moving thing" mean what it says, and gives the next task its ruler: where the AI is in the level is the camera's travel plus where it stands on the screen. Limits recorded: a cut to a place with the same tiles can be believed once as a move; features thinner than 4 pixels are not seen by the wide search on a big screen; a panel down the side and layered scrolling are not handled. Next: pay the AI for new ground.
### T-989 – The brain reads what is around it off the screen
- **Status:** Done
- **Phase:** 8 (the plan's Stage 3: the brain reads the screen. After T-988 the eyes meet their targets on the practice bench, and the brain still knows nothing of what they see but the nearest moving thing: every death on the bench is a fall into a gap it has no way of seeing coming except by remembering where in the level it is, which is the memorising the user's game showed does not carry over. Second finding: `StateEncoder` adds the screen parts on top of a state that may already fill the feature map (32 seats), where a newcomer is dropped when every holder is present, so on a game with many believed values the brain may not get the screen parts at all)
- **Objective:** (a) `observation/surroundings.py`: `read(frame, box, backdrop)` gives, from one screen, the box the player was seen in and the backdrop colour, five small numbers. Floor to the right and to the left: how far from its edge the first column is with nothing but backdrop from its feet down to the bottom of the screen, in steps of 8 pixels, 0 to 6 (6: 48 pixels or more, or none in sight). Clear way to the right and left: how far the first column is with anything but backdrop in it at the player's own height (its top three quarters, so a floor a little higher is not a wall), same steps. Under it: 0 standing on something, 1 something within its own height below, 2 something further below, 3 nothing. Past the edge of the screen counts as floor and as clear (it cannot see that it is not). No colour, size or direction is named anywhere: both sides are read alike. (b) `ScreenWatch` reads them at every look in which it sees itself and gives them to the brain first, before the nearest-mover parts (`parts()`); the fall rule of T-988 uses the same reading for "nothing under it". (c) `StateEncoder` keeps `SCREEN_SEATS` (now 12) seats for the screen out of its most while a screen source is set, so the whole state fits the feature map; the parts have words for the log.  (d) The bench measures the floor readings against the game's own level at every look.
- **Scope:** `observation/surroundings.py` (new), `training/vision.py`, `learning/state.py`, `tools/practice_bench.py`. **Out of scope:** what the AI is paid for (next task), learning which colours are only decoration, a look on every step, a screen with a strip along the bottom (no column is ever open there; recorded as a limit).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. On drawn screens the five readings are right: flat ground, a gap and a wall at each distance either side, in the air over ground and over a gap, at the screen's edges, at the bottom of the screen, a box partly off the screen.
  2. Nonsense is refused (not a screen, a bad box); a backdrop of another depth gives no reading.
  3. The watch gives the five parts first at every look in which it sees itself, the mover parts after, nothing when it does not see itself, with or without the player's colours; the T-988 fall tests pass unchanged.
  4. With a screen source the encoder's state never holds more than the feature map's width: memory and distance seats give way to `SCREEN_SEATS`; without one nothing changes. The parts read in words in the log.
  5. Measured: on `practice_bench --goes 40`, seeds 0 and 3, the floor to the right and left agree with the game's level in at least 95% of the looks in which it sees itself; furthest reached before and after recorded here as it is.
